title: serve: strata_prefix marks a chat whose history has pictures
body:
Issue: none open for this. Related, not resolved by it: #2255 (pinned prefixes filling the conversation cache).

## Summary

`"strata_prefix"` was ignored for any request with an image in it (`strata_prefix ignored: the request has images`), so one photo anywhere in a chat's history turned it off until that message left the context. Pictures before the boundary now count with the tokens they take in the prompt, and the prefix is marked as for a text-only request.

The use case: a chat client sends `{"messages": K}` with K the index of its final user message. That message carries per-turn text (recalled memories, the clock) that the next turn replays without, so the turn checkpoint never matches again and only the system-prompt checkpoint was reused. With the pin, each turn resumes where the replayed history ends. A chat that once contained a photo lost this until now.

## What changed

- `serve/server.py`
  - The loop in `prepare()` that turns each `<|vision_start|><|image_pad|>` into one pad per image token moved, unchanged, into `Service.expand_image_pads(ids, counts)`. `prepare()` calls it with the encoded counts and keeps its "the prompt and its images do not match" check.
  - `resolve_prefix()` takes the request's image token counts (`image_counts`, in prompt order) instead of `has_images`. `head_ids()` expands the rendered head's pictures with the same helper, so the longest common start runs through them. The refusal for images is gone.
  - New guard: a boundary inside a picture's tokens is ignored with `strata_prefix ... ignored: it ends inside a picture` (only `{"tokens": N}` can land there; a message boundary cannot).
- `serve/test_server.py`, class `SharedPrefix`: three tests with a fake encoder whose two pictures take 3 and 5 tokens, so a wrong count or order misses the boundary:
  - `test_messages_resolve_past_a_picture_in_the_history`: a photo in the history; the prefix ends at the final message's `<|im_start|>` and holds all 3 of its tokens.
  - `test_a_picture_after_the_prefix_stays_out_of_it`: pictures on both sides; 3 tokens before the boundary, 5 after.
  - `test_a_token_boundary_inside_a_picture_is_ignored`: `{"tokens": N}` inside the picture is ignored and said in the log.
  The first two failed before the change (ignored / `KeyError: 'tokens'`); the third fails with the guard removed (`{'tokens': 225} != {}`).
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: the pinned-prefix paragraph says pictures count now, names the chat-client use, and gives the measurement below.

## What it leaves alone

- A request without `strata_prefix` takes the same path as before: `prepare()` runs the moved loop with the same counts. `test_without_the_field_nothing_changes` and the `ImageMarkers` tests (#150, #2228) pass unchanged.
- A request with `strata_prefix` and no pictures: `image_counts` is `None`, and `head_ids()` returns what it did.
- The engine: no change. `pin=N` is one more cut in the same read loop as the turn and system-prompt checkpoints, which already handle pictures.
- Python only; no CUDA, HIP or SYCL file is touched.

## How it was checked

- `python -m unittest discover -s serve -t . -p "test_*.py"` on this branch (`477ac13c` + this change, macOS, Python 3.14): 851 tests, 850 pass, 11 skipped. Against `main` without the change: 848 tests, 847 pass. The one failure is the same in both, `test_keepawake.KeepAwakeTests.test_service_holds_for_the_whole_request_including_early_close`, and it fails on this Mac without the change too.
- Live, on the DGX Spark port (#2419, engine 0.1.44.1; the same server patch applied there), GB10, Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL, 131,072 context, `--kv int8`, images on, 2026-10-17. A four-turn chat with a 640x400 PNG in its first message, `{"messages": K}` on every turn with history, per-turn text in the final user message:

  | Turn | Prompt | Reused | Read | Time to read |
  |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 1 | 5,333 | 0 | 5,333 | 7.9 s |
  | 2 | 5,478 | 5,392 | 86 | 0.96 s |
  | 3 | 5,503 | 5,395 | 108 | 1.20 s |
  | 4 | 5,527 | 5,421 | 106 | 1.18 s |

  No `ignored` line in the server window. Turns 3 and 4 resumed at the pin of the turn before and still answered about the picture correctly (its colours and its text), so the picture's tokens come back intact from the pinned checkpoint.
- The same client in a real chat (23-31k tokens) before the change, with a photo 27 messages back: every turn reused only the system prompt's checkpoint and read 4.8-7.0k tokens (4.7-7.5 s) before answering.

## Not tested

- Other chat templates than the Qwen3.8 one, and `/v1/messages` and `/v1/responses` requests with pictures (they reach `resolve_prefix` through the same `prepare()`).
- `{"message": I, "chars": N}` with pictures before message I (covered by the same expansion, no test of its own).
- Pictures given by URL.
- Windows, and any GPU other than the GB10.

## Title
Issue: Resolves #2865

## Summary
With `stream_options.include_usage`, the streamed usage now goes in its own final chunk with `"choices": []`, as in OpenAI's streaming contract. Without the option nothing changes.

## What changed
- `serve/server.py` (+10): in the streaming loop of `/v1/chat/completions`, a `split_usage` flag from `stream_options.include_usage`. When it is set and a chunk carries `usage`, that chunk is written as two chunks: the same chunk without `usage`, then a chunk with `"choices": []` and the usage.
- `serve/test_server.py` (+59): three tests (usage alone in the last `choices: []` chunk with the option; usage unchanged on the `finish_reason` chunk without it; same numbers as the non-streaming reply).

Left alone: non-streaming replies; requests without the option (the new branch is skipped and the original write is used); `/v1/messages`; `/v1/responses`; the legacy completions endpoint of #2278.

## Extra Notes
How I checked:
- The new tests and the whole `serve/test_server.py` suite pass (340 tests) on v0.1.45 + this commit.
- Live, on engine 0.1.45 (2x NVIDIA A2, UD-Q4_K_XL): a streamed request with the option puts the usage alone in the last `choices: []` chunk; without the option it stays on the `finish_reason` chunk.

Not checked: HIP/SYCL (Python-only change, no engine file touched), clients other than LiteLLM, and I compared the chunk structure rather than a byte diff for the default path.

title: mtp: the draft layer's experts at Q8_0 and BF16, alongside Q2_0
body:
The MTP draft layer's 512 routed experts were Q2_0 only: a format picked by measured draft acceptance, carrying a relative RMS error of 0.42 on the first experts.  Higher precision buys better drafts, hence a higher accept rate, hence speed - never a different output, since the verify window decides every emitted token.  This adds Q8_0 (2.49 GiB) and BF16 (4.69 GiB) as opt-in arms and leaves Q2_0 the default.

Which arm a run uses is the runtime directory, not a flag: `--mtp rt-q8_0` or `--mtp rt-bf16`.  The selection is an `experts.fmt` marker that tools/mtp_rt.py writes beside experts.bin, one line `<format> <gu_type> <d_type>`.  No marker means Q2_0, so every `rt/` that exists today keeps taking exactly the path it always did.

Engine:
  * iq_kernels.cu: Fmt<30> (BF16 weights against a q8_1 activation), and 30 in STRATA_GU_FMTS / STRATA_D_FMTS / STRATA_MMVQ_FMTS.  Q8_0's grouped path at this shape is covered here for the first time as well.
  * `native_expert_supported` asks `embed_type_supported` rather than `is_iq`, which is the set dq_dispatch implements; `is_iq` is left alone, so nothing that gates on it moves.
  * mtp.cpp: one branch in load(), taken once.  The per-expert stride is a function of the chosen layout rather than cpu::BLOB, and the activation buffer is carved at q8_1's 36 bytes per 32 values with Q2_0 reading its 34-byte prefix.  A shared drafter now inherits the layout with the buffer it shares: without that a second session would stride a q8_0 buffer by the Q2_0 blob, silently.
  * The size of experts.bin is checked against the layout, because a mismatch does not crash - it drafts from the wrong bytes and is merely accepted less often.

tools/mtp_pack.py gains a lossless bf16 arm (the checkpoint's own 16-bit words, no round trip, so its reconstruction error is exactly zero) and tools/mtp_rt.py writes the per-expert native blob: gate_up[e] then down[e].  Whole-tensor order would hand every expert the head of its neighbour.

Measured on the 4-GPU rig (iq3_s, 256 greedy tokens): BF16 does not fit - the draft layer lands entirely on the last stage's 8 GB card and 4.84 GiB of experts leaves too few cache slots for the prompt path.  Q8_0 runs at 48.9 tok/s against Q2_0's 49.5-49.9, with an accept rate indistinguishable within the engine's ~8-point run-to-run spread, at a 2007 -> 1134 slot cost on that card.  So this is an arm to measure, not a win to claim.

title: generate: STRATA_VRAM_RESERVE_MIB, a VRAM reserve per part
body:
## What this changes

`STRATA_VRAM_RESERVE_MIB="100,100,300,300"` — an opt-in VRAM reserve per part of a layer split, in the split's
order, in MiB. Entry 0 is the first card and replaces `--vram-reserve-mib`; entry *i* is the *i*-th later card and
replaces `--vram-reserve-later-mib` for that card. A shorter list reuses its last number; extra numbers are
ignored. `STRATA_GLM_RESERVE_MB` is accepted as the same knob.

Today the flags give the first card its own number and every later card one shared number, which cannot express a
rig whose cards are not the same size or do not hold the same kind of layer. `stage_room()` now takes the part's
ordinal and prefers the list's entry for it; the split search, the stage sizing, the drafter reservation and the
LOW free-VRAM warning all go through it. When the list is active, the LOW line's suggested fix names the list entry
to raise instead of the flag the list overrides.

The start prints the reserve each part will use:

strata generate: VRAM reserves per part: CUDA0 700 MiB, CUDA1 700 MiB, ... (STRATA_VRAM_RESERVE_MIB)

From the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), `Glm5Model::pool_reserve` (`STRATA_GLM_RESERVE_MB`).

## What it leaves alone

Unset, `vram_reserve_parts_mib` is empty, `stage_room()` takes the old flag path, the print block does not run, and
its stderr line is absent. The two flags decide exactly as before. This is by construction, not by a measurement.

## Measurements

No speedup is claimed; this is a control knob. On the four-way Q8_0 rig this was written for (CUDA0/CUDA1 12 GB,
CUDA2/CUDA3 8 GB), a run's LOW lines showed CUDA1 with 511 MiB, CUDA2 with 388 MiB and CUDA3 with 1,156 MiB free.
CUDA3's one layer held all 512 profiled pairs of its layer, so its free VRAM cannot buy another expert there and
that is the card whose reserve can rise without losing cache. A per-card A/B (same split, same
`STRATA_PREFILL_MAX`, list against flags) is the test on a given rig; it has not been run.

## Checks

- **Default path:** unset = byte-identical by construction (empty list; `stage_room()` uses the old flags; no
  print).
- **Build:** CUDA. `generate.cpp` is host-only code and this adds no device code; it compiles clean against this
  branch's headers with the build's own flags (`-fsyntax-only`; one pre-existing unused-variable warning in
  unrelated code). The development branch that also carries the change built fully with ninja (nvcc 13.2).
- **HIP / SYCL:** not compiled here (no toolchain on the machine). `generate.cpp` carries no per-backend code, so
  both builds compile the same change.
- **On a start:** the per-part reserve line above; an unset-vs-set A/B of a run's free VRAM and prompt rate is the
  test of whether a given per-card split pays.

title: serve: the Monitor's Workers card - one widget per batch slot, each with its own tok/s (#465)
body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #2857

## Summary
With `"parallel": N` the server runs several requests at once, but the Monitor still shows one
request's numbers: the header pill reads the newest request's rate and the Model state card
shows one request's progress. There is no way to see on the page whether the requests are
decoding together or one after the other.

This adds a **Workers** card to the Monitor — one widget per batch slot with its own state, live
tok/s, tokens written and context fill — and makes the header pill name every decoding stream
(`2 decoding · 80.4 + 76.1 tok/s`). It is opt-in by construction: the card is in the markup
hidden and is shown only when `/metrics` reports `live.parallel`, which the server sets only for
a run config with `"parallel": N`.

## What changed
- `serve/web/index.html` (+7): the `workers-card` markup after *Model state*, `hidden` by
  default, with `workers-sum`, `workers` and `workers-note`.
- `serve/web/app.js` (+63 / -1): `workerWidgetsFor()` builds one widget per slot the first time
  and reuses it, so state and progress transitions animate instead of being replaced every
  second; `renderWorkers()` fills it from the existing `live.slots` and is called from
  `renderMonitor()`. The pill line gained a branch: when two or more slots are decoding it lists
  their rates; otherwise it is the old text.
- `serve/web/app.css` (+17): the card's styles, from existing design tokens only (no new
  colors, fonts or selectors outside `.worker*`).
- `serve/test_monitor.py` (+11): `test_the_workers_card_is_on_the_page_and_opt_in` — the same
  page assertion as `test_the_card_is_on_the_page`, plus that the card ships `hidden` and is
  gated on `live.parallel`.

## Extra Notes
- **Nothing outside `serve/web` and this test.** No server, setup or engine file changed, so
  there is nothing to build: no CUDA, HIP or SYCL file is touched.
- **The default path is unchanged.** Checked on this branch with a `/metrics` payload without
  `parallel`: the card stays hidden, no widget is built, and the pill reads
  `Generating · 79.8 tok/s` as before. With `parallel: 2` both slots render with their own rate.
  No console errors in either state.
- **Tests:** `python -m unittest serve.test_monitor serve.test_runconfig` → 20 tests, all pass
  (19 on `main` + the new one). `node --check serve/web/app.js` is clean.
- **No new API.** The widget reads `live.slots` as `slots_view()` in `serve/server.py` already
  publishes it; the server and its tests are untouched.
- The widgets are filled one second at a time from the existing `poll()`, the way the request
  table already is; each widget keeps its own context bar against `engine.max_context`.
- Left alone on purpose: the standalone API Monitor page (`serve/web/monitor.html`), the Chat
  and About tabs, and every hardware card.
- Possibly touching the same markup as #1114 (rearrangeable Monitor layout) and #2317 (one line
  per card on a layer split); no functional overlap — happy to rebase if either lands first.

title: Add RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell benchmark reports: UD-IQ4_XS tuning A/B and UD-Q4_K_XL
body:
Results-only submission of four folders under `bench/results/`, all measured on one machine with `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test) plus an interleaved A/B driver for the tuning part. No engine changes.

## Hardware and software

- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell, 24 GiB VRAM
- CPU: Intel Core Ultra 9 285K (24 cores / 24 threads, no AVX-512), 125.3 GiB RAM
- OS: Linux 6.17.0-1033-oem, driver 595.99.02, CUDA 13.2
- Strata: project 0.1.44.1, commit 296b59d2, engine 0.1.44.1

## What is in each folder

| Folder | Model | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `2026-10-15-...-unsloth-ud-iq4-xs` | UD-IQ4_XS | baseline before the tuning switches: `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`, no `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP`, `--prefill auto` |
| `2026-10-16-...-unsloth-ud-iq4-xs` | UD-IQ4_XS | same machine after the switches: tail-skip at its 0.1.42+ CUDA default, `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1`, `--prefill auto:16384` |
| `2026-10-16-tuning-tail-skip-adapt-overlap-rtx-pro-4000` | UD-IQ4_XS | the interleaved A/B that picked the switches (`ab*.py`, `arms/` configs and logs, raw rows), plus the two reports above as its before/after |
| `2026-10-17-...-unsloth-ud-q4-k-xl` | UD-Q4_K_XL | the larger quantization at the same settings |

The two UD-IQ4_XS community reports are not duplicates: the first is the "before", the second the "after", and the tuning folder is what links them.

## Headline numbers (median, ranges in the reports)

UD-IQ4_XS, before -> after the switches (decode tok/s pooled over 4 requests): 77.9 -> 89.1 (**x1.144** from `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP` alone), `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1` adds x1.015. Full suite after the change: short chat 89.1 tok/s, 4K prompt 2465.8 tok/s, 16K prompt 2874.4 tok/s, agent decode 96.2 tok/s, cache hit 68.8 %.

UD-Q4_K_XL at the same settings: short chat 77.8 tok/s, 4K prompt 2142.1 tok/s, 16K prompt 2916.5 tok/s, agent decode 84.4 tok/s, cache hit 68.4 %. So the bigger quantization costs about 13 % decode and 13 % on a 4K prompt, while 16K prefill is the same within noise.

All runs: 131072 context, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`, `--mtp rt`, `--pool-workers 15`, thinking off, temperature 0, one slot. Configs in the folders are the install's own, unchanged.

## Limitations

Speed only: no correctness check, no KL check, no needle test. One machine, one GPU, two rounds per tuning arm (greedy), background load and power limits not recorded. `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP` changes the output slightly by design (teacher-forced KL 0.003-0.006, top-1 agreement 97.7-98.2 % per `docs/DETAILS.md`). Home folder paths in the tuning folder are replaced by `/home/user`; no API keys, host names or IP addresses are included.

title: Slot checkpoints for clients that rewrite the end of their history (3/3, depends on #2527 and #2528): STRATA_SLOT_CHECKPOINTS, STRATA_BRANCH_CHECKPOINT, BCHECKS
body:
## Summary

A client that rewrites the end of its history every time never finds a checkpoint to continue from. Claude Code's
safety classifier is one: each query is the agent's transcript with the new tool calls inserted before the closing
text (`... </transcript>` and the instruction), so the next query leaves this one a few dozen tokens before its end.
The turn checkpoint is past that point, the periodic ones are up to 16K tokens before it, and a slot that receives
the conversation (park=, an admission continuing in its slot) keeps only its deepest checkpoint. On our server
(3 x RTX A4000 layer split, --batch 6) every classifier query of 2026-10-16 read its whole 42-74K-token transcript
again: 15.6-27.4 s per call, several per agent step.

**Part 3, depends on #2527 and #2528**: the branch includes their commits (rebased on 0.1.45); this PR's own are the
last five (`batch: STRATA_SLOT_CHECKPOINTS=N`, `generate: STRATA_BRANCH_CHECKPOINT=<margin>`, `batch, serve: BCHECKS`,
`batch: a slot keeps its deepest checkpoint and the branch one; ...`, `batch: STRATA_BRANCH_CHECKPOINT and
STRATA_SLOT_CHECKPOINTS apart`). The placement side of the same problem - a slot holding an older version of the
conversation is the one to replace (`STRATA_SLOT_SIBLING_SHARE`) - is in #2528.

## Change (all opt-in)

- `STRATA_BRANCH_CHECKPOINT=<margin>` (serve, batch or not): before reading, the engine measures how far the prompt
  runs along each conversation it holds (the main session's, every idle slot's) before leaving it; when that point
  is `<margin>` tokens or more past where the read starts and before the turn boundary, the read stops there for one
  more checkpoint, like the root and turn cuts. The next query - which leaves this one later - resumes there. With it
  on, a slot keeps the deepest such branch checkpoint of its conversation (alone, whatever N is).
- `STRATA_SLOT_CHECKPOINTS=N` (batch; unset 1, as before): how many checkpoints a slot keeps - the deepest, then the
  deepest others, the branch one counted in N. The two switches are apart:

  | | without `STRATA_BRANCH_CHECKPOINT` | with it |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | N = 1 | the deepest (the turn checkpoint), as before | the turn and the branch one (one before there is one) |
  | N = 2 | the two deepest (the turn before or a periodic one) | two: the turn and the branch one, or else the next deepest |

  A restore from a slot checkpoint brings the slot's shallower ones back with it, and a slot that gives back all it
  holds gives back its checkpoints of that conversation with it. Log: `slot 2 keeps 2 checkpoints (at 43340 43867;
  227.6 MiB)`. Pure helpers in `include/strata/program/slot_checkpoints.hpp`, unit test `slot_checkpoints_test`.
- With upstream's `STRATA_SLOT_CKPT_MOVE=1` an admission moves all of them into the slot instead of copying (the
  chain's root and a pinned prefix are copied): the main session drops checkpoints of another conversation at its next
  request anyway. A slot that gives back all it holds moves them back, so the next admission keeps them again (without
  that, the moved ones were lost there - also upstream's single moved turn checkpoint - and a next turn sent back
  without its thinking read 19,342 tokens in 8.5 s instead of 154 in 0.63 s).
- `BCHECKS <slot> <tokens> <lengths>` (with N > 1 or `STRATA_BRANCH_CHECKPOINT`): after `PARKED`, `BADM 1` and
  `BYIELD` the engine says which checkpoints a slot keeps; the server keeps them per slot (forgotten before it sends
  anything that overwrites the slot), shows them in `/metrics` (`checkpoint_tokens`), and `place()` uses the deepest
  one that starts the prompt as the hint where no slot's history continues it (it was 0). Information only: the
  engine still picks what it reuses.

Unset, every path is the one before.

## Results

3 x RTX A4000, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, 0.1.45 + #2527 / #2528, --batch 6 in 3 groups, 200K context,
`STRATA_SLOT_CKPT_MOVE=1 STRATA_CKPT_POOL=1`. A 43-45K-token classifier transcript growing by about 250 tokens per
query, an agent conversation taking the main session between the queries (S: alone; B: a client decoding beside it);
seconds per query 1-6:

| | S | B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| without either switch (0.1.45) | 13.7, 13.6, 13.8, 13.9, 14.1, 14.2 | 14.1-14.2 |
| `STRATA_BRANCH_CHECKPOINT=1024`, N unset (1) | 13.6, 14.2, 1.21, 1.65, 1.89, 2.03 | 0.56, 1.20, 1.09, 1.55, 1.82, 1.98 |
| the same, N = 2 | 13.6, 7.3, 1.48, 1.40, 1.89, 2.04 | 0.56, 1.21, 1.09, 1.57, 1.80, 1.97 |
| branch checkpoints taken but not kept by the slot (the rule before the switches were apart, N 1) | 13.6-14.9, none reused | 14.2-15.1, none reused |

From query 3 on, queries resume at the branch checkpoint (43,340 reused, 534-1,329 read). N = 2 adds the second
query of a chain: no branch checkpoint exists yet, and it resumes at the periodic checkpoint (32,768) instead of
reading the whole transcript. The last row is why the branch switch keeps its checkpoint in the slot by itself: the
cut is paid (0.6-0.8 s per query over no switch) and the checkpoint is dropped with the main session's chain.

Margin: 256 against 1024 (both with the slot keeping the branch checkpoint): reads stay at about 570 tokens instead
of growing to 1,329 until the next cut, but a cut in almost every query costs about the same (B, queries 2-6: 7.64 s
both), and a query branching further back than the newest branch checkpoint read its whole transcript again (B
query 1: 14.1 s against 0.56 s). With 1024 a query never falls back to a periodic checkpoint once a branch one exists:
it resumes at the last branch checkpoint, at most the margin plus one query's growth behind.

A thinking chat's next turn sent back without its thinking: 0.63 s (19,176 reused + 154 read). Throughput 62.8 /
180.6 tok/s at 1 / 6 clients (60.9 / 179.0 without either switch; `tools/serve_load.py`).

Memory (host RAM, a checkpoint is 113-114 MiB here): the branch checkpoints count in the main session's
`--prompt-cache` (6); a slot keeps one more where its conversation has one (N 1) or wherever it has two checkpoints
(N 2). With 6 slots the bound grows from 12 to 18 checkpoints, +0.67 GiB, at N 1 in practice by about 114 MiB per
slot holding a classifier-like conversation; with the move a moved checkpoint is not also in the main session's chain.

## How it was checked

Exactness (0.1.44.1 base), with docs/BATCHING.md's settings (STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1, --pcie-frac 0, --adapt-every
1000000, --no-prefill-borrow), greedy: the 6 queries' short answers are the same tokens without and with; of 6
160-token answers, 5 are the same and the third differs from its first token. That one depends only on whether the
read had a cut at 43,340: read at once, or resumed from 32,768 without the cut -> answer A; read through the cut in
one request (no restore), resumed from the branch checkpoint in the main session, or from it in a slot -> answer B.
So the saved, copied and restored state is the one the read had there; the cut changes the chunks of the read after
it, as `pin=` or a resume from an earlier turn checkpoint does.

Tests: `slot_checkpoints_test` 31 checks (the picks for N 0-9 with and without the branch switch, shared prefix, the
branch boundary's conditions); `conv_cache_test`, `conversation_cache_test`; `serve/test_slot_alloc.py` 74 (the hint
from reported checkpoints; BCHECKS lines kept per slot and forgotten before an overwrite), `test_parallel` 35,
`test_slots` 30, `test_cache_trace`.

Built natively on CUDA (sm_86, Linux). The engine change is in `src/program/generate.cpp` only (shared by every
backend's serve loop); not built here: HIP, SYCL.

## Extra Notes

Our production profiles on the machine above run `STRATA_BRANCH_CHECKPOINT=1024 STRATA_SLOT_CKPT_MOVE=1
STRATA_CKPT_POOL=1` with N unset (1) since 2026-10-17. In a field test on 2026-10-18 (two Claude Code sessions at once, run twice) each conversation kept its own slot after its first two requests, and every later request re-read only its new part (48-7,260 tokens; 20 of 24 requests in the second run). The claim of the classifier's prompt layout comes from our server's logs of Claude Code (a query's
transcript grows inside `<transcript>...</transcript>`; each new query inserts its tool calls before the closing
tag).

title: serve: cap the expert arena at a share of RAM ("arena_budget"), and a STOP.bat that only stops Strata
body:
## What this changes

Two things, both from one machine's problem: a 63.7 GiB PC with a 68 GB IQ2_XS model that could not hold its own expert arena.

### 1. `"arena_budget"` — a cap on the arena, as a share of RAM (opt-in)

The engine sizes the arena from what the machine has free at start, which is the wrong size on a PC that is also used for something else. On the machine above it asked for 33.02 GiB and said so:

```
WARNING: the expert arena needs 33.02 GiB of RAM but 26.21 GiB is available (6.81 GiB short):
         the load may swap or be stopped by the OS
```

and from there the load swapped, `cudaHostRegister` of the whole arena failed, the large pages were refused (`VirtualAlloc error 1450`) and the run fell back to 4 KB pages. Decode ran beside 2.6 MB/s of disk and 43% CPU.

A **fixed** number is the wrong shape for a fix — 28 GiB is generous on a 32 GB PC, wasteful on a 128 GB one, and wrong again the moment the PC is used for something else. So the key is a share of physical RAM, and the GiB are computed at every start from the RAM that PC actually has:

```json
"arena_budget": 0.45
"arena_budget": {"share": 0.45, "min_gib": 6, "headroom_gib": 8}
"arena_budget": "auto"
```

| key | default | range | what it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| the whole key | `"auto"` (an absent key is the same) | `"auto"`, `true`, a number, or an object | `"auto"`/absent: no cap, the engine sizes the arena itself |
| `share` | `0.45` (also what `true` means) | `0.10`–`0.85` | the share of physical RAM the arena may take |
| `min_gib` | `6` | `>= 1` | the floor |
| `headroom_gib` | `8` | `>= 0` | the RAM the rest of the PC keeps |

The cap is `clamp(share × total RAM, min_gib, total RAM − headroom_gib)`, rounded **down** to whole GiB, so it follows the hardware: `0.45` is 7 GiB on a 16 GB PC, 14 on 32 GB, 28 on 64 GB, 57 on 128 GB. `min_gib` never beats `headroom_gib`: on a PC too small for both, the cap is skipped rather than made impossible.

**How it takes effect.** Computed at start and passed as the engine's own `--resident-budget-gib N`. `--resident-budget-gib` alone — `generate.cpp:2223` already sets `mmap_experts` / `resident_cpu_experts` / `resident_pin` when it parses it, so `--mmap-experts` would be redundant, and it is refused beside some pack layouts. Read at start, so a change is used from the next start; the server prints the arithmetic once:

```
[strata] arena_budget: 0.45 x 63.7 GiB of RAM = 28 GiB for the expert arena -> --resident-budget-gib 28; the rest of the PC keeps 35.7 GiB
```

A value out of range, of the wrong type or with an unknown key is said once and then ignored, with the engine sizing the arena as before: a typo never stops a start.

### 2. `STOP.bat` / `stop-strata.ps1` — stop Strata, and only Strata

Replaces the recipe it was written to replace, which ends **every** `python.exe` on the PC and with it a Jupyter kernel, a build script or another model server:

```bat
for /f "tokens=2" %%a in ('tasklist ^| findstr "python.exe"') do taskkill /f /pid %%a
```

A process is now stopped only when one of two rules names it:

1. **launcher** — the python running *this install's* `serve\server.py` (its own interpreter inside the install, or the install's absolute script path in the command line);
2. **engine** — `strata.exe` / `strata-vision.exe` whose executable sits inside the install.

The launcher goes first, so a supervisor cannot restart the engine behind us. Each process gets a plain `taskkill` (`WM_CLOSE`) and only then `/F`. A process whose path cannot be read is reported and left alone rather than guessed. No match prints `没有找到正在运行的 Strata` and exits 0, so running it twice is safe. `-WhatIf` lists what would be stopped and stops nothing; `-Root` points it at another install.

## What it leaves alone

- **The default path is byte-identical.** An absent `arena_budget` adds nothing to the engine's arguments — `serve/test_arena_budget.py::Wiring::test_engine_args_without_the_key_is_byte_identical` asserts exactly that.
- A `--resident-budget-gib` already written into the config's `"args"` is **never** overridden: the number written by hand wins.
- No other config key is touched, and nothing is written back to the file.
- `warn_budget_over_ram` (#1080) is unchanged and still reports a share that ends up larger than the RAM this PC has free.
- Nothing in `src/`, `include/` or the setup path changes: no engine rebuild, no backend touched.

## How it was checked

- `python -m unittest serve.test_arena_budget` — 22 pass, no GPU and no model needed (shares on 16/32/64/128/256 GB, both clamps, the floor never beating the headroom, out-of-range and wrong-type refusals, a hand-written budget winning, the line said once per start, and the `engine_args` wiring).
- `python -m unittest serve.test_runconfig` — 9 pass (no regression in the Settings view).
- `from serve import server` imports clean; `engine_args({"args": [...]})` without the key returns the list unchanged.
- **The stop script, against a fake install:** a launcher and an engine placed under the root were both stopped, launcher first, exit code 0. A decoy `python.exe` whose command line mentions `serve\server.py` and the install path but whose executable lives outside the install was **left running**. A second run found nothing and exited 0. The decoy case is the regression that the first version of the rule failed, which is why rule 1 now needs the full absolute script path, not just the install path somewhere in the command line.
- Both scripts were parsed with `[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile` (0 errors) and are UTF-8 with BOM (`stop-strata.ps1`) / pure ASCII (`STOP.bat`), CRLF.

**Not tested:** a real engine start with the cap on a second machine, and the stop script against a genuine `strata.exe` (the engine had already exited when the fake-install run was made). The cap's effect on decode speed on this model is the trade the user chooses — the numbers in `bench/results/2026-10-01-iq4xs-64gb` say a RAM budget costs ~30% against a warm mapped run at that size, which is why this stays opt-in rather than a new default.

## Files

| file | |
|---|---|
| `serve/arena_budget.py` | new — the share, the two clamps, the line, the argument |
| `serve/test_arena_budget.py` | new — 22 tests |
| `serve/server.py` | +2 lines: the import, and one call in `engine_args` |
| `STOP.bat`, `stop-strata.ps1` | new — stop Strata, and only Strata |
| `docs/DETAILS.md` | the key, its defaults, its range, how it takes effect |
| `docs/AI_SETUP.md` | stopping the server on Windows |

title: Windows: make device_free_bytes() unified-memory aware on APUs (Strix Halo gfx1151)
body:
# Windows: `device_free_bytes()` is not unified-memory aware, so the auto expert cache cannot size on Strix Halo (gfx1151)

## Summary

On Windows, an APU with unified memory (Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S, `gfx1151`) reports a tiny
"free VRAM" figure through `cudaMemGetInfo` — essentially the free space of the BIOS's dedicated
carve-out, often well under 2 GiB. `device_free_bytes()` (`src/core/expert_cache.cpp`) only applies
its unified-memory correction (`MemAvailable` minus headroom) under `#if defined(__linux__)`, so on
Windows the auto expert cache sizes from the small figure and refuses to start
("no VRAM is left for the expert cache"), and an explicit `--expert-cache N` is silently shrunk to
0 slots by the sizing pass ("pre-filled 0 of 0 slots from the profile", no "expert cache N slots"
line).

This PR extends the same unified-memory correction to Windows: when the current device reports
integrated graphics, the free figure is raised to `GlobalMemoryStatusEx().ullAvailPhys` minus the
same `STRATA_UMA_HEADROOM_GIB` headroom (default 6 GiB). The Linux path is unchanged, and discrete
GPUs are unchanged (the integrated check is per device, as before).

## What it changes

- `src/core/expert_cache.cpp`, `device_free_bytes()`: the integrated-GPU detection moves out of the
  `__linux__`-only block (HIP exposes `cudaDevAttrIntegrated`), and a `_WIN32` branch adds the
  `GlobalMemoryStatusEx` path beside the Linux `/proc/meminfo` path. The
  `STRATA_UMA_HEADROOM_GIB` knob, its default of 6, and its semantics are shared.
- `#include <windows.h>` under `_WIN32` for `GlobalMemoryStatusEx`.

## What it leaves alone

- The Linux `/proc/meminfo` path, the gfx906 compat exclusion, the headroom default and env knob.
- Discrete GPUs on every platform (`unified_memory` false → plain `cudaMemGetInfo`).
- The SYCL port's own copy (`sycl/src/core/expert_cache.cpp`) — not touched.

## Measured on

Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Radeon 8060S, `gfx1151`, wave32), Windows 11 (build 26100), Adrenalin driver
32.0.31041.1004, self-built HIP engine from this tree (`tools/hip/build_windows.bat`,
`STRATA_HIP_ARCHS=gfx1151`, ROCm 10.2.0a20260930 wheels), IQ3_S, 200K context, MTP on.

Free figure seen by the engine (after the session's allocations), by BIOS carve-out, before the fix:

| carve-out | `device_free_bytes()` | result |
|---|---|---|
| 0.5 GB | ~0 | auto: refuse; forced: shrunk to 0 slots |
| 16 GB | 0.37 GiB | auto: refuse (needs 241 slots / 611 MiB at 32K) |
| 32 GB | ~1.1 GiB | only 32K context fits (438 slots); 200K refuses |
| 64 GB | 6.69 GiB | 200K sizes 19339 slots — but see the caveats below |

After the fix (16 GB carve-out, 200K): auto sizes 19339 slots (36.84 GiB), pre-fills all of them
from the profile (6.5 s), serves at 40-45 tok/s decode (96.9% cache hit rate), where every
configuration refused to start or shrank to 0 slots before.

## Caveats, stated plainly

- On this chip the dedicated carve-out is smaller than the cache either way, so the cache lands in
  the driver's shared pool (WDDM GTT backed by the same LPDDR5X). The server's
  "0 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded - LOW" warning still prints (the reserve check reads
  the same function, which now reports the large figure and never triggers the shrink loop).
  Measured no stalls across benchmark runs; a follow-up that also accounts for the carve-out in the
  shrink loop may be worth it, but it is deliberately not in this PR.
- The cache allocation is charged to the system commit on Windows (issue #60's note), so a big
  cache wants a page file with room. `tools/hip/build_windows.bat`'s engine printed that note
  during a failed open before the fix; with the fix the auto path converged on the first open.

## How it was checked

- Built the HIP engine for gfx1151 with the patch and ran setup + serving end to end (the numbers
  above). Without the patch, the same tree reproduces the refusals in the table.
- `src/core/expert_cache.cpp` is also compiled by the CUDA build; on Windows CUDA there is no
  integrated AMD GPU, and on Linux the CUDA build already took the `__linux__` path (unchanged).
  Not built here (no NVIDIA GPU on this PC) — the CUDA path's behaviour for a discrete GPU is
  unchanged by construction (the new code only runs when `unified_memory` is true).

title: prefill: the prompt path's MMQ scratch rides in the loan (opt-in, STRATA_MMQ_SLAB)
body:
## What this changes

`STRATA_MMQ_SLAB=1` (opt-in; unset is off): the prompt path's MMQ scratch — its stream-k fixup tiles — comes out of
the loan's unused tail instead of free VRAM.

llama.cpp's `mmq.cuh` allocates those tiles lazily through `ggml_cuda_pool`, which this build backs with a `cudaMalloc`
on whatever is free at that moment — a few MB on a card the expert cache has filled, at the one moment a prompt is
running, and a malloc that fails there aborts the engine mid-read instead of failing the request. A layout does not
use the whole loan: the carve is a bump, so everything from its stop to the loan's end is the prompt's own memory,
provably (a loan is whole cache slots and the top one is only partly needed).

The pool takes the tiles from there in **size classes** (a power of two, 128 KiB floor). The classes are load-bearing:
MMQ's J search picks a different J per launch, so a cache keyed on the exact size holds one buffer per J — 32 buffers,
31.5 MiB on a 579-token chunk in the Maya checkout's measurement — where a class bounds the pool to a few MB.

Three guards make it safe, all load-bearing: it is published per layout keyed on the tail's **address** (a request
whose chunk moves `used` moves the tail and the pool drops the old buffers); `Prefill::run` drops it once the prompt is
read, before the caller refills the borrowed slots; and the loan is the participant's own expert cache `cudaMalloc`ed
on this device, so the tail is this card's memory to write. A tail that is empty (the layout used the whole loan, or
spilled into owned buffers) publishes nothing, and the pool allocates as it always did.

From the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commit `bf844d5`.

## What it leaves alone

Unset (the default), the pool stays on free VRAM exactly as before: `lend_mmq_scratch` publishes nothing and
`mmq::pool_slab` is not given a slab. The size classes are part of the slab path only (they bound the slab's pool);
with the knob off there is no slab to bound. Default path unchanged by construction.

## Measurements

- That commit hit the failure at a 16,384-token chunk on a 5060 (3.4 MB free of 7,707.7 MB, 1.2 MB wanted) and measured
  the slab costing 42–47 more lent experts per part and no change to the chunk arithmetic, on its live split
  (5060/5060/3060/3060).
- **No speedup is claimed here.** What the start's check line shows is whether the slab is in use on a given rig.

## Checks

- **Default path:** unset = off by construction (`v != nullptr && std::atoi(v) != 0`).
- **Build:** `src/prefill/prefill.cpp` compiles clean with the build's own flags (`-fsyntax-only`);
  `src/prefill/ggml_cuda_host.cu` and `src/prefill/moe_moe.cu` compile clean with the build's nvcc flags (CUDA 13.2,
  `compute_86` and `compute_120`). The development branch that also carries the change built fully with ninja.
- **HIP / SYCL:** not compiled here (no toolchain on the machine). The device files this touches are the CUDA MMQ
  target's; the slab plumbing in `prefill.cpp` has no per-backend branch.
- **On a start:** `strata prefill mmq: CUDA%d the scratch pool takes a new N MiB buffer` prints for a buffer of 4 MiB
  or more; with `STRATA_MMQ_SLAB=1` and a loan that has a tail it should not appear at all, and a prompt should read
  to completion as before.

title: docs: --prompt-cache-every is not a piece-size dial here (the fork's is)
body: ## What this changes A docs bullet for `--prompt-cache-every`, in `docs/DETAILS.md`: the knob is **not** a piece-size dial in this engine. In the Maya checkout it is also a wall-time dial because there its marks bound the segments the prompt path reads, and every segment pays a fill and a drain of the part chain. What the bullet records: - The Maya checkout's numbers for its `STRATA_GLM_CKPT_EVERY` (same 16384 default), local commit `3095719` (2026-10-15), on a 100,535-token fresh read (Maya-L split, 8192-token chunks, one 580-token warm prompt before each arm, engine restarted between arms): `16384` cut the read into 5 pieces read in 148.8 s, `32768` into 4 in 134.9 s (-9.3%), `0` into one of 13 chunks in 93.2 s (-37.4%) — that checkout's numbers on its rig, a piece fitting ~14.6 s + 6.5 s a chunk there. - Why they do not carry over here: a periodic mark is saved at a chunk boundary and the run carries on, so no piece ends at it. What cuts this engine's read into runs is the cut list — a re-read (`STRATA_CKPT_REREAD`), the system-prompt root, a message boundary (`STRATA_CACHE_MESSAGE_BOUNDARY`), the start of the last turn and a pinned prefix — and each of those is one fill and drain. - So `--prompt-cache-every 0` here skips the periodic marks and the near-tail one (a `--prompt-cache-tail` mark needs `--prompt-cache-every` above 0), while the root, the last turn, a message boundary and a pin are still saved — the same trade the Maya checkout documents for its `0`: a client that rewrote a turn *before* the last one mounts a farther mark. The lever for a fresh long read here is those cuts, not this cadence. ## What it leaves alone Documentation only: not one line of code or default changes. Every name and flag the bullet cites was checked against the tree it documents (`--prompt-cache-every`, `--prompt-cache-tail`, `STRATA_CKPT_REREAD`, `STRATA_CACHE_MESSAGE_BOUNDARY`). ## Measurements The numbers above are quoted with what they were measured on (the Maya checkout's rig, Maya-L split, the warm prompt, the restarts between arms). No number is claimed for this engine. ## Checks - Docs-only change; no build to run. The rendered Markdown is the only output. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: prefill: STRATA_PREFILL_KEEP (128) is the slots a loan leaves the cache
body:
## What this changes

`STRATA_PREFILL_KEEP=N` (**128 by default**): the expert-cache slots a loan must leave resident while a prompt chunk
borrows the cache's tail. On a small cache it is this number, not the auto lend's 90% cap, that picks the chunk. On
the Q8_0 four-way's 691- and 937-slot stages it leaves 563 and 809 slots where the cap would leave 621 and 843.
`STRATA_GLM_PREFILL_KEEP` is accepted as the same knob.

**The clamp is up, not down**: a lend has to leave the elastic K/V a region to grow into (its floor is
`STRATA_KV_GROW_FLOOR`, 128 by default), so a smaller `N` is clamped to that floor and the start says so — lower both
together to lend more of the cache and let the chunk grow at the K/V's expense. A larger `N` keeps more experts
resident for the prompt's own tokens and buys a smaller chunk.

The number is the same one the auto scan, the per-stage lend regions, the serve loan, the smallest cache a start
accepts and the vram-elastic reserve used before; this change routes all of them through one reader of the variable.

From the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commit `71c1ca7` (2026-10-15).

## What it leaves alone

Unset, every use is 128, exactly as before — this is by construction, not a measurement, and this PR's default run
is byte-identical on that path. With the variable set to 128 (its default) the numbers are also unchanged.

## Measurements

That commit lowered its pool's floor from 13 to 11 slots a layer (`STRATA_GLM_RESERVE_MB=400`) on a four-way split and
measured, on a 99,758-token conversation, the binding part reach an 8192-token chunk: a 49,152-token piece
61,762 → 57,507 ms (-6.9%) and a whole five-piece read 161,291 → 158,938 ms, on the live split (5060/5060/3060/3060)
— where it was not a free win either (a 16,384-token piece that went from three chunks to two lost 3%,
28,716 → 29,651 ms, since the parts run a chunk as a chain and there is less left to overlap). **No number is claimed
for our rig**: the four-way Q8_0 runs so far used 128, which is this default.

## Checks

- **Default path:** unset = 128 everywhere by construction.
- **Build:** `src/program/generate.cpp` compiles clean against this branch's headers with the build's own flags
  (`-fsyntax-only`; one pre-existing unused-variable warning in unrelated code). The development branch that also
  carries the change built fully with ninja (CUDA 13.2).
- **HIP / SYCL:** not compiled here (no toolchain on the machine). `generate.cpp` carries no per-backend code, so both
  builds compile the same change.

title: serve: STRATA_WARM_PROMPT (off) reads one synthetic prompt before READY
body:
Title: serve: STRATA_WARM_PROMPT (off) reads one synthetic prompt before READY

## What this changes

`STRATA_WARM_PROMPT=N` (`--serve`, off by default): one synthetic prompt of N tokens (32 if you ask for less) is read
through the whole part chain **before the engine says READY**, so a session's first request does not pay what only a
session's first prompt pays — the first chunk carries every kernel's first launch, the prompt path's own allocations
and the tiers' first reads, and no later prompt pays any of it. `STRATA_GLM_WARM_PROMPT` is accepted as the same
knob.

The synthetic ids are spread over the vocabulary (`100 + (i * 131) % 20000`), so the routes are not one expert's. It
takes the same loan a request takes (the slots the prompt path is laid out in go non-resident and are refilled from
the arena afterwards), and every participant's state is zeroed before and after it, so no conversation can see it. A
prompt path that cannot run prints why and the first prompt pays it; the start never fails because of it.

From the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commit `cc58309` (2026-10-14).

## What it leaves alone

Unset or `0` (the default), the whole block is skipped and the engine says READY exactly as before. Nothing outside
the block changes; this is by construction.

## Measurements

The Maya checkout's issue #8 reported 95–133 ms/token on a first prompt against 23–44 warm — that checkout's number
on its rig. On this engine the knob is how you measure it: the first request's time to first token, or its `PP` line,
with the variable set and unset is the A/B. **No number is claimed here**, because it has not been run on our
hardware.

## Checks

- **Default path:** unset = off by construction (`wn = 0` skips the block).
- **Build:** `src/program/generate.cpp` compiles clean against this branch's headers with the build's own flags
  (`-fsyntax-only`; one pre-existing unused-variable warning in unrelated code). The development branch that also
  carries the change built fully with ninja (CUDA 13.2).
- **HIP / SYCL:** not compiled here (no toolchain on the machine). `generate.cpp` carries no per-backend code, so both
  builds compile the same change.
- **On a start:** the engine prints `strata serve: warming the prompt path with a N-token prompt before READY`.

title: prefill: STRATA_PREFILL_STAGES (opt-in) prints where a prompt chunk's wall went
body:
## What this changes

`STRATA_PREFILL_STAGES=1` (opt-in; unset is off) turns on the chunk's stage line: **one line a stage a chunk** with
where the chunk's wall went — the chunk's wall, the copy lane's own span split into what ran before it (lead), the
lane itself and what ran behind it (tail), the bytes it moved and the bytes the chunk's consumers waited on (the
difference is the ring's read-ahead), the hand-off a later stage of a layer split paid, the GPU's own phases over the
chunk, and the experts and host time it spent. It also turns the phase timer on.

Without it a prefill change can only be judged by the prompt's ms/token, which mixes the chunk size, the copy lane,
the host and the phases. The line is what separates them.

From the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commit `a34f57c`, with its fixes `04b8d65` (the line's events are
destroyed with the prompt path) and `63b3690` (the line reads only the events its chunk recorded). Its spelling
`STRATA_GLM_PREFILL_STAGES` is accepted as the same knob, so a config written for that checkout runs unchanged.

## What it leaves alone

Unset (the default), `stages_on()` is false: no line is printed, the phase timer is not read for it, and no extra
sync is taken for it. The syncs the line does add when on wait only on copies the compute stream has already waited
for (the issuer is joined when the chunk ends), so `STRATA_PREFILL_STAGES=0` beside a `--bench` A/B is how you check
it costs nothing. The default path is unchanged by construction.

## Measurements

This is a diagnostic; it makes no claim to speed anything up. Its own cost is what the set-vs-unset A/B under
`--bench` measures, and the design keeps that at zero by waiting only on work already joined.

## Checks

- **Default path:** unset = off by construction (`stages_on()` reads the environment once and returns false).
- **Build:** `src/prefill/prefill.cpp` compiles clean against this branch's headers with the build's own flags
  (`-fsyntax-only`). The development branch that also carries the change built fully with ninja (CUDA 13.2).
- **HIP / SYCL:** not compiled here (no toolchain on the machine). The change adds no backend-specific branch; it uses
  the same stream/event API the file already used, and the events are only created when the knob is on.

title: STRATA_MTP_ROOM_MIN — a long prompt takes the MTP drafter's 512 experts (decode-only) as ring
body:
## What this changes

`STRATA_MTP_ROOM_MIN=TOKENS` (`--serve` with `--mtp`): a prompt of at least TOKENS tokens (`0`: every prompt) uses
the MTP drafter's 512 routed experts as the prompt path's ring while it is read. Those are 708 MB (675 MiB) that only
the **decode** reads — `record_rest` is their only reader; a prompt's passes run the draft layer's dense tensors and
its K/V — so the prompt path's ring is pointed **at the block itself**: `slot i = experts_base + (i - rule) *
MAXBLOB` (135 slots on a Q8_0 pack, whose largest blob is 4.98 MiB). Opening and closing a room moves the ring count
alone (`Prefill::set_ring_room_active`): the block is never freed, never allocated again and never moves, so no
prompt path is laid out again, the decode's captured round/step graphs stay valid (nothing is dropped), and what
comes back before the first window is the decode's own bytes (`MtpDrafter::experts_reclaim`). In the measured shape's
successor this is two 675 MiB DMAs around the read.

Limits, refused with the reason at start: `--serve` only, `--mtp` needed, `--batch` not supported (its slot drafters
share the solo drafter's weights). A layer split is fine (the room goes to the prompt path on the drafter's card),
`--pipeline-windows` is fine (the room closes before the request's first window), and `--prefill-head-alias` is fine.

From the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commits `7df369c` (`STRATA_GLM_ROOM_MIN`), `d4d0792` (the tail's
slots rounded up to the largest blob) and `5ccf9a4` (the in-place shape, for the MTP config's NextN block).

## What it leaves alone

Unset (the default) `mtp_room_min` is `-1` and not one line of the room runs; the prompt path is laid out exactly as
before. The new code is reachable only behind that check. This is by construction, not by a measurement.

## Measurements

- **The first shape was measured on our Q8_0 4-way rig (2026-10-16): it works, and it bought no time.** The room
  opened, the 675 MiB really went into the ring, the block came back before the first window and the decode ran
  unchanged — but a deeper ring was not what the prompt waited on at 3,080 or 14,859 tokens. That shape laid the
  prompt path out again around the block and cost **3.4–4.0 s per roomed request** on top of the read.
- **The shape in this PR is the in-place one** (no rebuild, no spill allocation, block never moves). It is built and
  compile-clean but **its runtime has not been run yet**; its expected cost is the two 675 MiB DMAs (~0.12 s), which
  is an estimate, not a measurement.
- `7df369c` records the room as not yet measured, with its standing baseline 89.5 s (1,123 tok/s) on its
  byte-identical 100,535-token read.
- **No speedup is claimed here.** The knob is how you measure it: the same prompt with the variable set and unset,
  `PP` line against `PP` line. Expect a gain only where the ring is the limit.

## Checks

- **Default path:** unset = off by construction (the parsed threshold is `-1` and every room call is behind it).
- **Build:** the three host files this touches (`src/prefill/prefill.cpp`, `src/core/mtp.cpp`,
  `src/program/generate.cpp`) compile clean against this branch's headers with the build's own flags
  (`-fsyntax-only`; one pre-existing unused-variable warning in unrelated code). The development branch that also
  carries the change built fully with ninja (`ninja -C build strata`, CUDA 13.2).
- **HIP / SYCL:** not compiled here (no toolchain on the machine). The room uses the same CUDA API the file already
  used (`cudaMallocHost`/`cudaFreeHost`/`cudaMemcpy` beside its existing `cudaFree`/`cudaStreamSynchronize`).
- **On a start:** the engine prints the room's threshold, MiB and slots; if the drafter's block ever moved, the
  first shape said so — the in-place shape cannot.

title: prefill: STRATA_PREFILL_MAX, a per-part prompt-chunk ceiling
body:
## What this changes

`STRATA_PREFILL_MAX="8192,4096,8192,8192"` — an opt-in ceiling on the prompt chunk of each prompt-path
participant, in the split's order. Entry 0 is the first card's path (it reads the chunk's embeddings and hands
its rows on), entry *i* the *i*-th stage; `0` or an absent entry is no ceiling, and values are multiples of 256.
`STRATA_GLM_PREFILL_MAX` is accepted as the same knob.

Strata's layer split is one grid: every stage reads prompt chunks of the chain's size, so a card whose expert
cache cannot fund one pulls *every* stage down to its number (the `#448` warning). The ceiling is the other
choice: a capped stage lays out at `min(chain, its cap)` and `Prefill::run_impl`'s `c0 += m.T` loop reads each
larger hand-off in steps of its own, forwarding each sub-step, while the other stages keep the chain's chunk.
A ceiling only lowers a stage and never raises one.

From the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commit `ef3b6e7` (2026-10-15).

Every chunk-pricing site prices a part at its own chunk: the auto scan (`fits_one`, `ring_room`, the old
candidate list), the serve loan (`lend`), the resident-RAM lend regions, stage init (at the stage's own maximum —
`relayout` requires `chunk <= T_max`), the init retry, split-small's extra slots, the own-buffers headroom test
and the head-alias candidates. The start prints one line per capped entry:
`strata serve: prompt chunk: CUDA%d reads N tokens a step (STRATA_PREFILL_MAX N)`, with
`, inside a larger chain chunk` when the cap is below the chain's.

## What it leaves alone

Unset, not one number changes: the list is empty, `part_chunk` / `part_ceiling` return the chain chunk,
`max_head` is 0, and the new print loop runs zero times. This is by construction, not by a measurement.

## Measurements

- That local commit measured moving every part as a loss: 94,840 ms for the capped 16k/16k/8k/7k shape against
  91,718.9 ms for 13 equal chunks of 7,744, on its byte-identical 100,535-token read (an earlier nesting took
  98,568.1 ms). That is why a ceiling only lowers a stage and why this is opt-in.
- **No speedup is claimed here.** On the four-way Q8_0 rig this was written for, the start log does show the case
  the knob is for — the chain settles at 4096 because CUDA3's 690 slots cannot fund 6912
  (`WARNING: prompt chunk 4096 tokens, not 6912 ...`, `#448`) — but a binding-cap A/B
  (`STRATA_PREFILL_MAX="8192,8192,8192,2048"`, expecting the chain to rise toward CUDA0's own 6912 while CUDA3
  reads its hand-offs in 2048-token steps) has not been run yet. Numbers to follow.

## Checks

- **Default path:** unset = byte-identical by construction (empty list; every priced site returns the chain
  chunk; no arithmetic changes).
- **Build:** CUDA. `generate.cpp` is host-only code and this adds no device code; it compiles clean against this
  branch's headers with the build's own flags (`-fsyntax-only`; one pre-existing unused-variable warning in
  unrelated code). The development branch that also carries the change built fully with ninja (nvcc 13.2).
- **HIP / SYCL:** not compiled here (no toolchain on the machine). `generate.cpp` carries no per-backend code, so
  both builds compile the same change.
- **On a start:** the new per-participant line above; an unset-vs-set A/B of the prefill rate is the test of
  whether a cap pays on a given rig.

title: bench: RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100) on AOOSTAR AG03 Oculink eGPU — swift-1.5 IQ2_XS, 131K context
body:
Adds a community benchmark: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX 24 GB (gfx1100) in an
AOOSTAR AG03 eGPU dock (Sapphire Pulse) over Oculink, driven by an ASRock
NUC Box K12 mini-PC (Ryzen 7 H 255, 64 GB RAM, Fedora).

## Setup

- **Strata** 0.1.44.1 (commit 296b59d2), engine 0.1.44.1, hip backend
- **Model** swift-1.5, IQ2_XS, 131,072-token context, 1 parallel slot
- **Config** `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp rt --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`,
  thinking off, temperature 0
- **GPU connection:** the 7900 XTX is not socketed in the mini-PC — it's an
  eGPU over Oculink. The engine matches the link at `pcie_frac 0.19`
  (~1/4 of a desktop x16 PCIe 4.0 bandwidth), so prompt/decode transfers
  are Oculink-bound. Noted in the report so reviewers don't discount the
  prompt rates.

## Results (suite 1, 3 runs each, medians with ranges)

| Test | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s | TTFT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Short chat (~46 → 100 new tokens) | — | 86.1 (67.1–105.3) | 0.35 s |
| 4K fresh | 1098.4 | — | 3.68 s |
| 16K fresh | 1389.7 | — | 11.58 s |
| 32K fresh | 1411.9 | — | 22.74 s |
| Agent follow-up turns | ~800 cached | 85.4 (68.1–122.5) | 3.65 s |

- Agent-session conversation-cache hit: **68.6%**, only ~52 earlier tokens
  re-read per session; ~13,729 new file tokens read once.

## Notes / limitations

- Speed only — no correctness check was run.
- Background load and GPU power limits not recorded.
- Suite total: 206 s. No concurrency test (`--clients`) was run.
- Per-request data: `results.json`. The server was already running, so there
  is no `engine-log-excerpt.txt` in this folder.

Adds `bench/results/2026-10-17-community-rx-7900-xtx-oculink-swift-1-5-iq2-xs-2/`
(README.md + results.json). No engine or runtime changes.

title: Web search and page reading for the web app's Chat (DuckDuckGo default, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Serper)
body:
## Web search and page reading for the web app's Chat

The Chat tab gets a built-in web search, modeled after how Open WebUI and similar chat tools do it: the model can look the question up before answering, and the answer shows its sources. **Web search is completely off by default**: until the user turns it on in Chat Settings, nothing about this feature sends anything out of the PC. Strata's Chat is deliberately lean, and this feature is built the same way: it adds no tokens until a chat turns search on, and results are budget-capped to a small slice of the model's context (defaults scale with the context window), so the Chat gains recent information without losing what makes it comfortable for long sessions.

### What it looks like in the UI
- A globe button in the composer (first icon, before the paperclip) toggles search for the next message.
- **Chat Settings** (gear) has a *Web search* section: enable/disable, engine picker, SearXNG URL, API key field, max results, page reading and a page reader mode (see below).
- When search is on, the results are injected as context before the model's turn, with an instruction to answer from them and cite by `[n]`.
- Under each answer the sources appear as `Sources (DuckDuckGo): [1] … | [2] …` (clickable, engine named, read pages get a `read` badge), and they are included in the "Save this chat as Markdown" export.

### Reading result pages in full
Snippets alone often miss the details, so search can also fetch the top result pages and inject their extracted text (Open WebUI's "Web Loader" idea, stdlib `html.parser` based, which skips nav/footer/scripts, prefers `main`/`article`):
- **"Read result pages"** toggle + **"Pages to read"** (1-5).
- **"Limit page text"** toggle (on by default) with a **"Max characters per page"** field (default 5000). Turning it off sends whole pages; see the budget below for why that is still safe.

### Page reader: direct fetch, or Jina Reader for JS-heavy pages
Plain `urllib` cannot render JavaScript-heavy pages, so there is a 3-tier **Page reader** setting:
- **Direct only (default)**: only the Strata server fetches pages; nothing goes to any third party.
- **Jina as fallback**: direct first; pages that fail (JS walls, blocks) are retried through [r.jina.ai](https://r.jina.ai) (free hosted headless browser, no key needed, Apache-2.0).
- **Jina for all pages**: every page goes through r.jina.ai.
- The base URL is overridable via `STRATA_JINA_URL` (e.g. a self-hosted instance), and failures of either path degrade to a readable combined reason.
- **Privacy is surfaced, not buried**: the dropdown explains per selection, a warning line appears whenever a third party could see the URLs, and turning search on fires a toast that names the engine *and* the reader mode ("… go through r.jina.ai - a third party sees those URLs").

### Context-aware reading budget
How much search text goes into the prompt scales with the model's own context window (`reported_ctx()`), so small-context instances are never overloaded:
- The reading budget is a slice of the window (~3 chars/token): **10 %** normally, **25 %** when the user explicitly turns the per-page limit off; the per-page cap is then derived from the budget instead of a fixed number.
- First-use defaults scale the same way from `/health`'s `max_context` (e.g. 16K ctx → 4 results / 1 page × 3000 chars; 128K → 6 / 2 × 5000; 262K → 8 / 3 × 5000).
- Unknown context falls back to the plain 5000/page default.

### Distinct, persistent search warnings
A failed search no longer fails silently: the reason stays on the message (in the sources line, warning-colored) and in the Markdown export, with a different message per cause:
- **no API key set** → `Brave Search needs its API key (Chat Settings > Web search)` (same for Tavily/Serper; a *rejected* key gets its own message, incl. Brave's 422)
- **engine unreachable** (e.g. SearXNG not running) → `SearXNG at http://127.0.0.1:8888 is not reachable (…); start it or pick another engine`
- **DuckDuckGo bot check** → DDG's lite endpoint answers Chrome-impersonating UAs with its `anomaly.js` page; the fetcher uses an honest custom UA and, if the bot page still shows up, says so instead of reporting "no results"
- **engine reachable but nothing found** → `no results`
- **unreadable page** → per-result `read_error` (shown as a warning line), never a silent empty string

### Security hardening
- **`/search` sits behind the web app's own-page guard** (`_own_page`): a JSON body is required (415 for form posts) and a foreign `Origin` is rejected (403; `trusted_origins` still allowed), so a random web page cannot make this PC run searches or fetch URLs through it.
- **http(s) only**: the SearXNG base URL and every result URL that gets page-read pass a scheme check (`_http_url`); `file://`, `data:`, `javascript:` and friends are refused with an explicit reason, so page reading can never become a local file reader.
- **Source links render defensively**: only `http(s)` URLs become clickable `<a href>`; anything else shows as plain text, so no `javascript:`/`data:` links from a poisoned result.
- **Prompt-injection hardening**: the injected search context states that titles, snippets and page text are untrusted web data whose embedded instructions must not be followed.
- **LAN-bound warning**: `/health` reports `lan_bound` (server bound beyond loopback, e.g. `0.0.0.0`); turning search on fires an extra toast line warning that queries and engine keys then cross the network in plain HTTP and that devices on it can use the search without an api_key. On the default `127.0.0.1` bind this warning never appears.
- API keys stay browser-only (localStorage); nothing search-related is stored server-side.

### Settings drawer updates
- The drawer was titled **"Sampling"**; since it now also holds web search settings it is renamed to **"Chat Settings"** (gear tooltip: "Chat Settings: Thinking & Web Search"), the close button got a proper "Close" tooltip, and the save toast says "Settings saved".
- The **Reset** button turns web search completely off and restores the first-use defaults: search disabled, engine back to DuckDuckGo, no API key, instead of leaving a stale engine or an active search behind.
- The empty-state privacy note is qualified and split into two fixed lines: "Nothing leaves it. / Web search is off by default - when on, only the search query goes out."

### Scroll fix (drive-by)
Auto-follow-to-bottom was broken for turns where content grows past the stick threshold mid-stream (the thinking panel expanding could pin the view at the user's own message). Stickiness is now captured *before* the content grows, so the view keeps following the answer.

### Engines
| engine | needs |
|---|---|
| DuckDuckGo (default, labeled "anonymous - no key needed") | nothing (lite endpoint) |
| SearXNG | a running instance (default `http://127.0.0.1:8888`) |
| Brave Search | API key |
| Tavily | API key |
| Serper (Google) | API key |

### Design notes
- `serve/websearch.py` is **stdlib-only** (`urllib`, `json`, `re`, `html.parser`, `os`); no new dependencies, cross-platform (Windows/Linux/macOS).
- `POST /search` carries its own engine config per request; **nothing is stored on the server**: API keys stay in the browser's localStorage, like the existing API-key field.
- All providers are fetched through the Strata server (a browser could not call them directly because of CORS).
- Page fetches are capped (10 s timeout, 2 MB download); read results use an explicit contract (`content` on success, `read_error` on failure, `read_via` for Jina-read pages) instead of heuristics.
- `/search` has a catch-all so an unexpected error returns a clean 502 with a server-side log line instead of a broken connection.

### Tested
Interactively on Windows with the live web app: DuckDuckGo and SearXNG return real results; each failure mode (missing key, rejected key, unreachable engine, DDG bot check, no results) shows its own warning on the message; sources appear in the answer and in the Markdown export; Reset restores DuckDuckGo defaults; the chat view follows long answers to the bottom. Page reading: real pages extract correctly; JS-heavy pages are rescued by the Jina tiers (fallback and always modes verified end-to-end, incl. both-paths-fail combined error); the budget math was unit-tested across context sizes (16K/128K, limit on/off, unknown context). The security behavior is covered by a 102-check regression suite: scheme guard against 15 non-http poison URLs across all three reader tiers, origin guard 403/415 vs. legitimate 200 on the live server, budget clamps at 10 %/25 % of the context, reader tier matrix and combined-error formatting as unit tests, and `lan_bound` verified on loopback vs. `0.0.0.0` mock servers.

Happy to adjust anything (naming, where the settings live, engine list, budget shares, the Jina default) if this should look different.

title: Q36: release the GGUF mapping and stop zeroing the overwritten arena
body:
## Summary
Implements the Q36 memory-compaction plan (`docs/Q36_MEMORY_COMPACTION.md`): the engine reports its own memory/compaction counters, releases the GGUF mapping after load, and stops zeroing the 18.75 GiB expert arena it immediately overwrites. The original goal - quiet the `kcompactd` churn - was already met by host settings; the measured engine win is ~18.5 GiB of RAM returned to the OS at no decode cost.

## What changed
- `include/strata/platform/mem_report.{hpp,cpp}` (new) + `src/platform/mem_report_test.cpp`: read `/proc/meminfo`, `/proc/vmstat` and the THP mode into the engine's own log, behind `STRATA_MEM_REPORT` (off by default). A row the kernel does not export prints `-`, not 0.
- `include/strata/artifact/gguf_reader.hpp`: `GgufFile::release_pages()`/`released()` and `GgufModel::release_pages()`/`released()` — `madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)` then `posix_fadvise(POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED)` (fadvise cannot drop pages that are still mapped).
- `src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu`: `release_model_mapping()` after `place_experts()`, on by default; `STRATA_Q36_RELEASE_MAPPING=0` reverts. A guard makes `expert_blob()` fail loudly if it is ever called after the release. The arena memset now zeroes only the stride padding and the `kMmqTail` tail (plus an NVFP4 scale tail) instead of the whole 18.75 GiB.
- `tests/core/expert_blob_padding_test.cpp` (new): the padding-only zeroing is byte-identical to the whole memset.

## Extra Notes
Measured on an RTX 4060 Max-Q 8 GiB, Ryzen 7 7735HS, 62 GB, 32K, `--kv int8 --mtp 2`:

| | Cached | MemFree | decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 47.27 GiB | 3.47 GiB | ~10 |
| after | 28.75 GiB | 22.03 GiB | ~10 |

`Mlocked` stayed 104 KiB throughout - `cudaHostAlloc` on this driver (580.178.04) is memfd/shm-backed, not mlocked, so the plan's "un-pin the arena" phase and its dependent were dropped.

Built: CPU suite 44/44, CUDA build, and the native-expert parity suite on the card (14/14). HIP and SYCL builds were not run here (no ROCm/SYCL on this box).

title: serve: opt-in single-engine preemption for short requests
body:
## Goal

Let an interactive request run during a long single-engine response, while retaining the ordinary speculative decode path. The long stream stays connected and continues afterwards. Closes https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/2821.

This covers an already-running single `GEN`. #2109 addresses priority when admitting work to batch slots; this option rejects batch/parallel/replica configurations.

## Change

- Add opt-in `solo_priority: true`, off by default. Explicit integer `priority`, or a small-request boost when omitted; five-second minimum run quantum and 30-second queue aging.
- `STOP`, drain accepted tokens through `DONE`, then resume with original token IDs plus accepted output. Keep the original streaming parser, UTF-8 decoder, tool-call identity and sampled seed alive.
- Scoped cancellation for queued/active/parked requests; explicit failure on engine death. Serialize maintenance around parked work. Keep per-request statistics separate.
- Guard restored-prefix prefill: reach decoding before yielding so the engine cannot consume and discard a restored snapshot mid-prefill. Regression reproduces the failure on the earlier implementation.
- Add counters, deployment/rollback documentation, real-pipe tests and reproducible synthetic soak/lifecycle clients. No returned model tool is executed by these clients.

No native source, engine binary, cache format or model change. Default remains off. The old protocol body is extracted into `_generate_single`; normalized AST checks match the old dispatch/validation/protocol after excluding the opt-in callback. `server.py` as a whole is not byte-identical. Full Python regression suite below also exercises the default path.

## Validation

- Python 3.11.7 with regex 2026.9.10: 798 tests, 790 passed and 8 skipped, 296.962 seconds.
- Thirteen focused scheduler tests: trailing accepted tokens after STOP, split UTF-8, tools, cold and restored prefill, fairness, cancellation and engine failure. Old code fails the new restored-prefill regression; current code passes.
- Original non-abliterated Qwen3.8 Flash Next, ISTA-DASLab GSQ-RCO IQ3_S; Windows11 / RTX3090 24GiB / R95900X /128GiB. One-hour runtime `b121239`, final failure-path correction/control runtime `69a6b86`, upstream `296b59d`, unchanged v0.1.44.1 native binary.
- One-hour three-conversation soak plus interactive requests: 409 results (395 normal completions, 14 intentional cancellations), 94 tool/result round trips, 28 exact 20-field audits, 301 pauses and zero processed-prefix losses. Short text TTFT: median 0.669s, p95 7.054s, max 46.503s. Independent strict JSON checks passed all 395 successful responses.
- Queued/active/parked disconnects leave the other client working and queues empty. Native Responses emits one 450-item call and recalls its result. Native-exit injection found a script-launch exception-identity defect; fixed and regression-tested. Final native retest: both Chat/Responses return structured errors within 1.228s; a new request auto-loads and succeeds in 23.621s. The full hour is reported on b121239; the corrected error path and matched control were retested on 69a6b86.
- Final same-build 3-pair-per-arm comparison: short TTFT 20.128→0.561s, aggregate 113.041→108.803tok/s(-3.75%), pair 27.362→28.428s(+3.89%). All six audits and short answers pass. A Windows GBK result-reader error occurred after completed measurements; retained UTF-8 records were independently revalidated and the controller error is disclosed. No measurements were replaced.

See [full report](https://github.com/Zcg2021/Strata/blob/d72db88fa76b9ae8631167eeecf2dada62c50d0f/bench/results/2026-10-16-solo-priority-qwen-soak/README.md) for exact settings, methodology, per-request measurements and the preflight failures. Earlier SC117 measurements are supplementary, not pooled into the original-model result.

## Limits

This is cooperative scheduling, not a hard real-time guarantee. One history rollover restored only 16K of a 132K prompt and a short request waited46.503s while the protected remaining prefill completed; no processed-prefix loss was recorded. Images/GENI and checkpoint opt-outs are not preempted. Cold first-prefill interruption may incur reread work.

The soak uses deterministic synthetic manifests, receipts and fact audits; it is not unrestricted autonomous development, model-generated compaction, or evidence that the model is hallucination-free. An earlier boolean-schema failure occurred equally with the flag off/on and is retained in the reports. One hour on one Windows/CUDA machine is not overnight or cross-backend validation. Native CUDA/HIP/SYCL files are untouched; no native backend build is claimed.

Rollback: remove/disable `solo_priority` and restart. Existing model, config and cache formats continue to work.
