title: metal: --rope-scaling, --rope-scale, --rope-freq-base, --rope-freq-scale and --yarn-* reach the decode window's RoPE table
body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #2767. No other issue or pull request covers RoPE scaling on the Mac engine (search in the first comment).

Every file:line is at 296b59d (v0.1.44.1, the last release) unless marked "branch". Short names are the files under src/, include/ or metal/, not their copies under sycl/; CMakeLists.txt is the root one. On the branch, window.cpp's lines 18-467 move 1 down and its lines after 475 move 4 up, setup_host.cpp's lines after 125 move 6 down, and metal/CMakeLists.txt's lines 106-123 move 9 down and its lines after 123 move 16 down.

## Summary
On a Mac, `--rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 4` is parsed, resolved and logged as active (`strata generate: rope scaling yarn, factor 4 ...`, generate.cpp:3002-3008), but, by the code, no rotation changes:
- `rope_table_set` does nothing on Metal (metal/src/engine/setup_host.cpp:151, "the window keeps its own table");
- every RoPE rotation on Metal is in `qsa_prep`, which reads only the decode window's own cos/sin table (qsa.metal:74);
- `Window::init` builds that table without scaling, from the model file's `rope.freq_base` (window.cpp:468-475).

This PR makes the window build the table with `build_rope_table(64, rope_scaling(), ...)`, the builder the PC's session table uses (layer.cpp:837-840). setup_host.cpp:116-150 keeps rope.cu:48-86: the same 417 tokens once comments, whitespace and braces are ignored. By the code, linear and YaRN scaling, the magnitude factor (YaRN's mscale, or `--yarn-attn-factor`), `--rope-freq-base` and `--rope-freq-scale` then reach every rotation on a Mac without a kernel change (the reading is in the first comment). On an M5 Max (On-model results), yarn x4 changes the decode windows' logits on this branch and changes nothing on main (#2767); for each prompt path (the resident prompt chain, the streaming prompt GEMM) the test compares how close the path stays under yarn x4 to the same prompts read through decode windows, against a threshold derived in the same sitting, and for both paths that threshold did not separate the measured numbers, so they stay a code reading, as the MTP draft layer does.

This is one engine part needed to run past the trained 262,144 tokens on a Mac, not all of them: Mac setup does not write the flags, and nothing checks the memory a long context takes on a resident pack.

## What changed
- `metal/src/engine/window.cpp`: the table loop in `Window::init` becomes one `window_rope_table(strata::kernels::rope_scaling(), MAXC + 16, cs_.as<float>())` call. The table keeps its size (MAXC + 16 rows) and layout (float2 [pos][32]).
- `metal/src/engine/rope_window.h` (new): `window_rope_table` builds the table with `build_rope_table` into two temporary vectors of (MAXC + 16) x 32 floats each (branch rope_window.h:21), freed when it returns, and interleaves them into the window's rows; nothing it allocates stays. The window and the test run this same code.
- `metal/src/engine/setup_host.cpp`: a declaration of the scaled `build_rope_table` with `__attribute__((flatten))` (branch :126-131), so `RopeScaling::mscale()` is inlined into it under the flag below; the function's body does not change. The file's opening comment now says that `rope_scaling()` and `build_rope_table` fill the window's table.
- `metal/CMakeLists.txt`: `set_source_files_properties(${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/engine/setup_host.cpp PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "-ffp-contract=off")`, the form CMakeLists.txt:450-453 uses for two HIP files, with a comment that gives the by-hand check for the flatten (below); and the `rope_table_parity` target with `add_test`. The test has its own folder because `tests/*.cpp` are globbed into mtl_rt-only programs (metal/CMakeLists.txt:41-47). Setup builds only `strata` (setup_mac.py:280).
- `metal/tests/engine/rope_table_parity.cpp` (new; CPU only, no GPU or model; 5.7 s and 0.54 GB in ctest on the M5 Max). At the allocation of the 1M probe (bench/results/2026-10-09-rope-yarn-long-context/probe.py, whose default capacity is `--max-context 1048832`, probe.py:32), 1,048,976 rows, it checks:
  1. unscaled: the new table against the replaced loop, byte for byte at every row; and with `--rope-freq-base 5e6`, against that loop given the same base (a copy of the test whose table ignores the base fails here);
  2. yarn x2, x3 and x4, linear x4, yarn x4 with `--yarn-attn-factor 0.9`, linear x4 with `--yarn-attn-factor 1.25` and yarn with `--rope-freq-scale 0.3`: bit for bit against a float64 transcription of ggml's `rope_yarn` (llama.cpp 3cf03257, ggml-cpu/ops.cpp:5958-5973) with every operation rounded on its own. As in src/kernels/rope_parity.cpp:233-236, the correction dims and the ramp come from the shared helpers; an oracle written from ggml's own formulas checks those too (first comment, with its code);
  3. row 0 is (mscale, 0); under YaRN the correction window is pairs [14, 22], and at the last row the first pair extrapolates and the last pair interpolates.

What it leaves alone:
- **The Metal kernels.** No `.metal` file is touched, the spare indexer key included (Extra Notes).
- **Mac setup.** On a Mac, setup.py hands every argument to `metal/setup_mac.py` before its own parser runs (setup.py:5706-5707, 5446), so the `--rope-scaling` and `--rope-scale` it defines (setup.py:5715-5719) never reach that parser; setup_mac.py still drops them with "not used on a Mac" (setup_mac.py:508-510) and writes no rope flags. Setup support is a later PR, which has to count a long context's memory first.
- **Every file outside `metal/`.** The root CMakeLists.txt and sycl/CMakeLists.txt do not reference `metal/`, so no CUDA, HIP or SYCL build compiles a changed file. They were not built.
- **docs/MAC.md.** "Context: measured up to 32K" (MAC.md:176) changes only with measured results.

### How the default path was checked
All on an M5 Max (128 GB), AppleClang 21.0.0, against the Metal build of 296b59d; the commands and their output lines are in the first comment.
1. **The table.** Test check 1: byte-identical at all 1,048,976 rows; a row depends only on its position, so every smaller context's table is a prefix. On the default path `rope_scaling()` is `RopeScaling{}` with `freq_base` from the model file's `qwen4exp.rope.freq_base` (generate.cpp:2940, 2969, 2978-2990), the key the window read before.
2. **The model files.** The GGUF headers (metadata only) of the six models Mac setup offers (setup_mac.py:45-55) and of the abliterated IQ3_S the on-model tests use all carry `qwen4exp.rope.freq_base = 10000000.0` and no `rope.scaling.*` key.
3. **The object code.** Of the 70 objects both builds have, `otool -X -s __TEXT __text <object> | shasum` differs only for `setup_host.cpp.o` (97573d5fa328b5c1 -> fd4ef0c308696cb7) and `window.cpp.o` (afaf2e316677789d -> fc9d170bb55b5ea8). In setup_host.cpp.o 36 of 37 functions are identical; only `build_rope_table(int, const RopeScaling&, int, float*, float*)` changes. In window.cpp.o, with the checkout path normalized, only `Window::init` changes; `window_rope_table` is new and the `std::map` lookup the old loop made is gone.
4. **Build and tests.** ctest passes 2/2 (`runtime_hello`, `rope_table_parity`). `-Wall -Wextra` gives no warning on setup_host.cpp, the test or a file that includes only rope_window.h. `tools.test_setup_mac` and `tools.test_setup_rope` pass (38 tests); no setup file is changed.

### Why `-ffp-contract=off`, and why `flatten`
The project holds this table bit for bit to a float64 reference (rope_scaling.hpp:24-26, 122-123). Without the flag Apple clang 21 fuses YaRN's blend and mscale (4 fused multiply-adds), and at 1M 2 of the 67,134,464 floats of the yarn x2 table differ from the reference (sin at position 589,449 pair 19 and at 910,519 pair 17); at `--max-context` 262,144 and 524,544 none do, which is why ctest runs the 1M allocation. With the flag all seven scaled configurations match.

`generate.cpp.o` keeps an out-of-line `RopeScaling::mscale()` with a fused multiply-add. Compiled with `-fno-inline` as a stand-in for a compiler that stops inlining it, the builder without `flatten` calls `mscale()`, and a strata link binds that call to generate.cpp.o's copy; the flattened builder makes no such call. Today's build inlines it either way, and the flattened build gives the same eight tables (hashes in the first comment). ctest cannot see a lost `flatten`, since the test does not link generate.cpp.o; the CMake comment gives an `nm` check, for the default Release build. With only mscale fused, the 1M yarn table would change at 1 of the 252 factors from 1.25 to 64 in steps of 0.25 (36.25, in 1 float).

Inferred from the build files, not checked on a PC: rope.cu gets no `-march`, `-mfma` or `/arch:` (CMakeLists.txt:354, 1219-1225, 1326-1352), so a PC whose host compiler targets baseline x86-64 rounds it the same way. A host compiler that can fuse by default (an ARM64 Linux host, or `-march=native` in the flags) may not.

## On-model results
Apple M5 Max (128 GB, macOS 27.0.1), 2026-10-16; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-abliterated-IQ3_S (revision eec4e10a, hashes in the first comment), greedy, thinking off; main is 296b59d's Metal build. B0-B2 and B6 ran resident at `--max-context 65536`, except B2's two streaming runs; B3-B5 streamed with `--kv int8`. Desktop programs stayed open (30-42 GB in use beside the engine), so every streaming start ran with its cap lowered by `STRATA_METAL_LEAVE_SHARE` (recorded per run) and with the model's pages dropped from the file cache first; the first comment says why and has every table.
- **B1, the default path (no flag): main against this branch.** One-token decode windows, 86 requests: tokens, DONE fields and draft counts identical, 86 of 86 first-window logit files and 191 of 191 `STRATA_METAL_LOGPOS` rows byte-identical. Setup's default config, 6 requests (decided: the control, this branch run twice, was identical): tokens and DONE fields identical, 6 of 6 logit files byte-identical.
- **B2 on main (#2767):** yarn x4 (`--rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 4 --yarn-orig-ctx 262144`) against no flag gives the same results in every comparison of B1, while the log says `rope scaling yarn, factor 4`.
- **B2 on this branch:** yarn x4 changes all 6 first-window rows of the default config and the logits at all 65 decode-window positions (mean KL 0.0152, top-1 agreement 0.923), and after all 20 prompts in the resident (mean KL 0.0276) and the streaming runs (0.0343). The prompt-path gate is undecided for both paths: the resident prompt chain n 0.0105, e 0.0318, d 0.0084, T 0.0183; the streaming prompt GEMM n 0.0070, e 0.0318, d 0.0101, T 0.0149. d is under T on the means, but T did not separate every prompt's n and e.
- **B6, needles at 8K, 16K and 32K:** 9 of 9 on main, on this branch without a flag (twice: the control was identical) and with yarn x4; main against this branch identical.
- **B3 and B3M, memory (streaming):** the engine holds 18.00, 25.62 and 41.08 GB before its arena at 262,144, 524,544 and 1,048,832 cells, with prompt buffers of 5.19, 6.26 and 8.41 GB; the least a 1M start can hold, computed with the smallest arena the harness accepts, is 58.5 GB, 24.0 GB under the engine's cap of 82.5 GB. `--kv int8` against fp16 at 32K: identical tokens and byte-identical logits, as #2707 reads the code (`qsa_prep` stores K and V as int8 whatever `--kv` says).
- **B4, 512K** (probe.py's three-code prompt, 524,288 tokens, the PC run's input by SHA-256): without scaling 3 of 3, prefill 752 tok/s (697 s), decode 22.1 tok/s; yarn x2 3 of 3, 657 tok/s (799 s), 21.6 tok/s. The cap was lowered to 55.9 GB (a 29.7 GB arena), so prompts read experts again more often than with the engine's own arena.
- **B5, 1M** (probe.py's three-code prompt, 1,048,576 tokens, the PC run's input by SHA-256; `STRATA_WATCHDOG_S=300`, the harness's setting when the arena is smaller than B4's): without scaling 1 of 3 (`CEDAR-482|MARBLE-956|QUARTZ-956`), prefill 589 tok/s (1,781 s), decode 20.0 tok/s; yarn x4 3 of 3, 580 tok/s (1,807 s), 18.0 tok/s. The cap was lowered to 54.6 GB (a 13.0 GB arena). The PC run in bench/results/2026-10-09-rope-yarn-long-context (README.md:146-148; RTX PRO 6000, IQ3_XXS, engine 0.1.41) found 0 of 3 and 3 of 3.

## Extra Notes
- **Newly honoured settings.** `--rope-freq-base` and a model file's `rope.scaling.*` keys now take effect on Metal, and `--rope-freq-scale` and the `--yarn-*` knobs do under linear or yarn, as on the PC (generate.cpp:2941-2944, 2957-2990); before, Metal ignored them. None of the six files Mac setup offers has `rope.scaling.*` keys.
- **Session files.** By the code, none can bring the old rotation into this build. On a Mac at 296b59d no SAVE or RESTORE gets past the RAM check, as the engine says when it starts (`memory guard: the available RAM cannot be read; parking and session save/restore are refused`, generate.cpp:2327-2331; conversation_memory.cpp:280-292; conversation_file.cpp:1153, 1216-1222). With #2503's macOS reading (its diff, read) a RESTORE still fails while the file is parsed: the window writes 4 indexer tail rows a QSA layer (window.cpp:1384-1397) where the read limit allows 3 (conversation_state.cpp:117-122, 338; conversation_file.cpp:733, 760-761).
- **The spare key is left as it is.** Metal's spare indexer key is normalized but not rotated (qsa.metal:109-111); CUDA's is multiplied by row 0 of the table (qsa.cu:189-199), so under YaRN Metal's lacks mscale. By the code that cannot change which cells are attended (first comment). Parity with CUDA can be a follow-up that touches qsa.metal.
- **Memory.** For a resident pack, nothing in the engine compares the weights plus a long context's buffers against a cap (arena_budget.h:137-141; stream.cpp:34-40, 47; first comment). No start in these tests was resident above setup's 65,536 cells; B3 and B3M measured what a streaming engine plans at 262,144, 524,544 and 1,048,832 cells.
- **Not checked here.** Images (M-RoPE) under YaRN. B4 and B5 ran the streaming prompt GEMM and the decode windows past 262K; the resident prompt chain and the draft layer were not run past 65,536 cells, and their index arithmetic there is read, not run (first comment).

title: bench: community report — 2x RTX 3060 12 GB, Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS, 131K context, agent-calibrated (engine 0.1.44.1)
body:
Community speed report from a dedicated 2x RTX 3060 machine: the UD-IQ4_XS pack at the full 131,072-token window, the engine at a `--layer-split auto` split across both cards, with the expert pool tiered in 94 GiB of system RAM.

Adds `bench/results/2026-10-16-community-2x-rtx-3060-ud-iq4-xs-0.1.44.1/` (`README.md` + `results.json`), produced by `tools/strata_bench.py` suite 1 against the running server.

## Machine

- MEG Z490 ACE, i7-11700 (8C/16T), 94.2 GiB RAM; Linux, driver 595.99.02, CUDA 13.2
- 2x RTX 3060 12 GB, both CPU-direct at Gen4 x8 (the CPU's 20 lanes split x8/x8, the NVMe takes the last x4); power limit 170 W per card — decode plateaus near 90 W, only prefill bursts reach the limit
- Strata 0.1.44.1 (commit 296b59d2, release build); `layer split auto`: layers 0-21 on GPU 0, layers 22-47 plus a 2939-slot (6.62 GiB) expert cache on GPU 1
- Calibrated with `./setup.sh --calibrate`: `--pcie-frac 0.20 --spec-min-p 0.70 --adapt-every 1 --adapt-swaps 80 --adapt-decay 0.97`; `STRATA_STAGE_TRIM=1 STRATA_IO_PREFETCH=1`

## Headline medians

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| short chat decode | 45.2 tok/s (TTFT 0.62 s) |
| agent follow-up turns decode | 52.1 tok/s |
| fresh prompt 4K / 16K | 799 / 1216 tok/s |
| agent turn TTFT | 5.22 s |
| conversation cache hit | 68.6 % |

## Notes

- Reproducibility: two independent suites on the same running server a few hours apart; every headline median agrees within 3 % (the README records the earlier run).
- Read alongside #2608 (same GPU pair, IQ3_S at 65K): the smaller quant decodes slightly faster on short chats there, while this report has 131K context and ~28 % faster 16K prefill — complementary points for the 3060 pair.
- Speed only: no recall/HumanEval run, no concurrency row; labelled as such in the README.

- [x] README read once before sharing; scrubber output checked (no host names, paths, or addresses)
- [x] report added under `bench/results/` in the `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md` format
- [x] engine version, hardware, power limits and settings recorded in the README

title: sycl: setup --vision cpu reads images on the Intel port (the CPU encoder, as on AMD)
body:
## Title
sycl: setup --vision cpu reads images on the Intel port (the CPU encoder, as on AMD)

Issue: Resolves #2816

## Summary

Images on the Intel (SYCL) port, the way the AMD (HIP) path has them since #304: the image encoder built for the
CPU by setup, the engine started with `--vision`. docs/INTEL.md's comparison table said "not yet" for images on
the SYCL port, but the engine side has been there since the port (`--vision`, the GENI request with the encoder's
embeddings, the per-cell M-RoPE position table in `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`); what was missing was the setup
wiring. `sycl/setup_intel.py` forced `--vision none`, mapped every `--vision` to "none" and dropped the config's
`"vision"` section. The encoder itself (`tools/vision`, llama.cpp's mtmd + the mmproj file) needs no SYCL: the
CPU build the AMD path uses runs on the PC, outside the container, and `serve/server.py` hands the engine the
embeddings.

With this change `./setup.sh --backend sycl --vision cpu` compiles the encoder for the CPU into `engine-sycl/`
(setup's own `build_vision_cpu`: `tools/vision` against the pinned llama.cpp, `-DSTRATA_VISION_CUDA=OFF
-DSTRATA_PORTABLE=OFF`, once, again when `tools/vision` changes), downloads the mmproj file as setup does, keeps
the config's `"vision"` section (`exe`, `mmproj`, `model`, `threads`: host paths, since the encoder runs on the
host) and `--vision`, and applies the port's own VRAM reserve rule (1,024 MiB up to 32K, ...) instead of the
700 MiB setup writes for the CUDA engine's GPU encoder: the CPU encoder takes no VRAM. A `--vram-reserve-mib`
the user gives is kept. `--vision yes` / `gpu` leave images off with a note saying to use `--vision cpu`, as
`hip_vision` does on AMD (there is no SYCL encoder build). Without `--vision cpu` nothing changes: the
throw-away engine folder and the config are as before.

Measured, 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB (kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4, oneAPI 2026.1, AOT bmg-g31),
AMD Threadripper 1950X, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, `--layer-split 30 --kv int8 --spec 4 --mtp
<BF16 draft layer> --mtp-max-t 4`, the encoder from `tools/vision` built with gcc 13 (native,
`-DSTRATA_PORTABLE=OFF`), `mmproj-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-BF16.gguf`, 8 threads:

- the encoder alone: a 256x256 PNG -> 64 image tokens (an 8x8 grid, 2,560 values each), 1,191 ms on 8 CPU
  threads, no VRAM.
- a 448x448 image of four coloured quadrants, "name the colour of each quadrant", through
  `/v1/chat/completions` on a development tree with the same `serve/` and vision path as `main`: all four
  named correctly ("Top-left: red, top-right: green, bottom-left: blue, bottom-right: yellow"; 280 prompt
  tokens, 4.8 s to the first token including the encode), also while a code request ran on the other slot; a
  512-token text reply decoded at 140.9 and 140.5 tok/s with `--vision` (about the 141 measured without it) on that tree.
- on `main` 296b59d2 (upstream's own engine build, this branch's config: the vision section and `--vision`):
  the four colours right ("Red, Green, Blue, Yellow" to "in the order top-left, top-right, bottom-left,
  bottom-right"), 246 prompt tokens with the picture read in 1.48 s including the encode; a 512-token greedy
  text reply at 81.7 / 79.4 tok/s with `--vision` against 81.8 / 79.4 without (an earlier run of the same binary
  and config), with identical text and draft counts: `--vision` changes nothing for text.
- `python -m unittest tools.test_setup_sycl`: 24 tests pass (6 new). Every `tools/test_setup_*.py` module run
  with and without this change gives the same result (the same 10 pre-existing failures on `main`: the
  `test_setup_golden` UD-Q4_K_XL cases and two `test_setup_engine_hash` cases; none in the SYCL, AMD, config or
  bench-tip modules).

## What changed

- `sycl/setup_intel.py`:
  - `sycl_vision(asked)` replaces `S.hip_vision` (was `lambda asked: "none"`): `cpu` -> `cpu`; `yes` / `gpu` ->
    `none` with a warning that says `--vision cpu`; anything else `none`.
  - `build_engine_sycl(gpu, llama, vision)` replaces `S.build_engine_hip` (was the stub): with `vision == "none"`
    it returns the same throw-away stub as before (`engine_stub()`, the code moved out of `install()`); with
    `cpu` it stops with the package to install when the PC has no C++ compiler, and otherwise calls setup's
    `build_vision_cpu(eng, stamp, meta, llama, vsrc)` with `eng = engine-sycl/` (new folder next to the
    checkout's `engine/`, which the SYCL setup never used): that compiles `tools/vision` into `build-vision/`,
    copies `strata-vision` beside the stamp and records `vision: cpu` and the `tools/vision` source hash in
    `engine-sycl/BUILD.json`, so a rerun compiles nothing. `build_vision_cpu` is added to the names
    `install()` checks setup.py still has.
  - `to_sycl`: the `"vision"` key is no longer dropped from the config; `--vision` was already passed through.
    The reserve: when `--vision` is in the args and the reserve is setup's vision default (`VISION["cpu"]
    ["reserve_mib"]`, 700) it is treated as not given, which is what setup's own `choices_from_config` does
    with that value (#493), so the port's rule applies.
  - `say_intel` rewrites `build_vision_cpu`'s "engine: engine-sycl/strata, image encoder (CPU): ..." line to
    "image encoder (CPU): ..." (there is no engine in that folder).
  - `install()` still appends `--vision none` when `--vision` is not given: images stay opt-in.
- `tools/test_setup_sycl.py`: `ToSycl.test_the_vision_section_is_kept_and_the_cpu_encoder_takes_no_reserve`
  and a new `Images` class (the vision choice; no images -> the stub and no `cmake_build` call; `cpu` -> one
  `cmake_build` of `tools/vision` with the AMD path's definitions, the copied encoder, the stamp, no second
  build on a rerun, a build again when `tools/vision` changes; no compiler -> a stop naming `build-essential`;
  the source still forces `--vision none` when not asked). No GPU, no network, no compiler: `cmake_build` is
  replaced.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: the comparison table's images row, an "Images" bullet in the setup section, the "Images: the
  encoder on the CPU" section with the measurements above, and the "Not done" entry narrowed to the llama.cpp
  configuration.

Not changed: `setup.py` (`git diff main -- setup.py` is empty; the CUDA and HIP paths run the same code), the
engine (`sycl/src`, `src`, `include`: no compiled file is touched, the binary is `main`'s), `serve/`,
`sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh`, `tools/vision`. A SYCL build of the encoder (GPU encode) is not part of this: the CPU
encoder is what runs on AMD too.

## Extra Notes

- The encoder runs on the host, not in the `strata-sycl-dev` container, so the PC needs a C++ compiler
  (`build-essential`); setup's pip-installed cmake and ninja do the rest. A PC without one gets a message with
  the package and the `--vision no` way out. The measured encoder above was built with the dev image's gcc 13
  and run inside the same image (our serving setup keeps the server in the container); the setup path builds it
  with the host's compiler - the same CMake definitions.
- Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code): the code, the measurements and this text were produced by Claude on the submitter's two Arc Pro B70s, at the submitter's request.

title: strata-q36 on Volta: K-quant prompt experts on a register-fragment tensor-core kernel - prompt +22-25% on a V100, same tokens
body:
On a Volta GPU, strata-q36's prompt-path MoE experts in Q4_K / Q5_K / Q6_K now use a new FP16 tensor-core kernel (`moe_tc_kq`) instead of MMQ's dp4a path. This covers the gate/up and down products of a prompt chunk.

**How it works**
- A block handles 64 routed rows against 128 weight rows, with 8 warps.
- In each warp, the four `mma.m8n8k4` quad pairs each take a 32-value chunk of a 128-value k step.
- Each lane decodes its row's 32 values straight into A fragments in registers, with the same arithmetic as ggml's `dequantize_row_q*_K`. Weights are never staged in shared memory.
- The q8_1 activations MMQ already produces (DS4 for Q4_K/Q5_K, D4 for Q6_K) are staged as FP16 in shared memory, double-buffered, with the next step's loads in flight under the current step's products.
- The four chunks' partial sums are added with shuffles. Accumulation is FP32.

**Scope**
- Used only when the device is sm_70. Turing and newer already run MMQ on int8 tensor cores.
- `STRATA_PREFILL_TCKQ=0` keeps MMQ.
- The source is compiled only when `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` includes 70 (or `native`/`all`). It is about 140 KB of device code, so default builds (`120`) are unchanged. Outside that build the header's inline no-ops leave the call site free of `#ifdef`s.

**Measured** on one Tesla V100 PCIe 32 GB with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP-UD-Q4_K_M. The build is this branch on main 296b59d2 with `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=70 -DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON`. Each run is `strata-q36 --bench-pp` (`--max-context 131072`), plus a 16K-token greedy generation compared by md5. Two cooled rounds, alternating the two settings:

| | `STRATA_PREFILL_TCKQ=0` (MMQ) | default (this kernel) |
|---|---:|---:|
| pp512 | 1,685.9 / 1,684.4 | **2,109.0 / 2,109.3** (+25%) |
| pp16384 | 1,518.8 / 1,518.3 | **1,854.6 / 1,854.2** (+22%) |
| MTP2 pp512 | 1,640.5 / 1,640.6 | 2,057.1 / 2,056.4 |
| tg256 | 100.6 / 100.3 | 99.7 / 100.8 |
| 16K greedy, tokens md5 | 75a302c75b7c | 75a302c75b7c (identical) |

The products use FP16 operands with FP32 sums, so they are not bit-identical to MMQ. The 16K greedy tokens came out identical in all four runs. The same kernel design in a Maya-based engine also matched llama.cpp's greedy output for 128 of 128 tokens on this model.

title: sycl: STRATA_GR_FUSED=1, the two-kernel BF16 hyper-connection read (opt-in)
body:
## Title
sycl: STRATA_GR_FUSED=1, the two-kernel BF16 hyper-connection read (opt-in)

Issue: Resolves #2811
Depends on #2810 (sycl: STRATA_HC_Q8=1 reads the Q8_0 hyper-connection projections) - this branch is that one
plus one commit and reuses its argument struct, scratch and helpers; merge that PR first.

## Summary

An opt-in hyper-connection read for the SYCL (Intel) build, `STRATA_GR_FUSED=1`: the norm, the down projection and
its partial reduction in one kernel, the up projection in a second, instead of the port's default four launches per
layer half (norm, sliced down, reduce, up). Same BF16 weights, no extra VRAM, the default read's per-element
arithmetic, another summation order. Default off: with the flag unset the default read runs unchanged (outputs and
draft counts identical to `main`, checked). It is the structure of the Q8_0 read of the PR it builds on, applied to
the BF16 weights, for the cases that keep BF16: an exact-weights read is wanted, or the Q8_0 copies' extra VRAM is
not. With `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` set the Q8_0 read runs and this flag changes nothing.

Not bitwise the default read (another summation order: lo / rs / mixed differ at FP32 rounding level, like upstream's
opt-in `STRATA_GR_V3`; greedy output changes after a near-tie). Bitwise: the default path; R_out (the pending write)
between the two reads; a captured graph's replays against the direct call; the fixed-stride fallback.

Measured, 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB (kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4, oneAPI 2026.1, AOT bmg-g31),
upstream main 296b59d2 vs this branch with the flag, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, `--layer-split 30
--prefill 8192 --kv int8 --spec 4 --mtp <BF16 draft layer> --mtp-max-t 4 --spec-min-p 0 --stream-experts
--expert-cache auto --max-context 65536`, one slot, greedy, a fixed prompt with a 512-token coding reply, 3 runs:

- verify window 39.4 / 39.5 / 39.7 -> 38.8 / 38.1 / 38.7 ms (-2.5%; independent of draft acceptance - the effect of
  the read);
- decode 81.8 / 79.5 / 78.7 -> 86.8 / 79.0 / 88.3 tok/s; the spread is mostly a different draft acceptance of the
  changed output (drafts accepted 360/462, 342/510, 362/456), so the per-window number is the one to read;
- a turn at a 40,796-token context 76.0 -> 79.4 tok/s (output differs); prompt reading unchanged (4K 993 -> 986 tok/s);
- kernel level (one card, graph replay, random weights not L2-resident, us per read, default -> two-kernel): T = 1
  38.7 -> 34.8 (-10%), T = 4 50.8 -> 41.5 (-18%), T = 6 62.0 -> 47.1 (-24%);
- `gr_fused_parity --selftest`: 33 of 33 cases pass. Coherence and per-card health after every run: pass.

## What changed

- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.dp.cpp`: `namespace gr_fused`: `gr_fused_down_kernel` (a work-group = 32 rows,
  2 per lane, x a 1,280-column slab = half a stream; stages `R' * w_norm` unscaled for the T rows with the slab's
  sums of squares, each lane's 2 rows' BF16 chunks over its sub-group's 80 columns, the 16 sub-group partials added in
  a fixed order; the LAST work-group of a row group to arrive applies rs per stream, writes lo / the injection and rs,
  resets the counter), `gr_fused_up_kernel` (16 columns x 4 streams = 64 rows per work-group, K = 320 in 4 quarters
  over the sub-groups summed in a fixed order, then the default read's epilogue: pending write, gate, stream mean),
  the launchers, `on()` (the env, or `fused_gr_set_fused`'s override), `read()`. The hook in `fused_gr_read_multi`,
  right after the Q8_0 one: `if (gr_fused::on() && gr_fused::read(m, st)) return false;`. Arguments not at the
  callers' fixed strides fall back to the default read with one line on stderr. `fused_gr_set_fused(int)`: 1 / 0 /
  -1 (= the env), for the parity test.
- `sycl/include/strata/kernels/fused_gr_fused.hpp` (new, the port's include tree): declares `fused_gr_set_fused`.
- `sycl/src/kernels/gr_fused_parity.cpp` (new) + `sycl/CMakeLists.txt` (one name in the `--selftest` loop): real
  geometry, T = 1..8 x pending write on / off x inject rows on / off; both reads against an FP64 reference (within
  1e-4 of the largest value) and against each other (within 1e-4; the differences printed), R_out bitwise, a captured
  graph replayed twice bitwise the direct call, the fixed-stride fallback bitwise the default read.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: a section: what it does, what is and is not bitwise, the numbers, the shapes tried.

Not changed: anything under `src/` or `include/`; the default SYCL read (flag unset: the new code is never entered);
the Q8_0 read of the PR below it (this PR adds a sibling namespace and one hook line after its hook).

## Extra Notes

- The name: `STRATA_GR_*` is the port's prefix for its hyper-connection read switches (`STRATA_GR_DOWN_SLICED`,
  `STRATA_GR_NORM_SPLIT`, `STRATA_GR_UP_COLS`, ...).
- The down kernel's shape (rows per lane x columns per sub-group) at T = 6 in a development tree with the same
  kernels: (1, 80) 30.6, (2, 40) 26.9, (1, 40) 30.2, (2, 80) 23.6 us - (2, 80) is built. The kernel-level numbers above
  come from the same probe; everything else was measured on this branch against `main`.
- Built: the SYCL engine and `gr_fused_parity` (oneAPI 2026.1, AOT bmg-g31). CUDA and HIP are not touched.
- Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code): the code, the measurements and this text were produced by Claude on the

title: sycl: STRATA_HC_Q8=1 reads the Q8_0 hyper-connection projections (it loaded them and never read them)
body:
## Title
sycl: STRATA_HC_Q8=1 reads the Q8_0 hyper-connection projections (it loaded them and never read them)

Issue: Resolves #2809

## Summary

On the SYCL (Intel) build `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` did nothing. The loader kept a Q8_0 copy of the hyper-connection
projections only when the GGUF stored them as Q8_0 (the ISTA files store BF16, so it copied nothing), and the
port's `fused_gr_read_multi` had no Q8_0 read: it ignored `q8_down` / `q8_up` and read the BF16 copies whatever the
flag said (`fused_gr.dp.cpp`: "the Q8_0 reads (S23 STRATA_HC_Q8) are not built"). For a GGUF that stores them as
Q8_0 the copies were made and never read. (From the source; on a development tree with the loader half fixed, a GPU
trace showed the same BF16 kernels with the flag on and off.)

With this change the flag does on SYCL what it does on CUDA: the hyper-connection down / up projections (the layers'
and the final mixer's) are read as Q8_0 in the verify window - the GGUF's own Q8_0 blocks, or Q8_0 of its BF16 values
quantized at load. Flag unset: nothing changes (the pointers stay null and the BF16 read runs as before; outputs and
draft counts identical to `main`, checked).

As on CUDA (`fused_gr.cu`, "an output-changing step") the Q8_0 read is NOT bitwise the BF16 read: Q8_0-rounded
weights, another summation order. Bitwise: the default path; R_out (the pending write) between the two reads; a
captured graph's replays against the direct call; the fallback for arguments not at the callers' fixed strides.

VRAM, said plainly: on this port the BF16 copies stay in the arena (the prompt path's GEMMs read them), so the flag
ADDS 0.63 GiB for Flash-Next (0.40 + 0.24 GiB over a two-card layer split) instead of replacing the BF16 bytes as on a
single CUDA GPU. That is cache the experts lose: on 2x B70 the model that ran at `--max-context 65536` without the
flag refused 310 experts with it (132 at 32768 with the default 1,024 MiB reserve); the A/B below ran at 32768 with
`--vram-reserve-mib 512`. Dropping the BF16 copies (`add_hc_skip` / `hc_bf16_view`) is not ported here.

Measured, 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB (kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4, oneAPI 2026.1, AOT bmg-g31),
upstream main 296b59d2 vs this branch, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS (BF16 hyper-connection tensors),
`--layer-split 30 --prefill 8192 --kv int8 --spec 4 --mtp <BF16 draft layer> --mtp-max-t 4 --spec-min-p 0
--stream-experts --expert-cache auto --max-context 32768 --vram-reserve-mib 512`, one slot, greedy, a fixed prompt
with a 512-token coding reply, 3 runs, same binary, flag unset vs set:

- verify window 39.4 / 39.6 / 39.8 -> 37.4 / 37.5 / 37.4 ms (-5.3%; independent of draft acceptance);
- decode 81.8 / 79.4 / 78.5 -> 85.0 / 88.0 / 86.0 tok/s (median 79.4 -> 86.0, +8.3%; part of it is a different draft
  acceptance of the changed output: drafts accepted 353/474, 349/489, 348/492 -> 351/489, 357/471, 353/483);
- prompt reading unchanged: 4K 1,093 / 1,190 -> 1,093 / 1,188 tok/s, 16K 1,774 / 1,749 -> 1,769 / 1,750;
- quality: teacher-forced NLL of 4,762 tokens of three texts through the decode windows, same targets: 3.1974 unset,
  3.1699 set. No degradation measured on this gate; not claimed as an improvement (rounding-only variants move this
  kind of gate by 0.01-0.1 nats per token).
- kernel level (one card, graph replay, random weights not L2-resident, us per read, BF16 -> Q8_0): T = 1 38.7 ->
  24.7, T = 4 50.8 -> 29.3, T = 6 62.0 -> 34.4.
- `gr_q8_parity --selftest`: 33 of 33 cases pass. Coherence and per-card health after every run: pass.

## What changed

- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.dp.cpp`: the Q8_0 read (`namespace gr_q8`), two kernels, one row per 16-lane
  sub-group lane. The down kernel stages a 512-column slab of `R' * w_norm` (unscaled) for the T rows with the slab's
  sums of squares; each lane holds 4 rows' quants and scales over its sub-group's 32 columns; the 16 sub-groups add
  their partials in local memory in a fixed order; the LAST work-group of a row group to arrive (an atomic counter,
  no waiting, so nothing assumes co-residency and it is safe inside a SYCL graph) applies rs per stream, writes lo /
  the injection and rs, and resets the counter. The up kernel splits each row's K = 320 over five sub-groups, sums
  the fifths in a fixed order, and runs the default read's epilogue (pending write, gate, stream mean). `w = d * q` is
  exact in FP32. The inject rows are read from the pack's BF16, as the CUDA read's default. One guarded line in
  `fused_gr_read_multi`, first thing after the queue is known: `if (a[0].q8_down && a[0].q8_up && gr_q8::read(m,
  st)) return false;` - null pointers (the default) skip it. Arguments whose rows are not at the fixed strides every
  caller uses (verify, mtp, the final mixer) fall back to the BF16 read with one line on stderr. The scratch
  (partials, sums of squares, counters) is one per queue, allocated and zeroed outside any capture.
  `fused_gr_q8_0_split_host`: the read's weight layout - every row's int8 quants row-major, then every row's fp16
  scales; the same bytes as ggml's 34-byte blocks, reordered.
- `sycl/include/strata/kernels/fused_gr_q8.hpp` (new, the port's own include tree): declares that layout function
  for the loader and the parity test.
- `sycl/src/core/native_dense.cpp`: with `STRATA_HC_Q8=1`, hyper-connection tensors of GGUF type 8 (Q8_0, as they
  are) AND type 30 (BF16: quantized on the host with the file's existing `q8_0_of`, ggml's rounding `d = amax / 127`
  as fp16, `q = round(x / d)`) are uploaded in the split layout. Shape-checked against the compiled geometry (hc_lr x
  hc * n_embd or the transpose); another stage's layers are skipped in a layer split (`outside` / `in_range`, as the
  main upload loop does). The inject rows are no longer copied: nothing read them before and the read takes the BF16
  rows, so `STRATA_HC_Q8_INJECT` has no effect on SYCL (said in the comment).
- `sycl/src/kernels/gr_q8_parity.cpp` (new) + `sycl/CMakeLists.txt` (one name in the `--selftest` loop): real
  geometry, T = 1..8 x pending write on / off x inject rows on / off. The Q8_0 read against an FP64 reference computed
  from the very Q8_0 bytes it reads (lo / rs / inject / mixed within 1e-4 of the largest value - FP32 summation
  order), R_out bitwise the BF16 read's, a captured graph replayed twice bitwise the direct call, the Q8_0 read's
  `mixed` different from the BF16 read's by the weights' rounding (proves the Q8_0 bytes are read - the bug), and
  the fixed-stride fallback bitwise the BF16 read.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: a section on the flag: what was wrong, what it does now, what is and is not bitwise, the VRAM
  cost, the numbers.

Not changed: anything under `src/` or `include/` (CUDA / HIP untouched); the default SYCL read and every other path
(flag unset: the new code is never entered); `STRATA_HC_Q8`'s meaning on CUDA / HIP / Mac; `STRATA_GR_V3`,
`STRATA_HC_SPLIT` and the port's other hyper-connection switches.

## Extra Notes

- Built: the SYCL engine and `gr_q8_parity` (oneAPI 2026.1, AOT bmg-g31). CUDA and HIP are not touched by any file
  of this PR (only `sycl/**` and `docs/INTEL.md`).
- The kernel-level numbers come from a probe in a development tree with the same two kernels (graph replay, random
  BF16 weights and their Q8_0, 8 weight sets, 48 reads per graph); everything else above was measured on this
  branch against `main`.
- Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code): the code, the measurements and this text were produced by Claude on the
  submitter's two Arc Pro B70s, at the submitter's request.

title: sycl: prompt attention over 8-query selection unions on XMX (opt-in STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_UNION=1)
body:
## Title
sycl: prompt attention over 8-query selection unions on XMX (opt-in `STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_UNION=1`)

Issue: Resolves #2807

## Summary

On the SYCL port the QSA prompt attention runs the FP32 decode kernel, 32 positions per launch, and every position
gathers its own ~2,051 selected K/V cells. The XMX port (`STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_XMX=1`) is slower than that, and
docs/INTEL.md left a kernel over the union of neighbouring positions' selections "not built".

This PR adds that kernel, opt-in. For every 8 neighbouring positions a first kernel builds the sorted union of their
selected cells, each cell marked with the positions that chose it. The attention kernel dequantizes the INT8 K/V of
64-cell chunks of that union once to FP16 and runs S^T = K Q^T and O += P V on joint_matrix (8x16x16, FP32 sums) for
all 96 rows (8 positions x 12 heads). In the online softmax a cell is -inf for the positions that did not select it,
so every position attends to exactly the cells it attends to with the FP32 kernel.

- Off by default. With the switch unset the outputs and draft counts are identical to upstream main's (both decode
  runs and a turn with 40,796 tokens of context); the only new code on that path is the switch, read once.
- INT8 KV on a Battlemage card. Any other KV format or card, or a failed scratch allocation, keeps the existing path
  (one stderr line says why).
- Not bitwise with the switch set: Q, K, V and the probabilities enter the products as FP16.

Measured 2026-10-16 on 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 (32 GB, `xe`, kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4, oneAPI 2026.1,
AOT `bmg-g31`), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, `--layer-split 30 --prefill 8192 --max-context 65536 --kv int8
--spec 4 --mtp <BF16 draft layer> --mtp-max-t 4 --spec-min-p 0 --stream-experts --expert-cache auto`, one slot,
greedy, fixed prompts; upstream main 296b59d2 against this branch:

| | upstream main | `STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_UNION=1` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| prompt, 4K tokens (two fresh prompts) | 993 / 1,189 tok/s | 1,127 / 1,382 tok/s |
| prompt, 32K tokens (two fresh prompts) | 2,004 / 1,956 tok/s | 2,314 / 2,246 tok/s |
| first token of a turn with 40,796 tokens of context | 23.28 s | 20.39 s |
| decode, 512 tokens (3 runs) | 78.7-81.8 tok/s | 79.1-82.9 tok/s |
| one verify window (3 runs) | 39.4-39.7 ms | 39.3-40.0 ms |

Decode is not touched. With the switch set the outputs differ (rounding), so decode tok/s moves with the draft
acceptance while the verify window takes the same time.

Accuracy:

- `qsa_prompt_attn_union_parity --selftest` (one card, random INT8 pools behind a shuffled page table, the prompt
  path's selection layout and cap of 2,051; 1.5K-40K contexts, ragged last groups, pages that are not resident, a
  bitwise rerun): 5 of 5 pass. Error against FP64 2.6e-3 - 5.0e-3 at an output scale of 3.3-3.6 (FP32 kernel 1.7e-6 -
  2.6e-6); union against FP32 on average 7e-5 of the scale.
- Teacher-forced NLL (`STRATA_LOGPOS`; 8 chats, each an ~8,400-token context read by the prompt path and a 1,617-token
  follow-up scored through the decode windows; 12,737 tokens, the same targets in every arm):

| arm | mean NLL | top-1 same as switch unset |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| switch unset | 2.6234 | - |
| `STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_UNION=1` | 2.5506 | 93.2% |
| control: switch unset, `--prefill 4096` (changes only rounding) | 2.6321 | 94.1% |

  The 0.073 lower NLL is not a measured improvement: single chats move by up to 0.2 nats/token in the control as well
  (the spread over the 8 chats is 0.12 nats/token in both arms), so 8 chats do not resolve a difference of this size
  (95% bootstrap interval of the NLL change over the chats: -0.160 to +0.015 for the switch, -0.072 to +0.092 for
  the control).

## What changed

- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/qsa_prompt_attn_union.dp.cpp` (new): the union kernel (one work-group per 8 positions,
  16K-cell local bitmaps), the attention kernel (one work-group per 8 positions and KV head, 12 sub-groups of 16,
  256 GRF), the launcher (256 groups per launch pair) and its scratch, one per queue.
- `sycl/include/strata/kernels/qsa_prompt_attn_union.hpp` (new): the entry point (the contract of
  `qsa_prompt_attn_batch`) and the switch.
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/qsa_prompt_attn.dp.cpp`: the include and the guarded call before the XMX v2 call (4 lines).
- `sycl/src/kernels/qsa_prompt_attn_union_parity.cpp` (new): the parity test (`--selftest` in ctest, skip code 77
  off Battlemage); `<context> <queries> [reps] [--drift F] [--sel <STRATA_DUMP_SEL file>]` times one chunk.
- `sycl/CMakeLists.txt`: the new source in `strata_kernels`, the parity target and its test.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: an entry after "XMX v2 in the full matrix, and why a grouped kernel is not next".

Left alone: the selection (block scores, top-k), decode, the FP32 and XMX v2 prompt kernels, the other KV formats,
and every file outside `sycl/` and `docs/` (CUDA, HIP and Metal builds see no change).

## Extra Notes

- Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code): the code, the measurements and this text were produced by Claude on the submitter's two Arc Pro B70s, at the submitter's request.
- `--max-context 65536` because at 200,000 not every expert fits on a plain two-card layer split of upstream main.
- The kernel pays only when neighbouring selections overlap. One chunk of 8,192 positions at 24K-32K context: the FP32
  kernel 137-152 ms, the union kernel 38.7 / 82.3 / 146.6 ms when the union of 8 selections is 1.15x / 2.67x / 5.22x
  one position's cells (docs/INTEL.md measured 3.3x on an 80K prompt). With independent selections it is no faster
  (512 positions at 32K, union 5.3x: 12.4 vs 11.0 ms).
- About 80 MB of device memory per card that reads a prompt, allocated at the first prompt (it comes out of the
  `--vram-reserve-mib` headroom).
- A cell is stored as an int32 with its 8-position mask in a separate byte, so any `--max-context` the engine accepts
  works.
- Not included: an earlier version of the kernel (S = Q K^T, 32-cell chunks; the same error, 15-20% slower per chunk)
  and a knob for the groups per launch.
- Not tested: the JIT build, other Xe2 parts (refused by the device check), `--kv-resident` (non-resident pages are
  masked as in the FP32 kernel; the parity test covers that case).

title: sycl: decode QSA selection and attention in fewer, shorter launches (opt-in, bitwise)
body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #2805

## Summary

On an Arc Pro B70 the QSA selection (block scores, top-k) and attention of a decode window are small, latency-bound
launches. This adds four opt-in switches that do the same arithmetic in fewer launches or with less serial work. Each
gives exactly the bits of the path it replaces. All are off by default, and each is a branch in front of the existing
code that tests its flag first, so the default path is unchanged.

| switch | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `STRATA_BATCH_QSA_ATTN=1` | A batch window (`--batch`) ran the scores, top-k and attention one row at a time, because each slot has its own K/V. Now the scores run once per slot, the top-k once per window, and the attention once per window over every slot's pools. |
| `STRATA_QSA_TOPK_SCAN=1` | The wide top-k kernel (a capacity above ~135K cells) found each radix pass's digit with one thread walking 256 bins. Now it is a work-group scan. Integers only: the same ids. |
| `STRATA_QSA_SCORES_TRANSPOSED=1` | The decode block scores reduce a block's (query, head) sums together: 16-31 shuffles per block instead of 20 per query, adding the same pairs in the same order. |
| `STRATA_ATTN_MERGE_ACTIVE=1` | The attention merge of a call of 8 rows or fewer folds only the chunks its selection reaches, with loads issued 8 at a time. The chunks past it hold no cells and were skipped anyway. The MTP drafter's 32K window is 512 chunks. |

Engine, main 296b59d2 vs this branch with all four on. Setup: 2x Arc Pro B70 32 GB, kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime
26.22.38646.4, oneAPI 2026.1, AOT bmg-g31. Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS. Flags:
`--layer-split 30 --prefill 8192 --kv int8 --spec 4 --mtp <BF16 draft layer> --mtp-max-t 4 --spec-min-p 0
--stream-experts --expert-cache auto`. Greedy, fixed prompts.

| | without | with the switches |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| one stream, `--max-context 65536`, tok/s, 3 runs (without = main) | 81.8 / 79.5 / 78.7 | 82.2 / 80.0 / 79.1 (+0.6%) |
| one turn on a 40,796-token context, tok/s (without = main) | 76.0 | 77.1 (+1.4%) |
| two streams in one window (`"parallel": 2 --batch-groups 1 --max-context 16384 --vram-reserve-mib 512`), tok/s together, 3 runs (without = switches unset) | 56.78 / 57.84 / 58.23 | 56.41 / 58.99 / 59.14 (median +2%) |

The outputs were identical in every row: text, and for one stream the draft counts too, which match main. With the
switches unset the branch matched main, and prompt reading was unchanged. Coherence and per-card health passed after
every run.

Kernels (`qsa_verify_batch_parity --bench`, one B70, synthetic layers: 24 q heads, INT8 K/V, a 200,000-cell
capacity; graph replay, us; 1K / 16K / 64K of context):

| | off | on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `STRATA_BATCH_QSA_ATTN`, 2 slots x 1 row, selection + attention per layer | 102.8 / 184.0 / 252.6 | 62.3 / 107.9 / 156.2 |
| `STRATA_BATCH_QSA_ATTN`, 2 slots x 2 rows | 183.6 / 365.0 / 498.2 | 78.3 / 138.2 / 205.0 |
| `STRATA_QSA_TOPK_SCAN`, one query (16K / 64K; at 1K every cell is selected) | 36.3 / 57.9 | 19.5 / 42.1 |
| `STRATA_QSA_SCORES_TRANSPOSED`, four queries | 5.5 / 18.7 / 63.1 | 4.6 / 14.1 / 43.2 |
| `STRATA_ATTN_MERGE_ACTIVE`, MTP drafter call (one row, 32K window) | 86.9 / 223.7 / 460.9 | 41.0 / 157.2 / 335.9 |

What it leaves alone:
- the default path;
- the prompt path: prefill calls take the active-count kernels, and the merge switch only acts on calls of 8 rows or
  fewer;
- `qsa_decode_attn_step` (decode without MTP);
- a batch window's K/V and indexer appends, which stay per row;
- batch windows with a streamed K/V, which keep the per-row path because their blocks are made resident row by row;
- CUDA and HIP: no shared file is touched.

## What changed

- `sycl/src/core/verify.cpp`: adds `STRATA_BATCH_QSA_ATTN`. In `record_window`'s QSA branch, a new branch before the
  per-row batch loop runs the scores per slot (a slot's rows are contiguous), one `qsa_block_topk` and one
  `qsa_decode_attn_multi` for the window.
- `sycl/include/strata/qsa_decode_attn_multi.hpp` (new, SYCL only) and `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/qsa_decode_attn.dp.cpp`:
  - `qsa_decode_attn_multi` is `qsa_decode_attn_batch` over up to four pool sets per launch. Row z's work-group picks
    its set; the chunk and merge kernels are the existing ones. Mixed KV formats or `STRATA_ATTN_LANECELL=1` fall back
    to one `qsa_decode_attn_batch` per set.
  - `STRATA_ATTN_MERGE_ACTIVE`: a new `attn_merge_active_kernel`, and a check in front of `qsa_decode_attn_batch`'s
    merge launch.
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.dp.cpp`:
  - `STRATA_QSA_TOPK_SCAN`: `block_topk_wide_kernel` gets `template <bool SCAN = false>`. The scan is an
    `if constexpr` branch that only the new launch instantiates; the existing launch compiles the same code.
  - `STRATA_QSA_SCORES_TRANSPOSED`: a new `block_scores_multi_t_kernel<NQ>`, launched from `qsa_block_scores`'s
    multi-query branch.
- `sycl/src/kernels/qsa_verify_batch_parity.cpp` (new) and `sycl/CMakeLists.txt` add two ctest entries:
  - `qsa_verify_batch_parity`, without switches, checks in process that:
    - the batch-window form equals the per-row calls (2x1, 2x2, 4x2, 6x1 and 1x4 windows at 1K / 16K / 64K);
    - the selections equal `qsa_block_topk_ref`;
    - the attention equals `qsa_decode_attn_step`;
    - 1-8-query scores equal one call per query;
    - the MTP drafter call equals `qsa_decode_attn_step`.

    It also writes a hash of each of its 45 outputs.
  - `qsa_verify_batch_parity_switches` repeats this with the three kernel switches set and requires the same hashes.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: a short section with the numbers above.

## Extra Notes

- Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code): the code, the measurements and this text were produced by Claude on the submitter's two Arc Pro B70s, at the submitter's request.
- How the bitwise claim was checked:
  - both ctest entries pass, and each switch alone passes against the same hashes;
  - the engine outputs above are identical with the switches on, off and unset, and match main.

  No tolerance is used anywhere.
- Built: SYCL (AOT bmg-g31), `strata` and `qsa_verify_batch_parity`. No CUDA or HIP file is touched.
- `STRATA_QSA_TOPK_SCAN` did not act in the engine runs. At `--max-context 65536` the wide top-k is not used.
  `--max-context 200000` (where it is) does not fit every expert on a plain two-card layer split: 710 were refused.
  Its effect is shown by the kernel bench only.
- On a layer split, main refuses `--batch-mtp`. So a two-stream window there is one row per slot, without MTP drafts.
  The default `--batch-groups auto` runs one slot per stage, where `STRATA_BATCH_QSA_ATTN` changes nothing. With
  `--batch-mtp` on one GPU a window is 2 rows per slot: the 2 x 2 kernel row.
- Not included (possible follow-ups), all measured on a development tree:
  - a value-pipelined chunk kernel for decode-sized calls. It needs a kernel variant main does not have; it was 7-10%
    faster on the MTP call.

title: sycl: KREG small-batch mmvq kernels for Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K/IQ4_XS at 1-8 columns (opt-in STRATA_MMVQ_KREG=1)
body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #2803

## Summary

On the Arc Pro B70 the SYCL port's decode GEMVs for Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K and IQ4_XS (`native_mmvq`, 1-8 columns) are
bound by instruction issue, not by memory: the wide kernels re-read every column's activations for every row. This
adds an opt-in kernel family, KREG: one work-group covers a row's whole K, each lane loads its slice of every
column's activations once into registers, and the group streams tiles of 2-8 rows against them.
`STRATA_MMVQ_KREG=1` turns it on. Unset, the default path is unchanged (output identical to main, measured below).

Upstream main 296b59d2 against this branch: 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB, kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4,
oneAPI 2026.1, AOT bmg-g31; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, `--layer-split 30 --prefill 8192
--max-context 65536 --kv int8 --spec 4 --mtp <BF16 draft layer> --mtp-max-t 4 --spec-min-p 0 --stream-experts
--expert-cache auto`, one slot, greedy, a fixed prompt with a 512-token coding reply, 3 runs each, the container
environment of docs/INTEL.md.

| | decode tok/s | tokens per verify window | ms per window |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 81.8 / 79.5 / 78.7 | 3.22 / 3.14 / 3.12 | 39.4 / 39.5 / 39.7 |
| this branch, flag unset | 81.9 / 79.4 | the same as main | - |
| this branch, `STRATA_MMVQ_KREG=1` | 95.0 / 93.1 / 96.3 | 3.35 / 3.20 / 3.33 | 35.2 / 34.4 / 34.5 |

- Median decode 79.5 -> 95.0 tok/s (+19.5%). The part that does not depend on the drafts is the verify window,
  39.5 -> 34.5 ms (-12%); the rest is the changed output drafting a little better on this prompt.
- Flag unset: output and draft counts identical to main on both runs and on a turn at a 40,796-token context.
- At a 40,796-token context: 76.0 -> 83.4 tok/s. Prompt reading unchanged: 4K 1,189 -> 1,191 tok/s, 32K
  1,956-2,004 -> 1,961-2,008.

Kernel time, us per call, default -> KREG (`mmvq_kreg_parity --bench`, one B70, random weights, distinct copies per
graph so L2 never holds a matrix):

| format, shape (n_in x n_out) | 1 column | 2 | 4 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q6_K 2560 x 10240 | 55.7 -> 41.0 | 63.0 -> 41.5 | 73.4 -> 46.0 | 88.9 -> 57.7 |
| Q5_K head 2560 x 248320 | 1063 -> 759 | 1374 -> 775 | 2013 -> 893 | 2691 -> 1175 |
| Q4_K 2560 x 10240 | 44.5 -> 28.8 | 55.6 -> 29.6 | 78.8 -> 31.9 | 107.9 -> 40.5 |
| IQ4_XS 2560 x 10240 | 42.9 -> 33.5 | 47.9 -> 37.8 | 55.9 -> 41.2 | 67.6 -> 49.3 |

## What changed

- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/native_mmvq.dp.cpp`
  - KREG kernels: `native_mmvq_kreg_kernel` with traits `KregQ4K`, `KregQ5K`, `KregQ6K`, `KregIQ4XS` (the wide
    kernels' lane split and dot expressions; K-quant scales decoded branch-free; IQ4_XS's codebook from a
    256-entry local-memory table), a transposed sub-group butterfly and a double-buffered local-memory sum across
    sub-groups. Rows per tile and the 256-register mode per format and column count come from a sweep on the B70.
  - `try_kreg<F>()`: its first statement reads the flag (latched once, one stderr line when on). It declines n_in
    above 32,768 and Q4_K/Q5_K (IQ4_XS) matrices that are not 16- (8-) byte aligned; the existing kernels then run
    as before.
  - One guarded hook per entry: `native_q4_k_mmvq`, `native_q5_k_mmvq`, `native_iq4_xs_mmvq` before `try_wide`;
    `native_q6_k_mmvq` after the `STRATA_Q6_PACKED` check. The output head goes through `native_mmvq`, so it is
    covered.
  - `native_mmvq_set_kreg(int)` for tests (1 on, 0 off, -1 the env latch, the default).
- `sycl/include/strata/kernels/native_mmvq.hpp`: its declaration (the port's copy of the header).
- `sycl/src/kernels/mmvq_kreg_parity.cpp` (new), in the `sycl/CMakeLists.txt` parity loop (`--selftest`). For each
  format, 5 shapes and 1-8 columns: KREG and the default kernels against a float64 reference over the same weight
  and Q8_1 bytes; KREG differs from the default kernels (the call reached it); a T-column KREG call bitwise equal to
  T one-column calls; a power check (one scale step in one sub-block must fail the bound). `--bench` times both on
  random weights (constant fills read too fast on Xe2: memory compression).
- `docs/INTEL.md`: a section for the flag with these numbers.

Left alone: the other formats (Q8_0, IQ4_NL, IQ3_S, Q2_0, ...), the multi/small/wave kernels, tensors packed by
`STRATA_Q6_PACKED`, `include/`, `src/` and the CUDA/HIP sources. Only the SYCL backend is touched and built.

## Extra Notes

- Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code): the code, the measurements and this text were produced by Claude on the submitter's two Arc Pro B70s, at the submitter's request.
- Default path: byte-identical by construction (with the flag unset each hook reads a latched bool and returns; no
  shared code changed), and measured identical output and draft counts against main (above).
- `mmvq_kreg_parity --selftest` on one B70: 0 failures over 160 cases (4 formats x 5 shapes x 1-8 columns). KREG and
  the default kernels are both within 5e-8 of sum |w x| of the reference, every multi-column output is bitwise
  equal to the one-column calls, KREG differs from the default kernels in 144 cases, no non-finite output.
- Not bitwise equal to the default kernels (another FP32 summation order), so greedy outputs change after some
  tokens and MTP acceptance moves with them; the per-window time is the fair comparison. Teacher-forced NLL on 3
  texts (4,762 tokens) through the decode-window path, measured in a development tree (expert parallelism over the
  two cards, not upstream main): mean NLL 0.013 nats lower with the flag, inside the noise band of other
  summation-order changes. Not re-run on main.
- In that development tree the same kernels gave single-stream decode 107.2 -> 131.7 tok/s and two streams
  63.9 -> 73.1 tok/s each.
- IQ4_XS at 1 column on small matrices (2560 x 512 / 640) is 0.90-0.98x of the default kernel. KREG still takes it,
  so that whether a call uses KREG never depends on the column count and multi-column calls stay bitwise equal to
  one-column calls.
- Not tested: two streams on main (main refuses `--batch-mtp` on a layer split), `--max-context 200000` (a plain
  two-card layer split of main does not fit all 24,576 experts there), the Arc A-series cards.

title: sycl: cheaper IQ decodes in the grouped expert kernels (STRATA_IQ_DECODE_FAST=1, opt-in, bitwise)
body:
## Title
sycl: cheaper IQ decodes in the grouped expert kernels (STRATA_IQ_DECODE_FAST=1, opt-in, bitwise)

Issue: Resolves #2801

## Summary

The SYCL lane kernels that read the routed experts (`native_gu_kernel` / `native_down_kernel`, 8 lanes a row) are
ALU-bound on an Arc Pro B70: 280-480 instructions per 32-weight part for the part's 8 dp4a, reading the experts at
19-44% of DRAM bandwidth. Most of it is the dpct per-byte emulation of `byte_level_permute` in the Q2_0 dot (476 per
part, 157 of them `mov`), the compare/select chain of the IQ4_NL codebook lookup, the popcount/multiply ksigns
unpacking, and 64-bit `kbx * sizeof(block)` address products every iteration.

`STRATA_IQ_DECODE_FAST=1` switches the seven IQ expert formats (IQ2_XXS, IQ2_XS, IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S, IQ2_S gate/up;
IQ4_NL, Q2_0 down) to kernels that produce the same bits with fewer instructions. Off by default: without the flag
the engine runs exactly the code it ran before (the hook is the first statement of `launch_gu_port` /
`launch_down_port` and returns at once). SYCL only.

Measured on two Arc Pro B70 (32 GB, kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4, oneAPI 2026.1, AOT `bmg-g31`),
upstream main 296b59d2 against this branch, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, `--layer-split 30 --prefill 8192
--max-context 65536 --kv int8 --spec 4 --mtp <BF16 draft layer> --mtp-max-t 4 --spec-min-p 0 --stream-experts
--expert-cache auto`, one slot, greedy, a fixed prompt with a 512-token coding reply:

- decode: main 81.8 / 79.5 / 78.7 tok/s (3 runs, median 79.5); this branch, flag unset, 81.7 / 79.3; with
  `STRATA_IQ_DECODE_FAST=1` 88.1 / 85.6 / 84.7 (median 85.6, +7.7%);
- the output tokens and the draft acceptance counts are identical in every run, flag on or off, so the gain is
  kernel time alone; a turn at a 40,796-token context: 76.0 -> 81.4 tok/s (+7.1%), identical output;
- prompt reading unchanged (4K 1189 -> 1192 tok/s, 32K 1956-2004 -> 1964-2009): the change is decode-only;
- `native_grouped_parity --iq`: 0 failures (15 cases bitwise equal); plain `native_grouped_parity`: 0 failures;
  per-card health after every run passed. Two concurrent streams were not tested (main does not take `--batch-mtp`
  on a layer split).

On a development tree, a grouped-call microbenchmark on one B70 (48 layers per graph streaming their own experts,
us per call, new against current, bitwise equal in every row) put the gain per layer type at: IQ2_XXS/Q2_0
114.8 -> 59.8 to 248.7 -> 147.3, IQ3_S/Q2_0 105.1 -> 70.3 to 256.9 -> 175.1, IQ2_S/Q2_0 97.0 -> 67.2 to
237.3 -> 161.9, IQ2_XS/IQ4_NL 135.6 -> 119.6 to 242.6 -> 205.4, IQ3_XXS/IQ4_NL 146.6 -> 127.9 to 253.4 -> 221.3
(the shapes of a two-card serve at 1 to 4 streams); the Q2_0 down product alone 63.7 -> 26.4 us.

## What changed

- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.dp.cpp` (+426 lines, inside the anonymous namespace, before the lane launchers):
  - `IqFast<TY>` decode traits for types 16, 17, 18, 21, 22, 42, 20. Each `prep` yields the same integers as
    `Multi<TY>::prep` / the `vec_dot_*_q8_1` dot and reuses the same `acts` and `finish` (IQ2_XXS and IQ2_XS, which
    have no `Multi<>`, get a `finish` with the statements of their `vec_dot` in the same order). Inside `prep`: the
    IQ2_XXS / IQ2_XS ksigns masks from a 2 KB table (`kIqKsignMask` = `unpack_ksigns` and the two `swar_ne4`); a
    signed grid byte as `(g ^ m) + (m & 0x01010101)`, which equals `swar_sub4(g ^ m, m)` for grid bytes under 128
    (every byte of the five IQ grids in ggml-common.h is 1..62); Q2_0 fields spread by shifts and masks and biased
    with `(t + 0x7F7F7F7F) ^ 0x80808080`; the IQ4_NL codebook through four 256-entry position tables (`kIqNlPos`,
    8 KB); IQ3_XXS / IQ3_S / IQ2_S keep their ALU sign masks (a table measured slower for them) and take aligned
    8-byte loads.
  - `rows_dot_fast<TY, LANES, R, E>`: R rows x E entries per lane, walking block pointers (with `LANES % ipb == 0` a
    lane's part index is fixed), the k order, per-entry float sum order and `lanes_sum` of `row_dot_lanes` /
    `row_dot_multi_iq`.
  - `native_gu_kernel_fast` / `native_down_kernel_fast`: the lane kernels with those dots, two rows per lane in
    16-lane sub-groups (the one-row SIMD32 form spilled registers and measured slower), entries in chunks of 4, 2 and
    1 as `row_entries`; IQ2_XXS thereby gets a multi-entry form (the current kernel decodes it once per entry).
  - `iq_fast_on(type)`: `STRATA_IQ_DECODE_FAST` read once at the first expert call (one stderr line when on);
    `STRATA_IQ_DECODE_FAST_FMTS=<ggml ids>` restricts it to some formats for an A/B. `launch_gu_fast` /
    `launch_down_fast` launch the kernels at 8 lanes a row only (other `STRATA_GU_LANES` / `STRATA_DOWN_LANES` keep
    the current kernels).
  - One hook line at the top of `launch_gu_port` and `launch_down_port`; `native_expert_set_iq_decode_fast(int)`
    for the parity test (declared there, like `native_expert_set_kq_split`; no header change).
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/iq_decode_tables.inc` (new): the two tables, with the formulas that generate them.
- `sycl/src/kernels/native_grouped_parity.cpp`: `--iq` mode: fast against current, bitwise, every IQ gate/up format
  with both IQ down formats at 512 x 256 and the model's five expert pairs at 2560 x 640, groups of 1..6 entries
  (the chunks of 4 and 2 and the single tail), entries from 0 and from 7, scattered destinations, stale scratch, the
  rows a call must not write included.
- `sycl/CMakeLists.txt`: ctest `native_grouped_parity_iq_decode`.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: a section on the flag with the measurements above.

Left alone: `include/`, `src/`, the CUDA and HIP backends, every kernel the default path runs, the K-quant / Q5_1 /
Q8_0 expert formats, the MMVQ kernels, the prompt path. Not included: a table form of the IQ3 sign masks and a
bit-slice IQ4_NL select (both measured slower), the one-row SIMD32 variant, and gate/up Q2_0 (not measured).

## Extra Notes

- Why the bits cannot move: each part's dp4a inputs are the same integers as before and the `finish` is the same
  expression in the same order; the per-entry float sums run in the same k order with the same `lanes_sum`. The
  parity test checks it on random blobs, the serve above end to end (identical tokens and acceptance counts).
- Built with the SYCL build (`sycl/CMakeLists.txt`): `strata` and `native_grouped_parity`. No CUDA or HIP file is
  touched.
- Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code): the code, the measurements and this text were produced by Claude on the submitter's two Arc Pro B70s, at the submitter's request.

title: HIP: verify-window routing for non-native routers (256 experts) on every HIP card
body:
## Summary

The native router is 512 × 10 only. A 256-expert model (the Coder) therefore takes the per-token `moe_route` loop inside the verify window on every card except gfx906: one projection + top-k launch pair per token and layer, about 360 small launches per `--spec 4` step. `moe_route_window` (one multi-column BF16 projection + one top-k per layer, bitwise equal to the per-token calls per `route_window_parity`) was compiled for gfx906 only.

This PR runs it on every HIP card by default. `STRATA_ROUTE_WIN=0` restores the per-token loop. On CUDA it is opt-in (`STRATA_ROUTE_WIN=1`), because I have not measured it there.

**Relation to #238:** this does not touch the native router or its 512-only guard. The Coder keeps the generic router's arithmetic; only the number of launches changes, and the output stays byte-identical (below).

## Commits

1. **Verify profile + parity test:** a profile-only stamp after the routing splits slot 17 into `router (proj+topk)` and `plan+bell`, so a slow router shows on its own line (it writes nothing unless `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE` or the #649 trace is on). `route_window_parity` now also checks T = 1 and 5 (the `--spec 4` verifier runs every T from 1 to 5).
2. **HIP:** the `STRATA_HIP_GFX906` guard around the `moe_route_window` branch becomes `route_window_on()`.

## Measurements

Radeon AI PRO R9700 32 GB (gfx1201, ROCm SDK 7.10 wheels), i7-14700, 32 GB RAM, Linux. Coder IQ1_M, `--spec 4`, MTP, resident experts (100 % VRAM hit rate). Engine built from this branch on main `296b59d2`, default gfx12 settings (so `STRATA_HC_Q8` was on in both arms). A = `STRATA_ROUTE_WIN=0` (current main behaviour), B = default.

- `route_window_parity`: **OK**, T = 1..6, 256 experts top-10 and the 1-row gate, bit-identical.
- Routing (projection + top-k) per verify window, `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1`:
  - GDN layers: 3.74 → 1.06 ms
  - QSA layers: 1.24 → 0.34 ms

| Benchmark (temp 0) | A tok/s | B tok/s | ms/step A → B | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 short code/text prompts, 600 max tokens | 98.5 | **108.1 (+9.7 %)** | 29.5 → 26.8 | same text, 5/5 |
| 3 prompts at 45K context, 500 max tokens | 87.1 | **95.1 (+9.2 %)** | 30.8 → 28.3 | same text, 3/3 |

Prefill is unchanged. Acceptance is unchanged (74.9 % / 74.8 %).

## Compatibility with open PRs

This branch merges cleanly with #2492 (gfx12 grid padding) and #2476 (no file lookahead when experts are resident). I run all three together on the same R9700: 13/13 served answers byte-identical to main (5 short, 5 Spanish, 3 at 45K context), with the measurements posted on those PRs.

## Not tested

- CUDA: the branch is guarded as opt-in there.
- gfx906: unchanged by default (it already took this path).
- Other RDNA cards: the path is architecture-independent and parity-checked, but I have only measured gfx1201.

docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md.

medians): Strata v0.1.44.1 source build (project 296b59d2), Flash-Next IQ3_XXS,
262,144-token context, --kv int8, vision on, automatic layer split (~99.4% of the

The report also notes that the suite caps generation at 24 tokens for its prompt

Adds four folders under `bench/results/`: one run folder per quantization, plus a summary folder that compares the three. Results only — no engine, setup or docs changes.

## Hardware

RTX 4090 24 GiB (driver 610.88, PCIe 4.0 x16), i7-13700K (16 cores/24 threads, no AVX-512), 127.8 GiB RAM, Windows 10 (10.0.26200). Strata 0.1.44.1 prebuilt engine (`bd18453f…`, unchanged across the runs), project commit 296b59d2.

## What was tested

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next at 262,144 tokens of context, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`, `--vision`, one request at a time (`settings.parallel` not set), each after `setup.py --calibrate` tuned it for this PC:

| Quantization | Experts in RAM | Tuned settings |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| IQ3_XXS (`ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF`) | 39.97 GiB | `--pcie-frac 0.35 --spec-min-p 0.70 --pool-workers 7 --adapt-swaps 80` |
| IQ3_S (same repo) | 46.84 GiB | `--pcie-frac 0.20 --spec-min-p 0.70 --pool-workers 7 --adapt-swaps 160` |
| Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL (`unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF`) | 71.73 GiB | `--pcie-frac 0.20 --spec-min-p 0.70 --pool-workers 7 --adapt-swaps 160` |

Measured with `python tools/strata_bench.py --runs 3 --clients 4 --long` against an already-running server; model load is not timed.

## Numbers (median of 3 runs)

| Quantization | chat decode tok/s | 4K prompt | 16K prompt | 32K prompt | agent decode | 4 clients total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| IQ3_XXS | 109.2 | 2634.9 | 4622.9 | 4771.2 | 132.3 | 95.3 |
| IQ3_S | 92.2 | 2158.7 | 4161.7 | 4228.6 | 119.8 | 74.8 |
| UD-Q4_K_XL | 62.8 | 1310.9 | 2510.6 | 2498.1 | 80.7 | 47.8 |

IQ3_S is 9-22 % slower than IQ3_XXS at every length here, with 6.9 GiB more experts in RAM — consistent with the registry note in `setup.py` ("about 15% slower than IQ3_XXS and 7 GB more RAM"), which had not been measured on this hardware. Needle recall: found at 128k and at 258,266 prompt tokens, depths 10 % and 90 % (IQ3_XXS 4/4, IQ3_S 2/2).

## Limitations

Speed only: no quality, coding or long-conversation evaluation, and the two quality columns quoted in the summary come from `docs/QUANTS.md` on a different machine. One session, one GPU, warm expert cache, background load not recorded, model-load time excluded. The three use different calibrated settings, so these are not kernel-only differences. UD-Q4_K_XL was not needle- or vision-checked in this session.

## Extra Notes
- Hardware: RTX 3060 12 GB behind PCIe Gen2 x4, 2x Xeon E5-2630 v2 (Ivy Bridge, AVX + F16C only), 252 GiB DDR3, Fedora 44
- Strata 296b59d2, engine 0.1.44.1, source build (CUDA 13.3, sm_86, `-DSTRATA_ISA_FLOOR=avx`)
- Model: Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ2_XS, context 40,960, KV int8, MTP spec 4, thinking off, network disconnected during the tests

Results:
- Unit tests: all AVX parity tests pass, no SIGILL; CTest 117/119 (two environmental failures, explained in the README)
- Decode: ~17 tok/s bound to NUMA node 1, 24-26 tok/s across both sockets (`ab_engine.py`, 3 rounds)
- Prompt: 178 / 342 / 352 tok/s at 4K / 16K / 32K; TTFT 22.6 / 47.0 / 91.0 s (cold and warm are the same)
- Needles 9/9 at 4K / 16K / 32K
- Same checks as the 2026-10-09 RTX 3060 report: HumanEval 0-39 37/40 base, 35/40 plus (report: 36/40, 35/40), Japanese 11/12, tools 8/8
- Soak 65.7 min, 116 requests, 0 failures, 29/29 known-answer checks
- Quant yardstick: two IQ2_XS runs byte-identical; IQ2_XS vs UD-IQ4_XS top-1 80.3%, KL 0.309

Limitations: one machine, IQ2_XS only for speed, contexts up to 40,960; five mocked setup tests hit the 600 s timeout once in the offline run. On rerun four passed and `test_setup_golden` failed as it does on upstream here (details in the README).

Finding worth noting for others on old dual-socket Xeons: spreading the engine across both sockets was ~40% faster for decode than binding it to the GPU's node.

title: bench/results: RTX 5070 Ti (16 GiB) with 31.6 GiB of RAM — IQ2_XS at 128K in low-RAM mode
body:
Adds a results-only report for an **RTX 5070 Ti (16 GiB) with 31.6 GiB of system RAM** — the same GPU as `2026-10-04-community-rtx-5070ti-windows` and `2026-10-06-community-rtx5070ti-5900x`, but at half their RAM, which in `bench/results/` is a combination that is not covered yet.

Only three files under `bench/results/2026-10-17-community-rtx-5070-ti-qwen3-8-flash-next-iq2-xs/` (`README.md`, `results.json`, `engine-log-excerpt.txt`). No engine or code changes, as the guide asks for a results-only submission.

## Hardware

- RTX 5070 Ti, 16,303 MiB VRAM, power limit 300 W (not reduced), PCIe Gen5 x16
- Ryzen 7 9700X (8C/16T, AVX-512), **31.6 GiB RAM**
- WD_BLACK SN770 1 TB NVMe (model files and OS on the same drive)
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, driver 616.64, CUDA 13.0
- Not an isolated machine (proxy, Steam, ComfyUI MCP bridge, antivirus; the GPU also drives the display)

## Model and configuration

- `ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF` @ `ed59f92`, IQ2_XS, both shards with their SHA-256
- Context **131,072**, KV `q4_0`, KV streaming off, **low-RAM mode (`--mmap-experts`)**, expert cache `auto` (~5,000 slots / ~6.8 GiB VRAM), `--prefill auto`, MTP `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`, `--vram-reserve-mib 1600`
- Strata 0.1.44.1 / engine 0.1.44.1, release binary, zip install (not a git checkout)
- Thinking off for the suite; the suite's requests set `temperature 0`

## Results (medians, ranges over 3 runs)

| Configuration | Actual prompt tokens | Runs | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s | TTFT s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| short chat (100 tok cap) | 46 | 9 | not measured | 57.2 (36.8-87.0) | 0.54 (0.42-1.06) |
| 4K prompt, fresh | 4019 | 3 | 270.0 (226.5-270.2) | not measured | 14.94 (14.94-17.80) |
| 16K prompt, fresh | 16058 | 3 | 447.8 (446.7-518.1) | not measured | 35.94 (31.07-36.03) |
| agent session, follow-up turns | 14572 | 3 | see report | 45.2 (32.3-51.4) | 12.79 (10.82-17.17) |

Total suite time 420 s.

## What the report is about — and its limitation

This install cannot keep the 36 GB expert arena in 31.6 GiB of RAM, so unlike the two 64 GiB 5070 Ti reports it runs the low-RAM mode and serves the experts through the OS file cache. The measured boundary:

- **decode** lands at ~85-87 tok/s once the cache is warm, roughly half the 64 GiB figures (102 tok/s)
- **prompt processing** is 270-448 tok/s against 1,992-3,523 tok/s at 64 GiB — **4-8x slower**, because the prompt path re-reads lent experts from the SSD

So on a 32 GiB machine the prompt/TTFT side, not decode, is what decides whether the setup is usable (a 16K prompt is 36 s before the first token). The chat row's 36.8-87.0 range is the low-RAM cache warming across the nine back-to-back requests, not run-to-run noise; the report says so in the Results section.

Also recorded because the guide asks for them: storage, PCIe link, power limit and the background load are filled in, and two things the tool got wrong are corrected — it reports the OS as "Windows 10 (10.0.26100)" (actually Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200) and its own README template asks for facts it cannot read (CUDA version, commit on a zip install).

## One tool bug found while preparing this

`tools/strata_bench.py:564` reads `CMakeLists.txt` with `read_text()` and no encoding, so on a Chinese/Japanese Windows (GBK code page) it raises `UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xbf in position 2` on the file's UTF-8 BOM and exits **before any measurement**. `setup.py:4649` reads the same file with `encoding="utf-8"`. `PYTHONUTF8=1` works around it. Happy to file it as an issue with the traceback if that is more useful than fixing it in this PR — I left it out of this PR to keep it results-only.

title: hip: route the asynchronous adaptive tier through adapt_copy_h2d (#884)
body:
## Title
<!-- If Applicable, reference the GitHub issue -->
Issue: relates to #884 — it makes that switch effective on a path it never reached. It does not claim to fix the ROCm barrier itself.

## Summary
`STRATA_HIP_ADAPT_KERNEL_COPY=1` (#884) is dead code whenever `--adapt-async 1` is on. The asynchronous adaptive tier copies its swaps in with a raw `cudaMemcpyAsync` and never calls `adapt_copy_h2d()`, so every swap goes back over SDMA — the combination #884 exists to avoid. On gfx1030 the queue then dies with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_INVALID_PACKET_FORMAT` (the malformed barrier packet), which the server reports as `verify: layer 0 never rang (unspecified launch failure)`.

## What changed
`src/program/generate.cpp`, `a_in_one` (the async tier's step-2 copy in): `cudaMemcpyAsync(...)` → `adapt_copy_h2d(...)`, the helper the blocking tier already calls. Two lines.

The stream, the asynchrony and the fallback are unchanged: `adapt_copy_h2d` ends in the identical `cudaMemcpyAsync` when the switch is off or the source is not mapped, so with the switch off this is behaviourally the old code.

Leaves alone: the blocking tier, `a_back` (the D2H side has no kernel-copy helper), and `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp` (its own `adapt_copy_h2d`, same gap).

## Evidence
gfx1030 (RX 6800), ROCm 7.13.0a, 0.1.44.1 source, `--adapt-async 1 --adapt-swaps 160 --kv-resident 32768 --cache-suffix-reuse 64`, arena mode, 250 MiB VRAM free, same config and box:

| binary | outcome | elapsed | AQL aborts |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| unpatched | aborted | 72.7 s | 2 |
| patched | completed | 185.2 s | 0 |

The switch's own line (`adaptive swaps copy with a kernel, not SDMA (#884)`) appears once with the patch and never without it. It is printed on the helper's first call, and `a_in_one` is the only GPU copy this config makes, so the line is the proof the helper is now reachable.

Cost — 3 alternating rounds, 512 greedy tokens each, medians:

| prompt | kernel copy | SDMA |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| essay | decode 39.5 tok/s | 40.4 tok/s |
| code | decode 36.7 tok/s | 36.6 tok/s |

−2.2% / +0.3%: no measurable cost, as the #884 reporter also measured.

## Extra Notes
- **Not built or run: CUDA and SYCL.** Only HIP/gfx1030 could be built here (no CUDA toolkit, no oneAPI installed). `src/program/generate.cpp` is one target for HIP and CUDA; the SYCL engine builds a separate file, `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`, whose `adapt_copy_h2d` has the same gap — left alone deliberately rather than hand-edited dpct output I cannot compile.
- The switch stays opt-in: with it off, the async tier keeps using SDMA and the abort returns.
- Reported from hardware the maintainers may not have (single RX 6800, not the reporter's 2x RX 6900 XT), so this is one machine's result.
