title: HIP: the RX 6600 / 6650 XT (gfx1032) in setup's cards and CMake's unvalidated list
body:
Issue: Refs #1375 (the gfx1032 report), #1378 (the open RX 6600 benchmark)

## Summary

Adds gfx1032 (AMD Radeon RX 6600 / 6650 XT, RDNA2) to the architectures setup installs and builds for, and to CMake's
`_strata_hip_unvalidated` list, so this card is no longer refused.

The engine already compiles for gfx1032: `include/strata/hip_compat/intrinsics.hpp` gates
`__gfx1030__ || __gfx1031__ || __gfx1032__` on the same signed-dot4 branch, and `docs/AMD_HIP.md` already listed gfx1032
as "the same `dp4a` path, no hardware report". Only the setup and CMake lists were missing. Built and run on one
RX 6650 XT (gfx1032, 8 GB, Fedora, ROCm 7.1.1).

## What changed

- `cmake/hip_backend.cmake`: gfx1032 added to `_strata_hip_unvalidated`, next to gfx1030/gfx1031 (the same `dp4a`
  path). A `-DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1032` now builds with the usual "not validated" warning instead of
  `FATAL_ERROR`.
- `setup.py`: gfx1032 added to `ROCM_INDEXES` (the `gfx103X-all` wheels, as gfx1030/gfx1031), `AMD_ARCHS` (so setup
  detects and builds for the card), `AMD_NAMES`, the `AMD_CARDS` sentence and the AMD header comment.
- `docs/AMD_HIP.md`: gfx1032 moved out of "Not validated" into a line of its own (like gfx1031), with what was run.
- `docs/OLDER_GPUS.md`: an RX 6600 / 6650 XT row in the AMD table.
- `tools/test_setup_amd.py`: gfx1032 is asserted to take the same wheels and path as gfx1030/gfx1031.

**Left alone:** the engine and kernel sources, the CUDA and SYCL backends, and every existing card's entry. On a
machine without a gfx1032 card nothing changes.

## How it was checked

- `python tools/test_setup_amd.py` -> 36 tests OK; `python tools/test_setup_rocm_pins.py` -> 17 tests OK (both run
  before and after the change).
- HIP engine built for gfx1032 on the machine (ROCm 7.1.1, rocBLAS from the `_rocm_sdk_libraries_gfx103X_all` wheel,
  see the notes below): `./build-hip/strata-device --selftest` ->
  `HIP arch gfx1032 wave32 (compiled for gfx1032) ... strata-device selftest OK`.
- A model served end to end (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q2_0 on the 8 GB card): `/v1/models` reports it loaded and chat
  answers are correct.

## Extra Notes

- Reported **unvalidated**, like gfx1030 in #311: one machine, and no llama.cpp parity or KL/quality run yet. A
  same-day A/B against a build on a supported card, and `tools/qwen35/parity.py` / `tools/quant_quality.py`, are not in
  this PR - I can follow up with them.
- Two notes specific to this box are **not** part of the patch (Fedora / AMD library packaging, not Strata):
  1. Fedora's ROCm 7.1.1 lives in `/usr` (no `/opt/rocm`, libraries in `lib64`); a small symlink shim gives setup the
     `ROCM_PATH` layout it expects, without changing system detection.
  2. The system rocBLAS Tensile library has no gfx1032 kernels, so a dense GEMM aborts or silently returns zeros. The
     `_rocm_sdk_libraries_gfx103X_all` wheel's `librocblas.so.5` **and** its library data must replace the system pair
     together; replacing only the library data is not enough (checked with a probe where the correct result is known).
     If other gfx1032 users hit it, it may deserve a line in `docs/AMD_HIP.md` - I left it out of this PR.
- Windows detection (`_WIN_AMD_DID` / `_WIN_AMD_NAME`) is not touched: I have no Windows machine here, so
  `setup --backend hip` on a Windows gfx1032 card is untested. The ready-made Windows zip has no gfx1032 code, like
  gfx1031 before 0.1.40.2, but the build is available from source (`-DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1032`).

title: Per-client expert memory
body:
When two programs share the server (an agent and a mail assistant), each request from the other one refills the VRAM cache with

(also with `--adapt-async 1`). RTX 5070 Ti, Q2_0, 61-75K context: agent step right after another program +21% tok/s (+24% by

title: Short prompt chunks: router push + decode grouped kernel for resident experts
body:
Agent workloads read many short prompt chunks (tool results, file excerpts): in a 5-hour coding-agent session on an RTX 5070 Ti
(Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO Q2_0, 256K) 74% of the reads were under 1,000 tokens and took 57% of the read time, at 200-750 tok/s.

With `STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING=1`, a 170-token chunk spends ~40% in what the timer calls "dequant": on a canonical (non-native)
pack, below `stream_all_min` MMQ converts every expert blob into GGUF blocks with one `gather_strata_q2` launch per expert
(~14,000 launches for 170 tokens); the copies from RAM are only ~3%.

The branch adds, for chunks below `stream_all_min` only:
- `STRATA_PF_ROUTE_PRIOR=lambda` — the decode push (`route_prior_top10`) also in the prefill router (opt-in, changes outputs
  like `STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR`);
- resident experts used by at most `STRATA_PF_DIRETTO_MAX` rows (default 8) leave MMQ's list — their rows form a block after the
  local ones, as the CPU share does — and run on `moe_grouped_s2` (or `native_expert_grouped` for native packs) straight from the
  compressed blob, in calls of up to 1,024 rows with a small own scratch (9 MiB). `STRATA_PF_DIRETTO=0` turns it off.

Measured (28K cached context, appended chunk, RTX 5070 Ti): 177 tokens 473 → ~315 ms, ~500 668 → ~470 ms, ~900 826 → ~677 ms;
>= 1,024 tokens and decode unchanged. Max rows 16 ≈ 8; 4 is worse; all rows is much worse (the decode kernel re-reads the blob
every 8 rows).

Two pitfalls found on the way: `moe_grouped_s2` handles at most `GMAX = 8` rows per group and silently drops the rest; MMQ closes
its last group at `rows_local` (`bounds_host[n]`), so `rows_local` must exclude the new block.

The read push is opt-in; so far only sanity-checked on outputs, no separate quality run yet (the decode push `STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=1.0` was quality-checked on two real tasks, 3+3 runs, no measurable loss).

Full notes and measurements: https://github.com/apatassini/Strata/blob/qwen38-16gb/QWEN38.md

Community benchmark from an RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100) — a first report for this GPU in `bench/results/`, run with `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1) against an already-running server.

**Hardware** — AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX 24 GiB; AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D; 63.7 GiB RAM; Windows 11 (26100); driver 32.0.31041.1004; model and engine on a Samsung 990 PRO 2 TB NVMe.

**Limitations** — speed only, no correctness check; background desktop load was present (expert cache filled to 9.0 GiB of VRAM during the run; ~14 GiB with an idle desktop); single machine, single sitting.

body:
Follow-up to the RTX 5090 Laptop entries (0.1.40.1, 0.1.40.3, 0.1.41 on main; 0.1.43 in #1976): same laptop, model files and scripts, Strata version changed. Results only, no engine changes.

**Median decode / prompt tok/s (Q2_0, 131K context, greedy, reasoning off, 256-token cap):**

| Prompt tokens | 0.1.43 | 0.1.44.1 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4,096 | 140.5 / 1,906.9 | 128.4 / 1,804.1 |
| 32,768 | 141.5 / 2,871.2 | 137.9 / 2,745.6 |
| 128,000 | 131.6 / 2,767.5 | 124.6 / 2,660.9 |

- The 3–9% drop is the laptop, not the engine: its vendor power profile went from "Extreme" to "Normal" on 2026-10-13 (CPU too hot in daily use). A before/after run on the same afternoon with identical configuration (0.1.43 vs 0.1.44.1, 1K–100K prompts) landed within ±2%. The README says so up front.
- Second difference to the 0.1.43 entry: conversation cache 12 GiB / 8 slots instead of 6 GiB / 2 (host RAM only; zero reused tokens in the speed requests).
- Needles 6/6. Coding check 6/10 (the Roman-numeral function got the subtractive forms wrong; 0.1.43 passed 10/10 on the same greedy prompt). Treated as one data point: our private agent task suite (44 tasks x 3 runs, production configuration) went the other way, 126/132 with 0.1.44.1 against 122 with 0.1.43, the best result on this machine so far.
- Restoring a parked 61,775-token conversation after a foreign request: 0.7 s (61,928 tokens reused), unchanged.
- The source was downloaded by commit (`archive/<sha>.zip`), every file was checked against the git tree, and it was built locally for sm_120 with CUDA 13.3.

title: Muse Spark: opt-in streaming reference runtime and CPU/CUDA parity
body:
## Summary

Refs #2762. **Draft: this is an experimental Muse Spark text reference runtime, not complete installer/API integration or verified 816B inference.**

Adds an OFF-by-default `STRATA_ENABLE_MUSE` build option and a separate `strata-muse` executable. It reads standard `muse-spark` GGUF shards, keeps weights file-backed and evaluates decoded row tiles on CPU or through an optional CUDA/cuBLAS adapter. No model weights are included or downloaded automatically.

## What changed

- Complete Muse text forward graph: gated local/global GQA, local NeoX RoPE, folded norm/residual scales, full-stream sigmoid routing with selection-only correction bias, latent projections, per-expert post-normalization before weighted reduction, and final logit scaling/softcap.
- Dynamic geometry, shard/tensor/encoding checks, checked KV/scratch sizing, strict token-ID CLI, metadata EOS/EOT and streamed JSON logits.
- Bounded CUDA matrix-vector adapter: explicitly allocates two 4 MiB buffers plus 256 output bytes; CUDA/cuBLAS overhead is additional. It is **not** Strata's optimized expert cache or a native GPU quantized kernel.
- Independent NumPy FP32 oracle, deterministic synthetic GGUF, strict comparator and mutation tests that expose omitted/reordered graph operations.
- Discoverable build/run documentation in `docs/MUSE_SPARK.md`.

Existing numerical sources, model families, setup defaults, server/frontend, requirements and dependency pins are unchanged. The normal `strata --families` inventory does not advertise Muse.

## Actual validation

Linux x86-64; Ryzen 9 3900X; CUDA 13.0; RTX 3060 12 GiB.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Integrated CPU build and focused CTests | 5/5 passed |
| CUDA-enabled build and focused CTests | 5/5 passed |
| Oracle unit tests | 13/13 passed, including 44 graph/router mutation cases |
| Focused existing Python regressions plus oracle on GPU host | 114 tests passed |
| CPU versus independent oracle, all 7 × 64 logits | max absolute error `1.25150586e-6` |
| **Actual RTX 3060 CUDA execution** versus oracle, all 7 × 64 logits | max absolute error `1.19227037e-6` |
| Comparator bound | `2e-5 + 2e-5 * abs(reference)` |
| Existing reference target with Muse disabled | binary SHA-256 unchanged from the same-day pre-change build |
| Worker sanitizer checks | ASan/UBSan plus leak detection passed |

The tiny test includes two layers, four experts/top2, local-window crossing, nonuniform/nonzero parameters and every Muse-specific graph operation. Separate native tests cover synthetic F32/F16/Q8_0 and production-sized IQ1_S/Q6_K rows, malformed storage/geometry, generation/EOS and allocation failures. Synthetic quantized-row tests are **not** published-checkpoint validation.

Baseline caveat: on untouched upstream `296b59d2f73c8f04a805df29c2fa97655adace78`, the existing setup-golden suite has eight Unsloth subtest failures. Its goldens were not regenerated or changed. The 114 passing tests above exclude that known-failing suite.

## Outstanding / not claimed

- These checks do not establish full 816B checkpoint inference, model quality, production memory requirements or usable speed.
- No tokenizer/chat-template integration, installer entry, OpenAI/Anthropic server integration, tool/reasoning parser, multimodal input, MTP or multi-GPU scheduling.
- No HIP, SYCL or Windows build/device validation. CPU and CUDA are the implemented reference paths.
- No global llama.cpp pin changes. Unsupported row encodings and scaled RoPE fail explicitly.
- Mapped-file/page-cache residency, headers, allocator and library overhead are outside the calculated KV/scratch bound. Input shards must remain unchanged during execution; a failed write/run can leave partial JSON.

This establishes a reproducible, tested numerical path toward #2762; it intentionally does **not** close the feature request or claim a drop-in Muse provider.

AI-assisted implementation used isolated swarm workers and separate fresh-context reviewers. The coordinator inspected changes, integrated ancestry-preserving lane commits, reran tests and performed the actual GPU checks. All testing used isolated temporary containers; no existing model/service/driver/client configuration was replaced.

title: Experimental gfx803 (RX 580) Q36 Linux path
body:
## Title
Experimental gfx803 (RX 580) Q36 Linux path

Issue: Related to #2768 (experimental native RX580/gfx803 support).

## Summary

Opt-in Linux RX580/native gfx803 enablement for `strata-q36`, not general Polaris support.

```text
STRATA_HIP_GFX803=ON
  native gfx803 ISA + existing wave64 compatibility path
  model/expert uploads → per-thread 1 MiB pinned staging → GPU
  bulk CPU experts → pageable arena → scoped source-page reclaim
  prompt batches → hybrid path only (effective rows 8..32)
```

Leaves Q8 KV/tiled attention, CPU batching optimizations, startup caching, setup auto-detection and dependency installation out of this PR.

## What changed

- `CMakeLists.txt`: explicit experimental gfx803 selection and three focused host tests.
- HIP compatibility header: missing hipBLAS aliases.
- `src/prefill/kernels.cu`: gfx803 fallback for an unavailable packed-FP16 instruction.
- Q36 engine/helpers: bounded synchronized uploads, pageable Linux expert arena, reclaim advice restricted to fully copied page-aligned source regions, and an 8–32 hybrid-row cap preventing entry into the faulting streamed expert/MMQ path.
- `tests/qwen35/`: transfer chunking, CPU FP16 conversion, batch-limit regression tests and configurable API smoke harness.
- `docs/AMD_HIP.md`: experimental build prerequisites, usage and limitations.

## Evidence

- **Before:** Unclamped candidate API/tool prompts entered streamed expert/MMQ and produced GPU VM protection faults. The unchanged safety guard stopped those runs.
  **After:** The bounded hybrid implementation passed the in-repository API harness: tool request/result round-trip, stream disconnect during generation, recovery, and fresh-process restart. This avoids the failing path; it does not fix or qualify streamed MMQ.
- Native gfx803 `strata-q36` build passed. All **3/3 host tests** and `git diff --check` passed. The FP16 host test does **not** exercise the changed GPU fallback.
- Hardware run: RX580 8 GiB, Linux, 32 GiB RAM; isolated ROCm 6.3.4 and separately built gfx803 rocBLAS/Tensile. Acceptance took **138.75 s**, peak GPU **58°C**, swap increase **4 KiB**, empty cursor-bounded kernel log and no guard stop. Thresholds: GPU 75°C, CPU 85°C, 2 GiB available-memory reserve, 64 MiB maximum swap growth.
- Model/config: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL; context 2,048; requested chunk 128 / hybrid rows 8 → effective chunk 8; 32 expert slots/layer; three CPU workers plus host; no graphs/warmup; `STRATA_Q8_PACKED=0`; native FP32 KV. This is a tested configuration, not a hardware context limit.
- Base: `296b59d2f73c8f04a805df29c2fa97655adace78`. Hardware-tested implementation: `452eb85a42eb177b195e44e5cb6d9d28fde2d202`. Head: `f82214d627f5fd4318de9a30f48d3c1d60674028`, differing only by a docs correction. Fresh independent final-head review verified unchanged executable/test/build tree identities and found no material findings.

Reproduce host checks after configuring/building the focused test targets:

```sh
ctest --test-dir <build> --output-on-failure \
  -R '^q36_(pageable_transfer|fp16_conversion|gfx803_batch_limits)_test$'
```

Hardware harness (run under an external thermal/memory/kernel-error guard; it is not itself a resource monitor):

```sh
<python> tests/qwen35/gfx803_hardware_acceptance.py \
  --cwd <checkout> --python <python> --config <engine-config.json> \
  --model <configured-model-name>
```

Build prerequisites are documented in `docs/AMD_HIP.md`. Guard receipts remain local; this is not bundled hardware CI or a same-day comparative performance benchmark.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Opt-in source/build changes can be reverted; no data migration or host/driver changes.

**Blast Radius:** backend

The gfx803 path is opt-in, but shared CMake/HIP compatibility/prefill files are touched. Non-gfx803 runtime semantics were checked by source review, **not** demonstrated byte-identical to the last release. CUDA, existing gfx906/RDNA HIP and SYCL build/regression checks remain outstanding. Do not treat this draft as satisfying the repository's all-affected-backends build gate.

## Extra Notes

### Contribution-guide status — incomplete

- [x] Searched open issues/PRs for overlapping RX580/gfx803 work before submission.
- [x] One platform-enablement change; independent optimizations excluded; feature opt-in.
- [x] Changed behavior and untested areas described with measured hardware scope.
- [x] Opened and linked feature request #2768 as requested by `AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] Build every affected backend before requesting maintainer review; only native gfx803 was built here.
- [ ] Demonstrate the default path remains byte-identical to the last release, as requested by `AGENTS.md`.

### Why draft

Unresolved historical model-logit differences prevent a numerical-equivalence claim. GPU fallback numerical qualification, full populated 262K context, sustained long-context thermals, MTP/speculative decoding, vision and other models/quantizations/cards are unverified. Synchronous staging sacrifices overlap. No performance gain is claimed for this patch, and results from the separately optimized local runtime are not attributed to it.

This is an experimental draft with contribution gates outstanding, not a request to merge as supported hardware.

title: Community benchmark: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Coder IQ1_M on a 5070ti laptop (12GB) GPU + 32 GB RAM
body:
Adds a community benchmark report for a laptop-class configuration: 12 GiB laptop GPU, 32 GB RAM,
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Coder IQ1_M, Strata 0.1.44.1 (296b59d2), low-RAM resident-expert mode.
Suite 1 (tools/strata_bench.py) plus power/thermal telemetry sampled every 2 s while it ran.
No engine code touched - report, raw results, telemetry and engine log only.

The short version: 20.5 tok/s decode in short chat (16.4-23.4), ~20 tok/s in a 6-turn agent session,
387 / 525 tok/s prompt at 4K / 16K, first token ~2.3 s. Decode is bounded by expert streaming
(53-63% expert-cache hit during decode) on this 30.5 GiB machine rather than by the GPU (56% average
utilization); 2x32 GB RAM is the upgrade that removes the penalty.

Report format follows the template in docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md.

---

# Community benchmark: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Coder IQ1_M on a 12 GB laptop GPU

Measured on 2026-10-16 by [Aoyi-Feng](https://github.com/Aoyi-Feng). A 32 GB machine cannot hold this
quant in RAM, so the experts stream from disk through the OS file cache; the limitation is memory
capacity, not the GPU.

**Summary.** A mid-range gaming laptop (RTX 5070 Ti Laptop 12 GB, 32 GB DDR5-5600, Ryzen 9
9955HX) runs the Coder IQ1_M quant of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next through Strata in low-RAM
resident-expert mode, because the experts do not fit in 32 GB of RAM. It works, and it is
usable for chat and agent work: **20.5 tok/s decode in short chat (16.4–23.4), ~20 tok/s in a
6-turn agent session**, with the first token in about **2.3 s**. Reading long prompts is fast
(**387 tok/s at 4K, 525 tok/s at 16K**); generating is the slow half, and it is bounded by
expert streaming from RAM/SSD (53–63 % expert-cache hit during decode), not by the GPU.
GPU utilization averaged 56 % while the CPU ran at 5.1 GHz and 88 °C, so the machine's CPU/IO
side, not the GPU, is what saturates. Same-model machines whose RAM holds all the experts
report roughly 90–117 tok/s, i.e. this configuration pays about a 4–5x penalty for the
missing RAM; 2 × 32 GB is the upgrade that removes it. Nothing here beats a hosted API on
speed — it is a private, offline, zero-marginal-cost setup that is usable, not fast.

## Hardware and software

- Laptop: MECHREVO JIAOLONG Series (16-inch class, AC power, hybrid iGPU)
- GPU and VRAM: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU, 12 GiB VRAM (12227 MiB); driver 615.78.08; VBIOS 98.05.31.00.59; power limit 140 W (default 65 W)
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX 16-core (16 cores, 32 threads, up to 5.39 GHz, AVX-512: avx512f/dq/bw/vl/ifma/vnni/bf16)
- RAM: 2 x 16 GiB Micron CT16G56C46S5.C8D, DDR5-5600, 2 x 1-rank, dual channel, non-ECC; installed 32 GB (30.5 GiB usable)
- Storage: model and packs on Samsung SSD 990 EVO Plus 2 TB (NVMe); second drive YMTC PC411 1 TB
- OS: Arch Linux, kernel 7.2.9-arch1-1; NVIDIA driver 615.78.08; CUDA toolkit 13.4 (V13.4.92, source build of the engine)
- PCIe link width/speed: not measured
- Strata: project 0.1.44.1, commit 296b59d2; engine 0.1.44.1

## Power and thermal control

- Power, fan and profile control: **TUXEDO Control Center** (`tccd.service`) on the shared Clevo/Uniwill barebone (`clevo_wmi`, `uniwill_wmi`, `tuxedo_io`, `tuxedo_nb02_nvidia_power_ctrl` loaded).
- Active profile: **`PERFORMANCE!!!`** — CPU governor `powersave` with energy-performance preference `balance_performance`, all 32 threads online, scaling 1.93–5.39 GHz; **fans forced on, 100 % minimum and maximum** (profile "Freezy").
- NVIDIA PowerCTRL is available on this unit: default TGP 65 W, maximum 140 W. The GPU drew 73 W on average and peaked at 134.5 W during the run, so the cap never bound.
- TCC itself reports CPU power draw as unavailable (`GetCpuPowerValuesJSON` -> `powerDraw: -1`) on this model, matching the missing k10temp/powercap energy counter.

## Power and thermals during the run

Sampled every 2 s with `nvidia-smi` plus the hwmon CPU sensors while the suite ran
(190 samples under load, GPU > 40 W); raw samples in `telemetry.csv`.

| Quantity | Average | Min | Max |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GPU power (W) | 72.9 | 41.1 | 134.5 |
| GPU SM clock (MHz) | 2259 | 1507 | 2797 |
| GPU temperature (C) | 67.6 | 44.0 | 76.0 |
| GPU utilization (%) | 55.8 | 0.0 | 100.0 |
| VRAM used (MiB) | 11657 | 11523 | 11714 |
| CPU temperature (C) | 87.6 | 69.1 | 93.6 |
| CPU clock (MHz) | 5100 | 3871 | 5391 |

- The GPU cap was set to 140 W; the run drew 73 W on average and peaked at 134.5 W, so the cap was not the binding limit at any point.
- CPU package power is not readable on this platform (`k10temp`/`powercap` expose no energy counter for the Ryzen 9 9955HX here), so CPU is reported as clock and temperature only.
- CPU ran at 5.10 GHz average and up to 93.6 C, i.e. the CPU expert pool was the busiest part of the machine while decode was running.

## Model and configuration

- Model repository and revision: `ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-Coder-GGUF` at `5348543e0147355ac9cbcb031184a3546350988e` (quant files). MTP block taken from the BF16 checkpoint `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` at `de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540` (31 tensors, 5.21 GB).
- Quantization: `IQ1_M` of the Coder family (GSQ-RCO). GGUF filenames: `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ1_M-00001-of-00002.gguf` (29,608,446,496 B) and `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ1_M-00002-of-00002.gguf` (28,800,138,432 B).
- Vision encoder: none (text-only model; `--vision` not used).
- Custom packs/profiles: preprocessed expert pack `coder-iq1_m` (`tools/iq_pack.py`, native experts sha256 `9ace1b92e1fe12595de469409e69dd52c8d5418c7981c405d9a51aa9d574dd3b`, 25,146,163,200 B); expert cache profile `expert-profile-coder.bin`, pre-loaded with `--expert-profile`.
- Context: 32768 tokens; parallel slots: 1; KV storage `int8`; KV streaming not used (`--kv-resident` off, whole KV in VRAM).
- Cache / low-RAM: `--expert-cache auto` (settles on 1620 resident experts, 3.12 GiB of VRAM), `--prefill auto`, `--resident-experts` (low-RAM mode).
- MTP: `--mtp <mtp dir>` with `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5` (speculative decoding active; draft acceptance 0.73-0.78 in the short-chat runs).
- Reasoning/thinking: off for the suite. Sampling: greedy (temperature 0). Calibration (`--calibrate`): not run. Experimental speed projection: not enabled.
- Settings are the install's own configuration, unchanged - no tuning was applied for this report.

```text
strata --pack coder-iq1_m --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ1_M-00001-of-00002.gguf --ple-gguf Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ1_M-00002-of-00002.gguf --expert-profile expert-profile-coder.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp rt --max-context 32768 --kv int8 --resident-experts
```

## Method

Run by `python tools/strata_bench.py` against the HTTP API of a Strata server (started by the benchmark from the install configuration); model loading is not timed. One warm-up chat and a 1K prompt are discarded first. Every prompt starts with a unique tag, so the conversation cache cannot help the fresh-prompt tests.

- short chat: the three questions of `tools/ab_engine.py`, up to 100 new tokens, 3 runs
- 4K / 16K prompts: generated word lists sized by a calibration request, 24 new tokens, 3 fresh prompts each
- agent session: system prompt and four tools, then 5 turns that each add about 1500 words of a project file and continue from the model's own earlier answers (the way agent clients resend a conversation), 64 new tokens per turn, 3 sessions; the cache numbers come from the answer's usage (`cached_tokens`) and timings (`prompt_n`)
- concurrency (when run): N requests sent at the same moment, total tokens over the wall time of the burst, latency over all requests

## Results

| Configuration | Actual prompt tokens | Reused tokens | Generated tokens | Runs | Prompt tok/s median and range | Decode tok/s median and range | TTFT seconds median and range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| short chat | 46 (43-51) | 0 | 100 (100-100) | 9 | not measured | 20.5 (16.4-23.4) | 2.31 (1.90-2.65) |
| 4K prompt, fresh | 4019 (4019-4019) | 0 (0-0) | 24 cap | 3 | 387.1 (382.0-392.8) | not measured | 10.44 (10.28-10.58) |
| 16K prompt, fresh | 16058 (16058-16058) | 0 (0-0) | 24 cap | 3 | 525.3 (520.9-529.4) | not measured | 30.63 (30.39-30.88) |
| agent session, follow-up turns | 14552 (14467-14580) at the last turn | see below | up to 64 | 3 | see below | 20.1 (11.8-22.6) | 10.16 (9.36-11.27) |

Ranges are the lowest and highest of the runs; `Runs` counts requests that returned a token.

### Agent session (conversation cache)

Cache hit over the follow-up turns: 68.7 % (68.5-68.8); earlier-turn tokens read again per session: 4 (4-74) (earlier turns that the cache did not hold; the 13729 (13727-13730) new tokens of the files are read once); first turn (nothing cached) first token: 7.78 s (7.74-8.22).

| Turn (run 1) | Prompt tokens | Reused | Read | Prompt tok/s | First token (s) | Decode tok/s |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 609 | 0 | 609 | 75.4 | 8.221 | 13.7 |
| 1 | 3755 | 632 | 3123 | 284.4 | 11.214 | 14.2 |
| 2 | 5288 | 3819 | 1469 | 157.2 | 9.514 | 16.9 |
| 3 | 8700 | 5320 | 3380 | 306.4 | 11.269 | 17.0 |
| 4 | 11626 | 8763 | 2863 | 275.9 | 10.878 | 21.4 |
| 5 | 14552 | 11653 | 2899 | 275.2 | 10.689 | 20.4 |

Per-request data: `results.json`. Engine log lines from the start: `engine-log-excerpt.txt` (when this run started the server).

## Correctness and limitations

Not measured: this is a speed suite - no correctness, needle-recall or quality checks were run.
The conversation uses the model's own replies, so token counts differ a little between runs.

The engine states the limitation itself at startup:

```text
WARNING: the resident RAM mode does not fit (FileExpertSource: resident complement 20.30 GiB
exceeds available RAM (2.97 GiB) minus the 4 GiB safety headroom ... the experts the GPU does not
hold are read from the model folder through the OS file cache (--mmap-experts), which is slower
when the RAM cannot keep them
```

- Repeated runs on this machine measured 14-20 tok/s decode for the same configuration (cold
  page cache at the low end, warm at the high end); the settle point in this report is the warm one.
- Power and thermals were sampled during this run and are reported above; CPU package power is
  `not measured` (unreadable on this platform, see above).
- Total time of the suite: 430 s.
- Not tested: other quantizations, larger contexts, concurrency (`--clients`), KV streaming, and
  the same model on a machine whose RAM holds the resident complement.

title: sycl: STRATA_QFUSE - commit one-token rounds (the commit skipped them, so QFUSE gave wrong output)
body:
## sycl: STRATA_QFUSE - commit one-token rounds (the commit skipped them, so QFUSE gave wrong output)

record_window does not self-commit a one-token window under STRATA_QFUSE (`!g_qfuse()` in its self_commit), but
Verifier::commit skipped the commit graph for every one-token window whenever one_token_self_commit() is on, so with
QFUSE those rounds never advanced the GDN state: wrong tokens. commit() now uses the same condition. Default path
(QFUSE off) unchanged.

A770, Coder IQ1_M, 8K code prompt, STRATA_QFUSE=1, 3 pairs: output is now the reference tokens (before the fix it
diverged); no speed change, QFUSE stays opt-in.

The CUDA/HIP engine looks to have the same mismatch: `src/core/verify.cpp` line 879 (record_window) has `!g_qfuse()` in its self-commit condition, but `Verifier::commit` (line 2655) does not. QFUSE was built on HIP, where the one-token self-commit is off, so it did not show there. I could not build or test CUDA here, so this PR only changes the SYCL port.

title: sycl: STRATA_RESIDENT_TOUCH=1 - re-touch the pinned resident experts after reclaim (xe shrinker backs them up to shmem)
body:
## sycl: STRATA_RESIDENT_TOUCH=1 - re-touch the pinned resident experts after reclaim (xe shrinker backs them up to shmem)

On an A770 under the xe driver with swap on, the decode CPU pool ran at 20-22 GB/s in some runs and ~30 in others
(decode ~10% apart). Root cause: the 28 GB load drives memory reclaim through to the prompt; reclaim runs the xe
shrinker (xe_shrinker_scan -> xe_bo_shrink -> ttm_backup, which only acts while free swap exists), and it backs the
idle pinned host chunks of the resident expert copy up to shmem. The pool then restores them one major fault at a
time during decode: 17-65K major faults / 2 s, on /dev/dri/renderD128 (perf -e major-faults).

Opt-in keeper thread: it watches /proc/vmstat (pgscan_kswapd + pgscan_direct); once reclaim has been quiet for 2 s after
a burst, it reads one byte of every 4 KiB page of the pinned chunks on 4 threads, so the restore is paid then rather
than inside the pool. Joined in close(). Default off: unchanged behaviour. Builds on the chunked pinned copy (#2485).

A770, Ryzen 7 3800X, 30 GB RAM + swap, Coder IQ1_M, 8K code prompt, 3 pairs: decode-phase major faults 17-65K ->
8-1.4K / 2 s, pool 20.4 -> 27.0 GB/s, decode 34.68 -> 37.59 tok/s (+8.4%), VRAM-tier refill unchanged, reference
tokens. Prefill 785 -> 743 tok/s (-5.4%) in that bench, where the prompt starts right after the load and the touch
(2-4 s) overlaps it; a server's prompts come later. Alternatives without it: no swap, or STRATA_RESIDENT_CHUNKED=0.

Stacked on #2485 (the chunked pinned copy this touches); the diff to review is the top commit. If you prefer, this can be an issue first: the root cause is a driver / swap interaction, and turning swap off also fixes it.

with none. Same kernels on one stream: the same bits.

title: sycl: Q4_K/Q5_K wide GEMV - pass dp4a's ones word as a value IGC cannot fold (it expanded each dp4a into ~24 ops)
body:
## sycl: Q4_K/Q5_K wide GEMV - pass dp4a's ones word as a value IGC cannot fold (it expanded each dp4a into ~24 ops)

The wide (multi-column) Q4_K / Q5_K kernels take the activation sum of the min term as dp4a(0x01010101, u). With the
literal constant IGC (oneAPI 2026.1, DG2) does not emit a dp4a: it expands each one into byte movs + add3 (16 movs +
8 add3 per SIMD16 half), ~60% of the 4-column kernel's integer instructions (offline ISA, ocloc acm-g10: 652 -> 320
integer instructions per loop iteration). For 2+ columns the kernels now compute one4 = 0x01010101 + (n_in >> 31),
which is 0x01010101 for every n_in >= 0 but a value the compiler cannot prove, and pass it down (WideIQ4XS takes the
same argument). One column keeps the literal: there it measured 4-14% faster. The same integers, so the same bits.

A770 dense_bench on main, the same output hash in every row:
- Q4_K: 1 column -0.2..+5%; 2 columns +6..+12%; 3 columns +10..+16%; 4 columns +12..+18% (e.g. QSA q 145.9 -> 171.7
  GB/s, out-proj 139.4 -> 164.9).
- Q5_K: 1 column the same (the small k/v and out-proj rows swing +-15% run to run on both builds); 2 columns -2..+3%,
  k/v -11%; 3 columns +10..+19%; 4 columns +3..+13% (QSA q 162.3 -> 183.1).
The engine's verify window runs mostly 4 columns. Engine on a fork tree (with #2207; Coder IQ1_M, 8K code prompt,
3 pairs): GPU wait 32.07 / 31.93 / 31.94 -> 31.85 / 31.63 / 31.59 ms a round, reference tokens.

title: sycl: Q6_K GEMV - subtract 32 from the 6-bit values with three integer ops instead of a saturating byte subtract
body:
## sycl: Q6_K GEMV - subtract 32 from the 6-bit values with three integer ops instead of a saturating byte subtract

The Q6_K dot paths took 32 from each 6-bit weight with dpct::vectorized_binary<char4>(v, 0x20202020, sub_sat()), which
unpacks and saturates byte by byte. The bytes are 0..63, so the result never leaves int8 range: q6_sub32(v) =
((v | 0x80808080) - 0x20202020) ^ 0x80808080 gives the same bytes (bit 7 set keeps one byte's subtract from borrowing
from the next; flipping it back restores the sign). Five sites. Hardware counters showed these kernels integer-ALU
bound, not memory bound.

A770 dense_bench, same output hashes: Q6_K GDN qkv 4 columns 239 -> 289 GB/s, 1 column 321 -> 366; QSA q 4 columns
242 -> 293; k/v 72 -> 94. Engine (Coder IQ1_M, 8K code prompt, 3 pairs): GPU wait 33.4-33.8 -> 32.0-32.2 ms a round,
decode 39.1 / 39.2 -> 39.6 / 39.4 tok/s, the same tokens. Measured on a tree that also has #2207 (1-column MMVQ in
large GRF). All devices: the arithmetic is the same integers.

Re-measured on main (A770 dense_bench, this branch vs main, the same hash in every row): Q6_K GDN qkv 4 columns
94.2 -> 159.6 GB/s, 3 columns 96.6 -> 197.1, 1 column 288.9 -> 310.5; QSA q 4 columns 92.2 -> 164.9; GDN z 4 columns

title: cpu pool: STRATA_POOL_FUSED=1 - a native layer's gate/up and down without the barrier between them; pool_layer_bench
body:
## CPU pool: a native layer's gate/up and down without the barrier between them (STRATA_POOL_FUSED=1, opt-in)

`run_split_multi_native` runs a layer's CPU experts in two phases: every expert's gate/up rows across all threads,
then the host quantizes the intermediates, then every expert's down rows. With `STRATA_POOL_FUSED=1` the pool runs a
new task mode instead (mode 7):

- each expert's gate/up rows are cut into 8 parts and its down rows into 4;
- the thread that finishes an expert's last gate/up part quantizes that expert's intermediate and sets a flag;
- that expert's down parts wait only for its own flag, not for the whole layer;
- the down parts are queued one expert behind the gate/up parts (`STRATA_POOL_FUSED_LAG`, default 1), so the flag is
  usually already set when a thread claims one.

Every row goes through the same `native_gu_rows` / `native_down_rows` call as before, only cut differently, and a row's
result does not depend on the cut. The output is the same bit for bit (the hash below). Q2_0 layers keep the two phases.
The existing claim protocol is unchanged. Off by default: it is measured on one CPU so far.

### Why

On a Ryzen 7 3800X (Zen 2, AVX2, 2 x DDR4-3200) the two halves of an expert are limited by different things.
`kq_cpu_bench` (fixed in #2750), 7 threads on cores 1-7, 1 token:

| | GB/s |
| --- | ---: |
| IQ2_S gate/up only | 27.3 |
| IQ3_XXS gate/up only | 24.7 |
| IQ4_NL down rows, inside the pool | ~39 |
| Gate/up and down interleaved per thread (IQ2_S / IQ3_XXS / IQ3_S pair) | 34.5 / 31.7 / 32.7 |

Gate/up is compute-bound on the i-quant decode (one core: 4-4.6 GB/s, IPC 3.3-3.7 under `perf`), and the down rows run
at RAM speed. With the barrier, each phase leaves the other's resource idle. Using the SMT siblings as well gave
0-8% (14 threads), so more threads are not the fix.

### Measured

`pool_layer_bench` (new, in this PR) drives the real `ExpertPool` the way decode does: one layer's CPU experts per call,
6 or 7 distinct experts, a quarter of them with 2 tokens, drawn from 4 GB of blobs. Pinned like the engine (7 workers
on cores 1-7, the host on core 0). It prints a hash of every output over 300 fixed layers. Ryzen 7 3800X, nothing else
running:

| Gate/up / down | Two phases | Fused | Output hash, both |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| IQ2_S / IQ4_NL | 0.420 ms a layer | 0.387 (-8%) | `1c64c600a48b3217` |
| IQ3_XXS / IQ4_NL | 0.496-0.504 | 0.456 (-9%) | `fc3f11e3f60dea42` |
| IQ3_S / IQ4_NL | 0.525-0.526 | 0.469 (-11%) | `2f5f9c94d2c599c5` |

Lag 2 measured the same or 1-2% slower; 8/4 parts were as good as 12/6 and better than 4/2 or 16/8.

In the engine (SYCL build on an Arc A770, Coder IQ1_M, 8K code prompt, 3 same-day pairs, reference tokens in all six
runs) the CPU pool call went from 25.45 / 21.83 / 21.62 to 23.01 / 20.42 / 20.50 ms a round and decode from 37.57 /
39.97 / 40.23 to 38.16 / 41.07 / 41.04 tok/s (+2.1%). That A/B also turned on a separate change to the single-token
IQ2_S gate/up rows (+7% on that kernel alone), which is not in this PR, so the engine numbers are not this change alone.

### Also

- `generate.cpp` (CUDA/HIP and SYCL): one stats line saying how many layer calls ran fused, because their down rows
  are then counted in the "gate/up" column.
- `pool_layer_bench` in both CMake files.

Not measured: AVX-512 CPUs, Intel hybrid CPUs, CUDA/HIP engine runs. The CUDA/HIP `generate.cpp` line is the same
three lines as the SYCL one; I could not compile the CUDA build here. `STRATA_POOL_FUSED_PARTS=<gu>,<down>` overrides
the cut for testing.

title: sycl: use packed word expansion for Q2_0 expert down on Battlemage
body:
## Summary

Replace the byte-permute/codebook expansion in Q2_0 expert down with exact packed-word shifts, masks and arithmetic. The decoder stays in the existing Q2_0 format specialization and is selected at compile time for the eligible down path. The existing INT8 DP4A operations, scales, FP32 accumulation and reduction order are preserved. On B70, warmed client TPOT improves by 4.18–4.48%; TTFT has no clear improvement.

The change is confined to `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.dp.cpp`; decoder helpers remain private to that translation unit. It follows upstream `intel_gpu_gen` / `IntelGpuGen::Battlemage` classification and the existing 8-lane, non-legacy, non-split dispatch conditions. There is no model-specific shape whitelist. Other formats and GU keep their existing algorithms and dispatch. Non-Battlemage devices retain the original decoder dispatch; eligible Q2 calls still incur the added cached host device check.

## Dispatch control

`STRATA_SYCL_Q2_WORD_EXPAND` controls the entire optimization:

- Unset (default) or `1`: use word expansion when the existing dispatch and Battlemage guards allow it.
- `0`: use the original Q2_0 down path. There are no child switches.

Set it before starting the engine and restart after changing it; the value is cached on first use. Normal operation needs no environment-variable setting.

## B70 validation

Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB, Linux/xe; `intel/omix:0.4.0-devel-ubuntu24.04`, oneAPI DPC++ 2026.1.1, compute runtime 26.31.39395.13, Level Zero loader 1.32.0. Container limits: 128 GiB RAM and 16 CPU quota. Builds and GPU tests ran inside the container, with AOT `bmg-g31`.

- Release engine build and `native_grouped_parity` pass with default and fallback dispatch.
- All 65,536 packed 16-bit words decode byte-identically to the original GPU implementation and CPU codebook; upper-bit handling is also checked.
- Real-GGUF expert tests pass byte-exact down and full-output comparisons with five activation patterns, T=1–8, GU16/GU22, graph replay, mixed host/device weights, empty groups and output guards.
- In the endpoint measurements below, corresponding output token IDs match across all arms, including warmups. Actual speculative work and cache capacity match between arms.

Timings and endpoint identity checks below were collected at `fe47faa548ea6aba50101987bc255b5ed8eccd03`, before the source cleanup. The current revision rebuilds the engine and parity targets and repeats decoder/down correctness validation. For these B70 AOT builds, executed kernel instructions and resource settings match the measured version; differences are limited to naming and non-executed markers after the final EOT. No new latency run is claimed.

## End-to-end performance

Baseline and frontend: upstream `296b59d2f73c8f04a805df29c2fa97655adace78`. The candidate adds only this Q2 down change and uses its default production dispatch.

Each input length uses baseline / candidate / baseline, restarting the engine for each arm. Exclude one short request and three full-input warmups, then measure three requests per arm. Changes average the three request-wise percentage changes relative to the mean of the matching before/after baseline samples; negative means faster. All three TPOT pairs improve at every input length.

TTFT is request send to the first nonempty SSE text arrival. TPOT is the first-to-last nonempty SSE arrival interval divided by generated tokens minus one. These are warmed, post-readiness measurements; the host page cache was not flushed.

| Input / output tokens | TTFT baseline → default (s) | Change | TPOT baseline → default (ms/token) | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096 / 128 | 3.500022 → 3.495323 | -0.134% | 14.552169 → 13.920341 | -4.345% |
| 8192 / 256 | 7.094365 → 7.104670 | +0.145% | 13.751785 → 13.134993 | -4.477% |
| 32768 / 256 | 30.016363 → 30.018130 | +0.006% | 14.223863 → 13.630544 | -4.183% |

Baseline before/after TPOT drift: +0.034%, +0.043%, -0.003%; TTFT drift: -0.177%, +0.362%, +0.017%, respectively.

<details>
<summary>Model and fixed configuration</summary>

- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO IQ2_XS, model revision `ed59f92082b1e93c0e96d60a8b11aab089b52f09`. Its routed expert down matrices use Q2_0.
- Greedy seed 42, thinking off; INT8 KV, max context 131072, resident KV 32768; prompt cache off.
- `--expert-cache auto`, reserve 1536 MiB, mirror budget 32768 MiB; auto prefill, no prefill borrowing.
- spec4 / min-p0.5 / suffix3; adapt-every8 / decay1. Actual windows/offered/accepted match for corresponding measured requests.
- Actual capacity in every arm: 17758 resident expert slots and 6818 mirrored experts, approximately 9.17 GiB. The 32768 MiB mirror setting is a budget.
- Common environment: `STRATA_VERIFY_DEVICE_PLAN=1`, `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=1`, `STRATA_STAGER_THREADS=12`, `STRATA_MIRROR_MIB=32768`, `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING=1`, `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:gpu`, `SYCL_CACHE_PERSISTENT=0`. Normal timing runs have no profiler.

</details>

## Down microbenchmark

Real GGUF weights at the model's down dimensions, K=640 and N=2560, with deterministic synthetic activations and fixed expert-group replay inputs. T is the token-window size. The probe directly selects the original or word-expansion down implementation in the same binary; end-to-end results above use production dispatch.

Three measured samples per baseline / candidate / baseline arm; each sample excludes at least 2 seconds/1000 calls of warmup and measures at least 3 seconds/2000 calls. These are steady graph-replay batched wall times including host submission and the final queue wait. They are not isolated GPU instruction latency, and their percentages are not added to endpoint gains.

| K / N / T | Original (µs) | Word expansion (µs) | Change | Baseline drift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 640 / 2560 / 1 | 40.445 | 22.696 | -43.883% | -0.180% |
| 640 / 2560 / 2 | 55.619 | 32.673 | -41.255% | +0.024% |
| 640 / 2560 / 3 | 78.320 | 45.022 | -42.515% | +0.011% |
| 640 / 2560 / 4 | 81.888 | 44.822 | -45.264% | -0.016% |

All three corresponding samples improve for each listed row. These measurements and current validation cover single-card B70 AOT; Windows, multi-GPU operation and JIT paths on other devices were not tested.

title: Qwen3.6: opt-in int8 K/V cache and single staging buffer
body:
## Title
Qwen3.6: opt-in int8 K/V cache and single staging buffer

## Summary
Two opt-in improvements to the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B own-engine path, both off by default so the default path stays byte-identical to the last release:

1. **int8 (q8_0) K/V cache** behind `--kv int8` — roughly 4x smaller K/V cache (~44 KiB/token fp32 -> ~11 KiB/token int8), so an 8 GB card doubles its context (16K -> 32K).
2. **Single staging buffer** behind `STRATA_Q36_SINGLE_STAGE=1` — halves the prompt-streaming staging VRAM (one buffer instead of two double-buffered).

## What changed
- `CMakeLists.txt` — build wiring for the new q8_0 K/V kernels.
- `include/strata/kernels/q36_kv_q8.hpp` — new int8 K/V kernel interface.
- `src/kernels/cuda/q36_kv_q8.cu` — CUDA q8_0 K/V cache kernel.
- `src/kernels/q36_kv_q8_parity.cpp` — CPU reference kernel for parity testing.
- `src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu` — the `--kv int8` engine path; `STRATA_Q36_SINGLE_STAGE=1` (single staging buffer), numeric `STRATA_Q36_NO_MMQ`, `STRATA_Q36_PLACE_DEBUG`, and an attention-scores-buffer shrink (256 -> 64 MB) so staging placement still succeeds on tight VRAM.
- `docs/Q36_INT8_KV.md` — design note with the measured numbers.
- `docs/DETAILS.md` — links the new section into the table of contents.

## Extra Notes
- `--kv int8` defaults to `--kv fp32`, which is byte-identical to the previous release.
- Benchmarks were measured on an RTX 4060 (8 GB); see `docs/Q36_INT8_KV.md`.

title: Add a Nemotron-H MoE engine path (Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B)
body: ## What this adds An engine path for **NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B** (unsloth's GGUFs, architecture `nemotron_h_moe`): `src/nemotron_h`, which `strata` switches to from the file's architecture the same way it switches to Qwen3.6's path, plus a standalone `strata-nh`. Text, images (GENI) and the GGUF's MTP block. - **Model**: 88 flat sublayers — 40 Mamba-2 mixers (causal conv + bias + SiLU, selective scan, SiLU(z)-gated group RMS norm), 8 NoPE GQA attention mixers (32 query / 2 KV heads, head 128, FP16 KV cache), 40 latent MoE blocks (sigmoid router with selection bias, top-22 of 512, normalized ×5; relu² experts without a gate in the 1024-wide latent; shared expert), the MTP block (`blk.88`) for drafts. - **Hybrid experts** (78 GB of experts, always hybrid): per-layer VRAM slots that follow the routing; a batch of ≤ `--hybrid-rows` rows splits resident experts (GPU) and the rest (CPU, ggml-cpu `vec_dot`); bigger prompt chunks stream non-resident experts through a VRAM ring into per-expert FP16 GEMMs. - **Taken over from Flash-Next's design**: a pinned expert arena on 2 MiB pages (THP + `cudaHostRegister`, falls back to `cudaHostAlloc`, then to the mapped file), an expert profile (`--expert-profile` / `--expert-profile-save`), the adaptive tier, the PCIe share of misses (`--pcie-frac`) and next-layer prefetch (`--prefetch`) — both opt-in —, and turn checkpoints of the recurrent state (a regenerated / edited last answer reads only the rest of its prompt). - **Kernels**: `native_expert_grouped_relu2` / `native_expert_layout_ungated` in `iq_kernels.cu` — new, opt-in functions; the gated path is not touched. - **Tokenizer / server**: the `tekken` pre-tokenizer with `ignore_merges` in `tools/strata_tokenizer.py`; `serve/server.py` reads `pre` from the pack's `tokenizer.json`, keeps a stop marker only when it is one token (this vocabulary has no `<|endoftext|>`, whose pieces would have stopped every reply at `<`), writes ` ×n ` for this model's pictures, and knows the family name. - **strata-vision**: a model without M-RoPE gets a 1-D grid (needs a llama.cpp with `PROJECTOR_TYPE_NEMOTRON_OMNI`, upstream since PR #30520). - **Tools**: `tools/nemotron_h/nh_llama_dump.cpp` (llama.cpp side, `-cmoe`, sublayer dumps) + `parity.py`; `nh_cpu_test`, `nh_cpu_bench`; `serve/test_nemotron_serve.py`. - Design and every number: `docs/NEMOTRON_H.md`. ## What it leaves alone Flash-Next's and Qwen3.6's engine paths and defaults. The reader's 64-entry array cap is not changed (this path takes the sublayer kinds from the tensors present). Qwen tokenization (`qwen35` stays the default `pre`). The new CMake targets build only with `STRATA_NATIVE_EXPERTS` and not on HIP. ## Tests Measured on one PC: RTX 3090 24 GB, i7-7800X (6 cores, AVX-512), 95 GiB DDR4-2133, `UD-Q4_K_XL`; llama.cpp 0.7.0 (`620d2225c`) as the reference. - **Parity with llama.cpp** (`tools/nemotron_h/parity.py`, teacher-forced): 5 chat prompts × 32 steps — first token matched 5/5; answers only (122 steps up to `<|im_end|>`): mean KL 0.00106, median 1.5e-5, top-1 0.992. Final build (arena + profile, 2 chat prompts + a 981-token one): answers-only KL 0.00124, top-1 0.984. With the PCIe share 0.6 + prefetch 16 (82% of routed entries on the GPU): KL 0.00279, top-1 0.979. - **Long prompt / streamed path** (981 tokens): KL 0.00328 vs llama.cpp CUDA while llama.cpp's own CPU backend is at 0.00277; per-sublayer drift equals llama.cpp CPU's (layer 40: 0.176 vs 0.174, layer 80: 0.311 vs 0.302). - **MTP**: greedy text identical with 2 and 3 drafts (96 tokens), 85% / 82% accepted; no speedup on this PC (verify windows route ~3× the distinct experts, mostly CPU misses), so the docs recommend `--mtp 0` there. - **CPU experts** vs a dequantized f64 reference (`nh_cpu_test`, all 41 MoE layers, Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K/Q8_0 × Q5_0/IQ4_NL/Q8_0): worst relative error 1.2% (activation rounding). - **Tokenizer** vs HF `tokenizers` on the model's `tokenizer.json`: 23 strings (chat markers, tool-call XML, Cyrillic, CJK, emoji, combining marks) identical; round trip 16/16. - **Server** (`serve/server.py --engine strata`): plain answer, thinking with `reasoning_content` split, a tool call (`get_weather {"city":"Kyiv"}`, `finish_reason: tool_calls`), an image (shapes, colours and text described correctly; 300 image tokens, 59 ms on the GPU encoder), streaming, a second turn reusing the first (45 cached tokens), a regenerated answer restoring its turn checkpoint (prompt 88 ms instead of 2011 ms, same text). - **Unit tests**: `serve.test_server` 314/314; `serve.test_family_name`, `serve.test_nemotron_serve`, `serve.test_images`, `serve.test_vision_busy`, `serve.test_detok`, `serve.test_reasoning_tools`, `serve.test_parser_track` 63 OK (5 skipped); `tools/test_setup_choices.py` OK. - **Speed** (`strata-nh --bench-pp 2048 --bench-tg 32`): prompt 337–350 tok/s, decode 12.2–13.1 tok/s; through the server 246 tok/s prompt (2795 tokens), 11.2 tok/s decode. 2 MiB arena pages vs 4 KiB: decode 11.75 vs 9.16 tok/s at equal slots; profile on a held-out prompt: 13.48 vs 11.83 tok/s (VRAM share 34% vs 16%). - **Builds**: CUDA 13.4, sm_86 (`strata`, `strata-nh`, `nh_cpu_test`, `nh_cpu_bench`, `strata-vision` against llama.cpp 0.7.0). ## Not tested / not done HIP and SYCL builds (`iq_kernels.cu`'s new functions follow the file's HIP conventions but were not compiled for HIP); other GPUs and CPUs; MMQ for the prompt's experts; video input; a setup entry. A server left running for several hours stopped once; the cause was not investigated yet.

## What changed

- Add a dated report with physical/engine GPU mapping, observed PCIe widths, model/build/configuration details and limitations.
- Include all 22 unique earlier throughput observations and a summary CSV; the final 6144/default-sampling/swap-blocked group has three runs and reports median/range.

The throughput measurements are October 14–15; the agent episodes are October 16. All earlier conditions and failures are retained. Earlier groups differ in sampling, reserve and swap policy and are not presented as a single controlled A/B.

The custom agent result is not an official BFCL/tau/Terminal-Bench/Hermes score. The actual Hermes application was not invoked. The report discloses the scope-ambiguous quote task, equivalent-representation grading audit, all original verdicts, and the empty-final-response case.

The separately linked GLM comparison uses Project Maya 1.1.11 / Maya-M. It compares the two deployed stacks, with different native quantization/KV/MTP settings, rather than isolating engine or base-model quality.

title: batch-mtp: split the solo MTP budget across batch slots — multi-GPU multi-stream tuning (agent concurrency)
body:
## What

Two commits on `--batch-mtp` plus one Monitor-tab improvement, aimed at **multi-GPU (layer split) + multi-stream serving**:

1. **`batch-mtp`: proposals per slot = ceil(MTP budget / batch)** — the solo MTP budget is split across the batch slots (spec 3 + 2 slots → 2 drafts each; 3+ slots → 1). Chain-verified keep, `1 + D` rows per slot per window, and a startup note about the extra draft K/V/graph memory.
2. **`batch-mtp`: D uses the MTP budget as given** (`--mtp-max-t`, else `--spec`) — not the suffix-draft `spec+2` bump. The bumped spec is the verifier's window, not the drafter's budget; without this, `--spec 3 --batch 2` silently drafts 3 per slot.
3. **monitor: show every parallel request** — the Model state card renders one row per batch slot (reading progress / decoding tokens+tok/s+elapsed / idle-held tokens), plus solo-path, waiting-for-slot and queued counts. The single progress bar only ever showed the newest request.

## Why — the real-world scenario

This is a tuning pass for **agent workloads**: connecting a local Strata endpoint to agent frameworks (Hermes, Claude Code, etc.). A large task gets split into **sub-agents that fire concurrent requests**; with the stock configuration those requests queue serially, and once `--batch` is on, `--batch-mtp` on a layer split is gated off (helper expert caches) and each slot drafts only 1 proposal per window — so MTP is effectively **disabled exactly when concurrency arrives**, and per-stream decode collapses (measured: 1 stream 74 tok/s → 2 streams ~21 tok/s each on the pipelined default).

The commits make the MTP budget follow the concurrency: 1 stream keeps the full solo budget (solo path, untouched), 2 streams split it 2+2, 3 streams run 1 each inside the `kVerifyMaxT = 8` window. This is the 2×RTX 3090 / ≤3 streams corner of the design space (the window cap makes D>1 at 3 streams impossible: 3 slots × 3 rows = 9 > 8, and raising the cap touches `GMAX` in the grouped-MoE kernels).

## Measured on 2× RTX 3090, layer split auto, IQ3_S, `--batch 3 --batch-mtp --batch-groups 1 --spec 3 --vram-reserve-mib 1024`

Natural-stop long-form requests (~1500-token answers, `finish=stop`, not `length`-truncated):

| streams | before (pipelined default) | after (batch-mtp serial windows) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 74.1 tok/s (solo) | 74.1 tok/s (solo path unchanged) |
| 2 | ~42 agg | **66.4 agg** (31.8 / 36.8 per stream) |
| 3 | — | **88.8 agg** (30.0 / 29.0 / 34.3) |

Official `tools/strata_bench.py --clients 3` on the production instance: **82.7 tok/s aggregate, 0 errors**, TTFT p50 1.06 s / p95 1.74 s. MTP acceptance rose 59.8% → 67.2% (spec 4 → 3). Single-stream costs are within noise (agent decode 109.5 → 107.0); 4K prefill −9% is the 3 slot sessions' 1.37 GiB expert-cache tax, which is the documented `--batch` cost.

D=2 at 2 streams was measured four independent times: **net zero** (acceptance decay cancels the extra draft cost) — the split formula keeps D=2 available where it helps (single-GPU builds, higher acceptance) and clamps to 1 at 3+ streams where the window demands it.

## Notes

- No behaviour change without `--batch-mtp`; the solo path is untouched.
- The window-cap clamp (`D ≤ 8//batch − 1`) is deliberate: 3 streams × D=2 overflows `kVerifyMaxT` and measured −19% (window rotation starves the third slot).
- The Monitor rows read the existing `/metrics` `live.slots` (`slots_view()`); pure frontend, no engine ABI change.

title: bench: community report - GTX 1080 Ti (sm_61): eight-knob screen, long context 32K-250K with needles, 1h soak
body:
A results-only report from the same rig as #2642 / #2684 (GTX 1080 Ti 11 GB, 2x Xeon E5-2696 v4, IQ3_S, engine 0.1.44.1, CUDA 12.8): eight opt-in knobs screened one at a time (base = #2695's `STRATA_DENSE_F32=1`), the winners stacked, then long-context behavior with needle checks and a one-hour soak. It also answers the TEST_REQUESTS row "a long soak (an hour or more of back-to-back requests) ... on a resident setup" (see below).

## What it adds

`bench/results/2026-10-16-community-gtx-1080-ti-tuning-soak-longctx/`: pair transcripts with the engine's own lines and quality probes, `needles-lg-grow2.json`, `soak-results.json` (237 rows), the runner scripts (incl. the root-level cpuset cgroup wrapper this rig needs for node binding), and a README in the report format. One list entry in `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`.

## What it leaves alone

No engine, setup or tool change; no default is flipped. `docs/OLDER_GPUS.md` is untouched here (#2695 already edits it).

## The screen (medians of 3 requests per arm; decode verdicts only when all 3 moved together)

| Knob | prompt short/long | decode short/long | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--mtp-hnorm stream` | unchanged | **+28% / +28%** | adopted (#2227 replicated on sm_61, bigger than sm_89) |
| `--ple-io ram` | unchanged | **+9% / +12%** | adopted (28.8 GB PLE table; mlock refused by ulimit, pages faulted in) |
| no `--pcie-frac` (auto picks 0.32) | unchanged | **+12% / +20%** | adopted (#2498's 0.00 recommendation measured slower here too) |
| `--adapt-async 1` | unchanged | +7% / +2% | not adopted (weak) |
| `--kv k8v4` | unchanged | unchanged | not adopted |
| `--kv-grow` + `--expert-profile-save` | unchanged | unchanged | profile-save kept; `--kv-grow` dropped (negative at long context too) |
| `--aux-cpus auto` | unchanged | **−23% / −15%** | rejected |
| `--batch 2 --batch-mtp` | **−45%** | −20% | rejected (2-client burst: 40.6 s queued vs 71.4 s batched; #2126's startup hang did not reproduce) |
| the three adopted together | short +3% | **+10% / +16%** | confirmed |

## Long context and soak

32K/128K/250K fresh prompts: 415 / 372 / 333 prompt tok/s, decode flat with depth (28-32). KV streaming at 128K served 88.27% of 431,340 block reads from VRAM (203.9 MiB from RAM). Needles at depth 50: **FOUND at 124,782 and at 251,546 tokens** — first correctness evidence at the far end of the 262K window on an 11 GB Pascal card with `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`. `--kv-grow` was negative at every depth for these fresh prompts (its #2650 benefit is drift inside one growing session). Soak: 60 min, 237 requests, **0 failures, no drift**, end temp 73 C without throttling.

## Limitations

One round per knob (decode is noisy on this rig, ±20% between runs; prompt numbers are steady ±3%); 250K is one run per arm (the needle is the anchor); correctness evidence is two needles plus one arithmetic probe identical in all 20 arms — no quality suite; single model, single card, Linux only.

Cross-refs: #2227 (mtp-hnorm), #2498 (pcie-frac), #2650 (kv-grow), #2642 (same rig's suite report — it never got the 32K prompts), #2684 (the NUMA binding used), #2695 (the same day's dense-F32 A/B).

title: tools: add opt-in FP4-Local CSF checkpoint conversion
body:
The FP4-Local checkpoint stores expert scales as CSF streams and uses mixed MXFP8/NVFP4 weights, which the existing offline converter cannot read. This adds a separate explicit converter that writes a main text GGUF and a streamed BF16 PLE GGUF for Strata’s existing readers.

Refs #2726. The full pinned checkpoint has now been converted and served through Strata 0.1.44.1 on an RTX 5090 32 GB / Core Ultra 9 285K / 64 GiB RAM / Ubuntu host.

- Routed-expert codes and decoded scale bytes are retained; the pinned converter performs the NVFP4 repack.
- Dense MXFP8/non-expert NVFP4 weights are decoded before the existing BF16/F16/Q8_0 policy, adding rounding.
- The NVFP4 PLE table is streamed to BF16 in bounded row chunks (102,400,491,520 payload bytes for FP4-Local).
- Metadata-only `--dry-run` reports the conversion plan. Outputs/manifests are new files; source checkpoint files remain read-only.
- Experts are grouped by layer before repacking so the real checkpoint’s interleaved shards do not accumulate the entire arena in RAM. Explicit source config values are preserved across AutoConfig normalization, including `full_attention` names needed by the pinned metadata writer. Both full-run failures have regression tests with failing negative controls against the previous implementation.
- Vision and MTP are excluded. The upstream installer, runtime/backend and ordinary `nvfp4_convert.py` remain unchanged. Compatibility adapters are scoped to the new command and restored on exit/failure.

Validation:

- CPU suites: 5 codec tests + 14 converter tests passed on the target host; Ruff and `git diff --check` passed.
- The CLI also converted a bounded real-tensor fixture end to end, retaining nine independently computed expert projection hashes and writing a readable BF16 PLE file.
- Full output: 1,511 tensors / 73,939,912,352 bytes in the main GGUF; 144 NVFP4 expert tensors with 512 experts each. Nine projection hashes/global scales matched; 18 BF16 PLE rows across first/middle/final shards matched source reconstruction. Expert pack: 48 layers / 63.28 GiB.
- The initial full export’s fixed-size compression-ratio metadata was repaired without changing tensor payloads. All 38 architecture fields then matched a fresh metadata export from the corrected converter, and tensor checks were repeated.
- Live API checks passed text, structured tool calling and tool-result continuation, separated reasoning, streaming and retrieval from an 18,040-token prompt. A client gateway round trip passed. The corrected service remained stable with zero restarts during these checks.
- Smoke-check rates: 3,224 prompt tokens/s on the retrieval prompt, 49 tokens/s for a 77-token reasoning reply, 54 tokens/s for a 109-token streamed paragraph. Configuration: 128K maximum context, INT8 KV with 32K resident cells, 38 GiB expert RAM budget, no MTP or vision sidecar. These short checks are not a quality/throughput comparison; the full 128K limit was not exercised.
- Earlier three-expert CUDA parity passed the existing test (1.096%, 1.156%, 1.159% relative output error; threshold 3%). No GPU/kernel changes.

The docs record the pinned checkpoint/reference revisions, precision changes, memory needs, conversion caveats and measurements. Full answer-quality comparison, full-context retrieval, vision and MTP remain untested.

Format reference: [vLLM #60646](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60646). AI-assisted implementation and testing.

title: bench: RX 7900 XT (Windows HIP) community results + fix BENCH.bat on GBK Windows

Two commits:

1. `tools/strata_bench.py`: `project_version()` called `CMakeLists.txt.read_text()` without an encoding. On a Chinese Windows install (GBK default) decoding raises `UnicodeDecodeError` — and because that is a ValueError it slips past the `except OSError` and kills the whole benchmark before the first test. Pinning `encoding="utf-8"` fixes it; reproduced on the current main, and the full suite runs afterwards.

2. `bench/results/2026-10-16-community-rx-7900-xt-swift-1-5-iq3-xxs`: community benchmark row for a Windows HIP setup on an RX 7900 XT (24 GB), Swift-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, engine 0.1.44.1, 320K context (yarn 1.25), int8 KV, spec 4 + MTP, vision through a Vulkan encoder pinned to the AMD card. Medians: chat decode 50.7 tok/s (TTFT 0.65 s), 4K prompt 416 tok/s, 16K prompt 560 tok/s, agent session cache hit 68.4%, agent decode 53.6 tok/s.

One note on the sanitizer: `results.json` still contained a second data folder (`D:\...` style paths outside the Strata folder and the user home) that the scrubber missed; I cleaned it by hand in this branch. Worth widening the scrubber if you ever get reports from multi-drive installs.

title: prefill: STRATA_PF_PEER_CPU=1 (opt-in) runs the CPU share beside a peer GPU (--peer-device)
body:
The share took nothing there (cpu_maybe required !m.pp).  With the switch it takes only experts that neither card computes (not peer-held, not peer-streamed), and its rows go before the peer's block, so the peer's block stays the tail the peer combine reads from back_at (layout: primary GPU, CPU, peer).  The staged chunks then go up to cpu_share_max()'s 3072 tokens instead of the default share's 1024 (an explicit STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE_MAX still wins).  Without the switch nothing changes.

RTX 5060 Ti (PCIe 3.0 x8) + RTX 3060 (x16), Xeon E5-2683 v4, IQ3_XXS, a 161-173K-token agent conversation, tool results read one after another (STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING): 117-132 tokens 1.80-1.92 -> 1.16 s, 325-335 2.12-2.89 -> 1.36-1.63 s, 524 3.33 -> 1.99 s, 1067 3.74 -> 2.64 s, 1170 3.81 -> 3.26 s, 2012 4.33 -> 4.22 s, 3.2-3.5K unchanged; the chain of 12 reads 36.0 -> 29.7 s (the base twice: 36.1, 36.0).  A question about the last tool output answered the same in all three runs.  In daily use on that rig since 2026-10-15.

Not tested: HIP, SYCL, a layer split's helper (the change is in the CUDA prompt path's host code; the share stays off on HIP unless set), other peer pairs.

**How it was checked.** Built on its own on top of `main` (296b59d2): CUDA 13.3, sm_86 + sm_120, Linux (Ubuntu), the `strata` target. HIP, SYCL and Metal were not built: I have only the NVIDIA rig.

One change per PR; nothing else from my fork is in it.

title: --peer-device: the adaptive tier's copies land while the next window runs (opt-in STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1); opt-in STRATA_PEER_LAUNCH_IN_POOL=1 launches the peer inside the pool's first phase
body:
In peer mode every decode window began with a blocking wait for the previous adapt round's copies (3.0-7.7 ms of a 27-43 ms window, in 94-99% of the windows; --adapt-every 1, 17-38 swaps a window): the overlap gate left --peer-device out.  With STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1 the peer tier now joins it: PeerExperts::adapt issues its copies in layer order and signals each layer's landing with the primary's kind of signal (a stream-ordered D2H copy of the layer number into a pinned int, or host functions where the primary uses them), its table takes the swaps at the window's start (flip_pending), and a layer waits for a tier's copies only when that tier swapped in it.  Without a peer the per-layer wait is the one it was; without the variable nothing changes.

Separately, STRATA_PEER_LAUNCH_IN_POOL=1 (opt-in): the peer's launch (~30 us of host work a layer) ran before the CPU pool started, with every worker waiting; with the switch it runs on the host thread right after the pool's first phase is published (ExpertPool::run_split_multi_native with `aside`).  The rows are the same either way; without the switch the order is the old one.  STRATA_DECODE_TIMING gains a line with the peer's launch and wait and the CPU pool's own time per expert.

```
RTX 5060 Ti (PCIe 3.0 x8) + RTX 3060 (x16), Xeon E5-2683 v4, IQ3_XXS, 7 greedy requests of 300-600 tokens, means of
two alternating rounds:
  0.1.43, before                  72.2 tok/s   copy wait 3.0-7.7 ms per window
  + overlap for the peer          74.6         0.2 ms
  + STRATA_PEER_LAUNCH_IN_POOL     75.9         0.2 ms   (this step alone is inside the run-to-run spread)
  0.1.43.1 (stream-ordered signal): 75.6 -> 77.1 (inside the spread), code 91.7 -> 96.3; the host-function signal
  on the same build 76.9 / 93.5.
Not kept, measured flat or slower on the same rig: the peer streaming missed experts over its own link (-2.4%),
pacing the copies through the window (-3%), a low-priority refill stream (0), --adapt-min-gain 4 / 8 / 15 (-1 / -5 /
-7%).
```

Not tested: HIP, SYCL, Metal, Windows, a layer split; on 0.1.44.1 (this base) it was rebased and has run in daily use on the rig above since 2026-10-14, but on/off was not measured again.  Tokens are not compared bit for bit: two runs of the unchanged engine already differ (the adaptive tier makes the output depend on timing).

**How it was checked.** Built on its own on top of `main` (296b59d2): CUDA 13.3, sm_86 + sm_120, Linux (Ubuntu), the `strata` target. Without `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1` peer mode runs as before, and without `STRATA_PEER_LAUNCH_IN_POOL=1` the peer launches first and the rows are zeroed exactly as before. HIP, SYCL and Metal were not built: I have only the NVIDIA rig.

One change per PR; nothing else from my fork is in it.

title: --prompt-cache-spread (opt-in): the first checkpoint in every --prompt-cache-every tokens of the conversation stays, so a request that departs far back reads at most that much again
body:
An agent session grows by short turns and every request saves a checkpoint at its new turn, so least recent use keeps the root and the last few turns - all at the conversation's end.  A request that departs further back (the client's summarization call over the older part, an old tool result rewritten) then falls to the root and reads everything after it again.  With the option, eviction_victim_spread (conv_cache.hpp) keeps the first checkpoint in every --prompt-cache-every tokens as a milestone; the rest rotate by least recent use, the two most recently used always stay, and when only milestones are left the one whose neighbours are closest goes.  Without the option, with fewer than 4 checkpoints or --prompt-cache-every 0 the policy is the plain one.  conv_cache_test covers the new policy.

RTX 5060 Ti (PCIe 3.0 x8) + RTX 3060, --peer-device, IQ3_XXS, --prompt-cache 14: a conversation of 80 turns to 121K tokens, then a request with its first 55 turns and a new instruction (86,182 tokens): without the option 5,023 reused + 81,159 read in 60.3 s, with it 83,387 reused + 2,795 read in 4.1 s.  A day of real agent use (31 automatic compactions): the summarization call read a median 8,062 tokens in 7.2 s instead of ~72K in ~55 s.  The answers can differ in wording (a restored checkpoint and a batched re-read round differently).  Not measured: the RAM of 14 checkpoints at its peak; HIP, SYCL and Metal (the change is host code shared by all of them).

**How it was checked.** Built on its own on top of `main` (296b59d2): CUDA 13.3, sm_86 + sm_120, Linux (Ubuntu), the `strata` target. `conv_cache_test` (header-only) compiled with g++ and passes, including the two new spread cases. The option has run in daily agent use on the rig above since 2026-10-13. HIP, SYCL and Metal were not built: I have only the NVIDIA rig.

One change per PR; nothing else from my fork is in it.

title: Community benchmark: 4x RTX 3090 24 GiB (250 W each) - Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS at 262,144-token context
body:
## Summary

Community benchmark report for **4x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 24 GiB** running **Unsloth Dynamic UD-IQ4_XS** (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) at the **262,144-token native context**, measured with `tools/strata_bench.py --clients 1 --long` (3 runs per test, thinking off, medians with ranges; suite total 131 s).

| Test | Prompt tok/s (median, range) | Decode tok/s (median, range) | TTFT s (median, range) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| short chat (n=9) | not measured | 113.3 (88.8-153.1) | 0.24 (0.22-0.26) |
| 4K fresh prompt (4,019 tok) | 1313.3 (1249.7-1313.8) | not measured | 3.08 (3.08-3.23) |
| 16K fresh prompt (16,058 tok) | 2393.8 (2359.3-2398.1) | not measured | 6.73 (6.72-6.83) |
| 32K fresh prompt (32,049 tok) | 3240.1 (3234.1-3248.9) | not measured | 9.92 (9.89-9.94) |
| agent session follow-ups | ~1000 mid-session | 127.1 (81.5-139.5) | 2.76 (2.05-3.19) |
| concurrency, 1 client | 75.5 total (69.9-79.4) | - | p95 0.335 |

## Hardware / software

- 4x RTX 3090 24 GiB, **each power-limited to 250 W** on the host (factory 350 W / 420 W for GPU1); GPU0 PCIe x16, GPU1-3 x4, no NVLink; layer split auto (0-11 / 12-26 / 27-35 / 36-47)
- i7-13700K, 44 GiB RAM, Debian 12 LXC on Proxmox VE, driver 595.84, CUDA 13.2, Strata 0.1.44.1 (commit 296b59d)

## Model / configuration

- Unsloth Dynamic UD-IQ4_XS (~94 GB, 3-shard GGUF), BF16 mmproj vision encoder, native-experts pack, MTP draft enabled (`--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`)
- 262,144-token context, `--kv int8`, `--batch 2` (2 parallel slots), `--expert-cache auto`, `--resident-budget-gib 20` pinned RAM tier: **89% of experts resident at load**, remaining ~35.4 GiB read from a CIFS network share through the file cache (decode expert hit rate 99.7-99.8% during the suite, <=0.1% cross-GPU PCIe reads)

## Limitations

- Speed suite only; no needle/recall check was run
- The `--clients 1` arm is effectively solo: a single request occupies one slot alone and keeps MTP; with shared batch windows MTP is disabled
- 250 W per-GPU power cap lowers sustained boost clocks (~1.73-1.80 GHz observed); expect somewhat better prompt throughput on machines at stock power
- Chat decode range is wide (88.8-153.1) due to MTP draft-acceptance variance on short chats; the agent-session median (127.1) is the more stable solo-decode figure

Per-run data: `results.json`. This PR adds only `bench/results/2026-10-15-community-rtx-3090-qwen3-8-flash-next/` (README.md + results.json).

title: log unauthorized API-key attempts with the client IP (issue #1847)
body:
## What this does

Adds a log line on API-key authentication failure that includes the client source IP, so fail2ban (or any log-based rate limiter) can match it and ban brute-force attempts. Closes #1847.

Before this change, `_authorized()` in `serve/server.py` replied with a silent 401 JSON body — nothing landed in the journal, so there was nothing for a filter to match on.

```python
print(f"unauthorized: Invalid API Key from {self.client_address[0]}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
```

The wording deliberately mirrors llama.cpp's `unauthorized: Invalid API Key from <ip>` verbatim (as requested in #1847), so an existing fail2ban filter written for llama.cpp works against Strata's logs unchanged.

Notes:
- Goes to `stderr`, consistent with other warnings in this file (e.g. the AMD line at L2845); `flush=True` keeps journald real-time so fail2ban doesn't miss events.
- No `[strata]` prefix on purpose, to keep the line byte-compatible with the stock llama.cpp filter regex.
- `sys` is already imported at module level; no new dependencies.

## Verification

- `python3 -m py_compile serve/server.py` passes.
- Smoke-tested the patched failure branch in isolation: emits exactly `unauthorized: Invalid API Key from 203.0.113.7` on stderr.
- Not end-to-end tested against a running server (needs GPU/model engine); the change is one print statement on the existing 401 path.

title: bench: community report, RX 7900 XT 20 GB (gfx1100) on Linux, UD-Q5_K_XL, v0.1.44.1
body:
## Title
bench: community report, RX 7900 XT 20 GB (gfx1100) on Linux, UD-Q5_K_XL, v0.1.44.1

Issue: no issue to resolve. Related: #2065 and #2477 (VRAM headroom), #2505 / #2632 (the UD-Q5_K_XL shard check this install hit).

## Summary
One RX 7900 XT 20 GB (gfx1100) in a Linux container on an EPYC 7K62 (48 CPUs, 128 GiB), v0.1.44.1 source build on a system ROCm 7.2.3 (hipBLASLt 1.2.2, setup picked the `100202` table), Unsloth UD-Q5_K_XL at 262,144 tokens with every expert in RAM. Hardware the maintainers do not list: a 7900 XT (not XTX) on Linux.

Same build, same machine, same day, `tools/strata_bench.py --runs 3 --long`, setup's configuration vs the same plus `--vram-reserve-mib 1024 --prefill auto:32768` (medians):

| Test | setup default | tuned |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| short chat decode tok/s | 17.2 | 22.7 |
| prompt tok/s, 4K / 16K / 32K fresh | 335 / 565 / 1,019 | 577 / 888 / 1,116 |
| agent follow-up first token s | 7.17 | 5.36 |
| agent follow-up decode tok/s | 15.1 | 26.1 |

`needle_bench.py` on the tuned configuration: 6 of 6 at 32K and 125K tokens (depths 10/50/90 %).

With setup's configuration only 562 MiB of VRAM was free after start and `serve` printed the `below 512 MiB` warning; the reserve trades 85 GPU expert slots for 888 MiB free. In the screening runs `STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=1` was slower or no faster in every pairing (unlike the IQ3_XXS / ROCm 7.1 numbers in `docs/AMD_HIP_PERFORMANCE.md`), as were `--pool-workers 47` and `--adapt-every 0`. One screening arm lost its run to `verify: timed out at layer 17` (#267 wording) after a stall; no failure in an 8-round soak of the kept configuration or in either suite run.

## What changed
- `bench/results/2026-10-15-community-rx-7900-xt-ud-q5-k-xl/`: `README.md` (hardware, ROCm, configuration, method, results, failures, what was not tested); `setup-default/` and `tuned/` (the bench tool's own `README.md` + `results.json` for each run); `needles.json`; `micro/` (the deterministic screening script and every arm's settings and samples, 15 KB).
- `bench/results/COMMUNITY.md`: one row.
- `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`: one entry.

No code changes.

## Extra Notes
- Install: one local change to `setup.py` only, not to the engine: `check_shards` skips shards with no tensors, because setup refused the current UD-Q5_K_XL `00001-of-00006` (10,946,618 bytes, identical to setup's own sha256 pin) as 6 bytes short. Same fix as #2505 / #2632; not part of this PR.
- The tool READMEs say "Settings: the install's own configuration, unchanged" because the tool was pointed at a running server; the top-level README states which configuration each folder ran.
- Not tested: thinking on, concurrency / `--batch`, vision, prompts above ~125K tokens, other quants, `--calibrate`, power and clocks. The host's other guests were not stopped and the container's CPUs are not pinned to whole cores.
- Measured and written up with an AI coding agent (Claude Code); numbers are from the files in the folder.
