title: Feature/windows amd vision telemetry
body: ## Title Windows AMD: ADL2 telemetry, one Monitor tile per GPU, images on Windows, and a setup that keeps a two-card split Issue: Refs #2614, #1380, #112, #2442 ## Summary A Windows AMD card had no telemetry: the Monitor's GPU tiles were empty and a PC with two cards had no way to see them apart. This reads every AMD card through ADL2 PMLog (`atiadlxx.dll` over ctypes — the same interface HWInfo and LibreHardwareMonitor use, no new dependency), gives the Monitor one tile per card, and carries the same numbers into `/metrics`. Alongside it, three things that stopped a Windows AMD install working: SETUP renumbered or dropped cards when `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` was already in the environment, re-running SETUP collapsed a two-card split back to one card (the engine then died at start, reported as "the embedding buffer failed"), and Windows had no image encoder at all. One commit, `d0dcf489` plus the review fixes listed under Telemetry and Tests: 35 files, +1501/−145 against `main` (v0.1.44.1). Everything is opt-in — the CUDA path is untouched, `--yes` never asks the new questions, AMD images stay off by default, and the default install path writes the same config as v0.1.44.1. No engine (C++/CUDA/HIP kernel) changes. ## What changed ### Telemetry (`serve/telemetry.py`, +366) - `_Adl` — ctypes bindings for ADL2 PMLog: adapter enumeration, `PmLogStart` with the sensor set (edge/mem temp, board power, gfx/mem activity, bus lanes, power limit), and the malloc callback through `ucrtbase.dll` (the heap `atiadlxx.dll` frees on). - `_AmdWin` — util = max(gfx, mem activity), temp = edge else mem, power = `BOARD_POWER` (already watts, no scaling), VRAM used = `DedicatedVRAMUsage`, total = `MemoryInfoX4`. Enumerates present discrete cards, deduped by the UDID's `DEV_xxxx` code (each card repeats once per display), integrated GPU skipped. - Every discrete card is sampled (`amd_card_count()`), not just the display-driving one — `Adapter_Get` hid a second idle card. HIP indices and ADL indices are different namespaces and are never mixed. - PCIe per card — PMLog `BUS_SPEED` is the GPU's internal bus and power-saves to Gen4 at idle, so the slot's generation comes from Device Manager (`DEVPKEY_PciDevice_MaxLinkSpeed`, one cached PowerShell query keyed by DEV code) and the negotiated width from PMLog `BUS_LANES`. Matches HWInfo on this PC: 9070 XT Gen5 x8, R9700 Gen5 x4. - A reader gives back what the driver lent it: `close()` releases the PMLog device handle and the ADL context, a finaliser covers readers that go away with the server, and the one-off call sites (`free_vram_mib()`, `server.gpu_vram_mib()`) release theirs. Numbers under Measured. - `sample()` always emits `gpus[]` with name, `pcie_gen_max` and `pcie_width` per card, even for one card. - Small NVML fix: `power_limit` returns `float(lim)` instead of a raw value that could be 0. ### SETUP behaviour (`setup.py`, +200/−33) - **AMD asks "Do you want images?" everywhere, Windows included** (default off; `--yes` never asks; the Unsloth Linux default-on is unchanged). `hip_vision()` is now platform-neutral: `yes`/`gpu` → gpu, `cpu` → cpu, else none. - **`previous_amd_split()`** — a re-run with no `--gpu`/`--gpus` keeps the installed config's split (accepts `"gpu"` as a list or a `"0,2"` string, newest config wins, keeps the split only while every card is still present and usable). - **`hip_devices()` clears `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` for the probe.** A user-set value hid cards and renumbered the rest, so a saved split "0,2" named a card that was no longer at 2. - **Windows `--gpus` works** — the old "multi-GPU is Linux only" refusal is gone. `engine_step()` renumbers the split's cards to HIP numbers after the probe (an integrated Radeon takes HIP 0) and prints what it settled on. - **`hip_vision_windows()`** — for the ready-made zip: run the zip's encoder when `BUILD.json` says `vision`/`vision_src`/`vision_archs` match; `gpu` asked without an encoder built for this arch warns and falls back to cpu; a stale or missing encoder is recompiled as CPU with MSVC; no compiler offers the winget Build Tools (~2 GB), and declining leaves images off. - **`install_msvc_build_tools()`** — winget `Microsoft.VisualStudio.2022.BuildTools` with the VCTools workload, asked first. `cmake_build()` pip-installs cmake and ninja when they are missing (old installs predate `requirements.txt`). - **VRAM reserve rule** — Windows AMD with the CPU encoder writes no `--vram-reserve-mib` at all, so the engine keeps its 2560 MiB WDDM floor (#1376, #1709); a written 700 would have defeated it. With a GPU encoder the reserve is `max(reserve, 3260)` = the 2560 floor + the encoder's 700. The 12 GB tip only shows where it applies. ### Multi-GPU enumeration and JSON config - The config is re-read and `gpu` normalised whether it is a list or a `"0,2"` string, so an old config survives. - `tools/hip/package_windows.py` records `vision: "cpu"`, `vision_src` (source hash) and `vision_archs` in `BUILD.json`, so SETUP can tell a matching encoder from a stale one. - `.gitignore` adds `/strata-*.bak` (SETUP's config backups) and `build-vision-cpu.bat`. ### Vision build and packaging - `tools/hip/build_windows.bat` builds a portable CPU `strata-vision.exe` (AVX2, static CRT, llama.cpp pinned by `setup.get_llama_cpp()`) into the zip; `package_windows.py --vision` ships it. - `tools/vision/CMakeLists.txt` gains `STRATA_VISION_HIP` (GGML_HIP) for the Linux HIP encoder path in `setup.build_vision_hip()` — **not yet run on hardware**, flagged in TEST_REQUESTS. - `tools/vision/strata_vision.cpp` also sets `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1` in CPU mode — the AMD runtime ignores `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`. - `tools/strata_mcp.py` drops the "hip on Windows" and vision refusals; the MCP `strata_install` accepts the same vision answers as SETUP (gpu is downgraded to cpu by setup itself when the arch has no encoder). ### Monitor UI (`serve/web/`) - **Image encoder card**: encoder cache bar, encode-time sparkline, facts (device + threads, last picture with tokens/grid/cache-hit, since-start totals, mmproj, picture cap), and a "Reading N pictures" pill and status line while an encode runs. - **Per-GPU tiles** (`renderGpuCards`) when the PC has ≥2 cards; summary Power and PCIe tiles get a `GPU:0 …` / `GPU:1 …` line each; the PCIe tile shows each card's own link ("Gen5 x8", "Gen5 x4"). - `app.css`/`app.js` are cache-busted (`?v=3`) so an open tab can't keep a stale script. ### Metrics (`serve/server.py`, `serve/prometheus.py`) - `Vision` records starts/stops, per-encode times, cache hits, failures and image tokens; `/metrics` gains a `vision` block, `encoding_images`, and per-request history rows (images / image tokens / encode ms). - Prometheus gains 7 series: `strata:vision_images_total`, `image_tokens_total`, `encode_seconds_total`, `encode_failures_total`, `cache_images`, `encoder_up`, `encode_ms_last` (absent on a cache hit). Nothing is emitted when the model has no vision. - `engine_args()` adds `--vram-reserve-mib 3260` for hip on Windows with a GPU encoder (2560 WDDM floor + 700 for the encoder). `gpu_vram_mib()` releases the reader it builds per card. ### Docs - `AMD_HIP.md`: the ADL2 telemetry paragraph with the B650E measurements, the two-cards-one-model Windows section, and the Images-on-Windows section (zip encoder, 2.7–2.9 s per 512×512 picture on a 7800X3D, Build Tools ~2 GB, the 3260 reserve). - `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`: new entry "SETUP.bat forgets a two-card split" with the `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` root cause, how to check it, and the measured before/after probe results. - `DETAILS.md`: Monitor sources (ADL2/NVML/sysfs, per-slot PCIe), the `strata:vision_*` series, the AMD image-encoder table row, and the Image encoder card paragraph. - `MULTI_GPU.md`: Windows AMD `--gpus` line. `AI_SETUP.md`: the AMD images question. `TEST_REQUESTS.md`: two rows — Windows AMD `--vision cpu` reports wanted, `--vision gpu` never run on hardware. - README ×7: "AMD cards read pictures through the processor, on Linux and on Windows alike." ### Tests - New `serve/test_telemetry_adl.py` (+118): the ADL reader never raises when ADL is missing, readings are sane (temp 0–120 °C, watts), every card index below `card_count` reads, per-card PCIe present, and `AdlReaderCleanup` — `close()` is safe and idempotent, and 40 one-off `free_vram_mib()` reads do not grow the process handle count (Windows only, skipped where there is no `atiadlxx.dll`). - `tools/test_setup_amd.py`: probe ignores a set `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES`; the vision question is platform-neutral. - `tools/test_setup_choices.py`: 5 new `hip_vision_windows` cases — zip encoder used, gpu from zip, gpu falls back to cpu when the arch is missing, stale `vision_src` recompiles, no compiler asks then declines. - `tools/test_setup_unsloth.py`: `HipImages` (Windows asks, yes → cpu encoder with no `--vram-reserve-mib` in the config args, default off, `--yes` never asks, Linux Unsloth default stays on) and `HipSplit` (Windows `--gpus 0,2` renumbers to [1,2] when the iGPU takes 0, setup-again keeps a list or a "0,2" string, a fresh PC stays one card, Linux keeps its split). - `serve/test_server.py`: the vision instrumentation, and the three `AmdTelemetry` tests pinned to the Linux sysfs reader — they fake an amdgpu tree, so building a real ADL reader here made them depend on the machine (#1380). `WebApp.test_page_and_files` now matches `web/app.js` with its `?v=3` cache-bust. - `serve/test_monitor.py`, `test_prometheus.py`, `test_vision_elastic.py`: the Monitor card's DOM and the Prometheus series. `tools/test_strata_mcp.py`: hip vision cpu/yes/gpu/no accepted on both platforms. ## Extra Notes ### Test machine - Windows 11, Ryzen 7 7800X3D, B650E motherboard, Adrenalin 26.9.2 - AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 32 GB — HIP 0, gfx1201, Gen5 x4 (Device Manager and HWInfo agree: "PCIe v5.0 x16 @ x4") - AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB — HIP 2, gfx1201, Gen5 x8 - 7800X3D integrated graphics (2 CU RDNA2, gfx1036; rocminfo's marketing name is "AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D 8-Core Processor") — HIP 1, skipped by the split and by the ADL2 enumeration - Model split across the two cards: R9700 layers 0–30, 9070 XT layers 31–47 + head, 131K context - CPU image encoder running on the 7800X3D; a hand-built HIP encoder also ran on the R9700 (below) ### Measured on that machine - **Handle growth (the finding reported on #1434).** 40 one-off `free_vram_mib(0, amd=True)` calls hold the process handle count at 197 → 197 now that the reader is released. Keeping the readers gave 197 → 278, about +2 per call — the same signature crkva measured on a 7900 XTX in #1434 (267 → 347). The server's sampler keeps one reader per card, so the growth showed up on the one-off calls: `free_vram_mib()` in the startup retry loop and `gpu_vram_mib()` once per card. - **PCIe per card:** 9070 XT Gen5 x8, R9700 Gen5 x4 — Device Manager and HWInfo agree, and the B650E board really does bifurcate, so one aggregate link number would be wrong. - **Images:** 2.7–2.9 s per 512×512 picture (256 tokens) with the CPU encoder; the screenshot run measured 3,647 ms for a 23×12 (276-token) picture, cache hit on repeat. - **Prometheus scrape after 4 image requests:** `strata:vision_images_total 4`, `vision_image_tokens_total 1073`, `vision_encode_seconds_total 12.767`, `vision_encode_failures_total 0`, `vision_cache_images 4`, `vision_encoder_up 1`. `/metrics` also shows both `gpus[]` rows with correct ADL2 values. - **SETUP probe with `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES="0,2"` set:** the old probe returned 2 cards numbered 0,1; the fixed probe returns all 3 (R9700 = HIP 0, 7800X3D iGPU = HIP 1, 9070 XT = HIP 2). ### Test suite - `python -m unittest discover -s serve -p "test_*.py"`: 805 tests in 303 s, OK (15 skipped) on this machine. - The modules this branch touches, run on their own: `test_telemetry_adl` 8, `test_server` 17 (WebApp 14 + `AmdTelemetry` 3), `test_monitor` + `test_prometheus` + `test_vision_elastic` 29 — all passing. - Setup's own tests, no GPU or downloads: `test_setup_amd.py` 37, `test_setup_choices.py` 52, `test_setup_unsloth.py` 68, `test_setup_update.py` 8, `test_setup_sycl.py` 18 — all OK. - The three `AmdTelemetry` tests that already failed on `main` on this two-card PC now pass; nothing is left failing on this machine. - The Windows HIP engine and the CPU `strata-vision.exe` were built and then run end to end on this hardware (throwaway build/run scripts, not added to the repo). ### The GPU image encoder on Windows (built by hand, not shipped) The zip ships the CPU encoder and `package_windows.py` stamps `BUILD.json` `vision: "cpu"`, `vision_archs: []` — no published zip can select the GPU encoder yet. A HIP `strata-vision.exe` can still be built on Windows and run beside the ready-made engine; verified on this PC (gfx1201): - **Build:** vcvars64 + the `.rocm-win` venv's ROCm (`rocm-sdk.exe path --root`), then `tools/vision` with `-DSTRATA_VISION_HIP=ON -DSTRATA_VISION_CUDA=OFF`, ROCm's clang/clang++ as the C/C++ compilers, `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=` and `GPU_TARGETS=gfx1201` (`AMDGPU_TARGETS` is deprecated). The ROCm flags must ride in `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS` (`--rocm-path=… --rocm-device-lib-path=…`): on Windows ggml-hip forces `CXX_IS_HIPCC` and cmake ignores `CMAKE_HIP_FLAGS`, so without them the compile fails with "cannot find ROCm device library". - **Selection:** `engine\BUILD.json` must say `vision: "gpu"` and `vision_archs` must name the card, or `hip_vision_windows()` warns and falls back to cpu. The config's vision section then carries `gpu: true`, `max_tokens: 1024` and `--vram-reserve-mib 3260` — SETUP writes all three on a fresh install; re-running over an installed model keeps the old config as-is (the reuse path starts it directly), so changing an installed model to the GPU encoder means editing the config or re-running with `--setup`. - **Run:** the server puts `engine\rocm\bin` on the encoder's PATH (the config's `lib_dirs`), where hipBLAS and rocBLAS live; `hip_runtime_beside_exe` copies only the HIP runtime beside the exes by design. Run from a bare terminal the exe dies in the loader with 0xC0000135 (DLL not found) and prints nothing — prepend `engine\rocm\bin` to PATH for a standalone test. - **Measured on the R9700:** model files loaded in 3.0 s, warm-up at 4,096 image tokens in 5.3 s, `READY 2560`; the Monitor's image card reads "running on the GPU", cap 1,024. Per-picture encode times: not measured yet. Shipping it would mean building the HIP encoder in `build_windows.bat` and stamping `vision_archs` in `package_windows.py` — a separate change, not in this PR. ### Screenshots Live from the machine above, model loaded, after real image requests. The PNGs are not committed. ### Where this overlaps Several open threads cover part of this, and they disagree in places. Flagging it rather than adding a sixth silently: - **AMD Windows telemetry:** #2614 (open issue, the place to discuss it), #1434 (gt50 — `ADL_POWER = (73, 23, 30)` and a `close()` after crkva's 7900 XTX validation), #1871 (kaiw1102), #2273 (YashwantBharaj, rebased on #1434), #1224 (Annoosha-1, sensor 23 first and a fresh `_Adl2()` per call — the pattern #1434 was called out for). This branch prefers sensor 73 (`PMLOG_BOARD_POWER`) for the reason crkva gave and releases handles the way #1434 does; it reads the slot's generation from Device Manager rather than PMLog `BUS_SPEED`, which power-saves to Gen4 at idle on this board. Happy to rebase onto whichever lands first, or to port the SETUP/vision/Monitor parts onto that reader and drop this one. - **Card numbering:** #1152 (crkva) enumerates through HIP and #112 asks for multi-GPU on Windows. This branch enumerates through ADL2 and keeps HIP and ADL indices as separate namespaces; `--gpus` on Windows is the part #112 asks for. - **Windows AMD build/packaging:** #2442 is a community guide to building this by hand, including a hand-built `strata-vision.exe`; the zip encoder here is the same thing, shipped by the installer. - **Vision metrics:** #2317 and #2272 touch `/metrics` and the Monitor. The `strata:vision_*` series are new names and emit nothing when the model has no vision. ### Not here - No CUDA/NVIDIA behaviour change beyond the `power_limit` guard. - The Linux HIP GPU encoder compiles but has never been run on hardware — TEST_REQUESTS asks for reports; SETUP still offers it knowingly. (A hand-built Windows HIP encoder ran on gfx1201 — see above — but the zip still ships the CPU one and no published zip can select a GPU encoder yet.) - No engine (C++/CUDA/HIP kernel) changes: this is setup, serve, tools and docs.

title: tests: track the server sampler thread on shutdown
body:
# Issue: Sampler shutdown test inspects unrelated process threads

The test counts process-wide threads, so unrelated threads can make the server
shutdown assertion fail.

# PR: Check the server-owned sampler thread on shutdown

Assert the lifecycle of the sampler thread owned by the server under test.
No production code changes.

Validation: `serve.test_responses`, including the shutdown regression.

PR #1840 only waits for threads in its new `test_literal_think_guard.py`;
it does not change this existing assertion. A deterministic disappearing-thread
control fails on 296b59d2 and passes with this change.
